entry.title: Satisfiability Solving with LLMs: A Matched-Pair Evaluation of Reasoning Capability

author.name: Leizhen Zhang, Shuhan Chen, Sheng Chen

entry.summary: This paper systematically evaluates LLMs on 2-SAT and 3-SAT plus reductions to Vertex Cover and 3D packing, finding standard metrics misleading because models over-predict satisfiability and fail to reproduce the classical easy-hard-easy phase transition. It probes representation-invariant reasoning on satisfiability.

entry.title: Multi-Adapter Representation Interventions via Energy Calibration

author.name: Manjiang Yu, Hongji Li, Junwei Chen, Xue Li, Priyanka Singh, Yang Cao, Lijie Hu

entry.summary: MARI proposes adaptive, per-input representation interventions for LLM alignment using a competitive multi-adapter mechanism with energy calibration, avoiding the capability degradation caused by uniform interventions. It targets behavior steering without weight modification.

entry.title: Bridging the Stability-Expressivity Gap: Synthetic Data Scaling and Preference Alignment for Low-Resource Spoken Language Models

author.name: Yizhong Geng, Yanliang Li, Jinghan Yang, Tianhan Jiang, Boxun An, Ya Li, Xiaoyu Shen

entry.summary: This work identifies a Stability-Expressivity Gap in spoken language models for low-resource languages, where synthetic data improves phonetic accuracy but suppresses prosodic variability, causing expressivity collapse. It proposes preference alignment to bridge the gap.

entry.title: Human-AI Collaboration for Estimating Scientific Replicability

author.name: Tatiana Chakravorti, Robert Fraleigh, Timothy Fritton, Christopher Griffin, Vaibhav Singh, Sai Koneru, C. Lee Giles, David Pennock, Anthony Kwasnica, Sarah Rajtmajer

entry.summary: This paper introduces a hybrid prediction market combining algorithmic agents and human forecasters to estimate scientific replicability, aiming to overcome limitations of pure human judgment or ML-only approaches. It addresses the long-standing replication crisis challenge.

entry.title: Benchmarking Fairness in Spiking Neural Networks: Data Bias, Spurious Features, and Hardware Effects

author.name: Hudi He, Fukun Wang, Zhe Wang, Xinyi Wang, Shuhan Ye, Jiarui Liu, Qing Qing, Ziqi Xu, Xikun Zhang, Renqiang Luo

entry.summary: This work introduces the first systematic fairness benchmark for Spiking Neural Networks, covering demographic coverage gaps, spurious feature leakage, and deployment-environment mismatches across four datasets and neuromorphic hardware simulators like Loihi 2 and SpiNNaker. It isolates how hardware affects fairness.

entry.title: Tackling Multimodal Learning Challenges with Mixture-of-Expert: A Survey

author.name: Liangwei Nathan Zheng, Wei Emma Zhang, Olaf Maennel, Lin Yue, Weitong Chen

entry.summary: This survey systematically reviews how Mixture-of-Experts addresses multimodal learning challenges, organizing methods around MoE as an efficient engine, modality balancer, and interaction modeler. It fills a gap where prior surveys treat MoE and multimodal learning separately.

entry.title: AdaMerge: Salience-Aware Adaptive Token Merging for Training-Free Acceleration of Vision Transformers

author.name: Semi Lee, Hyejin Go, Hyesong Choi

entry.summary: AdaMerge is a training-free token merging framework for Vision Transformers that uses salience-weighted similarity to address the false token-equality premise of prior methods, reducing information loss in high-salience tokens under aggressive compression. It accelerates ViT inference without retraining.

entry.title: Detect by Yourself: Self-Designing Agentic Workflows for Few-Shot Graph Anomaly Detection

author.name: Tairan Huang, Qiang Chen, Yili Wang, Yueyue Ma, Changlong He, Xiu Su, Yi Chen

entry.summary: SignGAD reformulates few-shot graph anomaly detection from training a fixed detector to self-designing task-conditioned agentic workflows, addressing fixed pipelines and weak evidence in existing methods. It explicitly incorporates contextual and structural anomaly signals.

entry.title: On the Subgaussianity of Quantized Linear Maps: An AI-Assisted Note

author.name: Guangyi Zou, Roman Vershynin

entry.summary: This short note presents a dimension-independent subgaussian concentration bound for Gaussian vectors under coordinate-wise nonlinear maps, applied to sign-quantized linear maps, with the result reportedly discovered by Gemini 3.5 Flash. Co-authored by Roman Vershynin.

entry.title: Hurwitz Quaternion Multiplicative Quantization for KV Cache Compression

author.name: Kabir Swain, Sijie Han, Daniel Karl I. Weidele, Mauro Martino, David Cox, Antonio Torralba

entry.summary: HQMQ is a calibration-free KV cache compression method that treats 4-element chunks as quaternions and quantizes directions using the 24-element Hurwitz group times a random secondary codebook. The multiplicative composition yields many effective codewords with few stored parameters.

entry.title: MemGuard: Preventing Memory Contamination in Long-Term Memory-Augmented Large Language Models

author.name: Hyeonjeong Ha, Jeonghwan Kim, Cheng Qian, Jiayu Liu, William M. Campbell, Yue Wu, Yuji Zhang, Kathleen McKeown, Dilek Hakkani-Tur, Heng Ji

entry.summary: MemGuard is a type-aware long-term memory framework that preserves functional boundaries between stable user facts, episodic events, and behavioral rules to prevent heterogeneous memory contamination in memory-augmented LLMs. It avoids overgeneralizing context-specific events into broad claims during retrieval and generation.

entry.title: MIRAGE: Context-Aware Prompt Injection against Mobile GUI Agents via User-Generated Content

author.name: Ruoqi Guo, Yi Liu, Gelei Deng, Yiheng Xiong, Yuekang Li, Ying Zhang, Leo Yu Zhang, Lida Zhao, Ji Jie, Yuxiao Lu

entry.summary: MIRAGE is a context-aware prompt injection pipeline against mobile GUI agents that embeds attacker-controlled text into user-generated content regions of benign screenshots, without modifying the agent, app, or OS. It exposes that VLM-driven GUI agents cannot reliably separate trusted interface elements from user content.

entry.title: IRDS: Interpretable RLVR Data Selection via Verifier-Coupled Sparse Autoencoder Coverage

author.name: Yuhan Li, Mingxu Zhang, Dazhong Shen, Ying Sun

entry.summary: IRDS selects training data for reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards using sparse autoencoder clusters, making selection auditable on recognizable problem motifs while targeting instances the model fails but can learn from. It combines verifier signals with interpretable coverage via greedy log-determinant maximization.

entry.title: CLANE: Continual Learning of Actions on Neuromorphic Hardware from Event Cameras

author.name: Elvin Hajizada, Michael Neumeier, Edward Paxon Frady, Yulia Sandamirskaya, Axel von Arnim, Bing Li, Eyke H\"ullermeier

entry.summary: CLANE is the first end-to-end continual on-device learning pipeline for event-based action recognition deployed on Intel Loihi 2 neuromorphic hardware, combining a spiking CNN with continual learning to recognize new actions without forgetting. It targets privacy-preserving, low-latency adaptation for AR/VR and robotics.

entry.title: Position: Retire the "Positive Backdoor" Label -- Secret Alignment Requires Strict and Systematic Evaluation

author.name: Jianwei Li, Jung-Eun Kim

entry.summary: This position paper argues the community should retire the 'positive backdoor' label and instead treat trigger-activated hidden behaviors as 'Secret Alignment' that must be presumed insecure unless rigorously evaluated. It unifies existing proposals and calls for strict, standardized evaluation in the private/open-weight AI era.

entry.title: A Simple State Space Model Excels at Multivariate Time Series Classification

author.name: Hassan Saadatmand, Geoffrey I. Webb, Hamid Rezatofighi, Mahsa Salehi

entry.summary: This paper presents the first systematic study spanning diagonal SSMs (S4D) and input-dependent SSMs (Mamba family) on large-scale multivariate time series classification benchmarks, finding the surprising result that simpler S4D consistently outperforms Mamba variants in both accuracy and efficiency. It challenges the assumption that input-dependent complexity is necessary for top TSC performance.

entry.title: Heterogeneous Parallelism for Multimodal Large Language Model Training

author.name: Yashaswi Karnati, Kamran Jafari, Akash Mehra, Li Ding, Pranav Prashant Thombre, Ali Roshan Ghias, Shifang Xu, Parth Mannan, Yu Yao, Hao Wu, Eric Harper, Ashwath Aithal, Nima Tajbakhsh

entry.summary: Proposes heterogeneous parallelism for multimodal LLM training, letting encoder and LLM modules use independent TP/CP/PP/DP/EP layouts rather than a single LLM-centric sharding scheme. This improves throughput especially at long contexts where encoder and LLM parallelism needs diverge.

entry.title: Fine-Tuning Dynamics of In-Context Factual Recall in Transformers

author.name: Ruomin Huang, Eshaan Nichani, Jason D. Lee, Rong Ge

entry.summary: Duplicate position note.

entry.title: AtomComposer: Discovering Chemical Space from First Principles with Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Bjarke Hastrup, Francois Cornet, Tejs Vegge, Arghya Bhowmik

entry.summary: AtomComposer is a self-guided RL agent that autonomously constructs valid 3D molecular isomers under stoichiometric constraints, trained entirely online without any pretraining data to explore chemical space from first principles. A multi-composition training scheme enables broad generalization beyond single chemical formulas.

entry.title: High Performance, Low Reliability: Uncertainty Benchmarking for Tabular Foundation Models

author.name: Jos\'e Lucas De Melo Costa, Fabrice Popineau, Arpad Rimmel, Bich-Li\^en Doan

entry.summary: Benchmarks uncertainty quantification of tabular foundation models versus gradient-boosted trees across 112 datasets, revealing a performance-uncertainty trade-off where TFMs win on accuracy but offer worse conformal coverage. This highlights trustworthiness gaps in increasingly popular tabular foundation models.

entry.title: When Interpretability Is Unequally Distributed: Fairness in Hybrid Interpretable Models

author.name: Ziba Jabbar Zare, Ulrich A\"ivodji, Julien Ferry, Thibaut Vidal

entry.summary: Formalizes Interpretability Coverage Disparity, a fairness concern where hybrid interpretable models route some demographic groups to transparent decisions while disproportionately deferring others to a black box. It studies this disparity across multiple hybrid methods and fairness benchmarks.

entry.title: Activation Steering for Synthetic Data Generation: The Role of Diversity in Downstream Safety Detection

author.name: Vijeta Deshpande, Tootiya Giyahchi, Veena Padmanabhan, Leman Akoglu, Anna Rumshisky

entry.summary: Investigates whether activation steering can generate high-quality synthetic training data for downstream safety classifiers, introducing diversity as a previously absent quality axis. It evaluates across four concepts, two models, and four steering methods with intrinsic and extrinsic measures.

entry.title: Representation-Conditioned Diffusion Models for Guided Training Data Generation

author.name: Nithesh Chandher Karthikeyan, Jonas Unger, Gabriel Eilertsen

entry.summary: Evaluates classifiers trained on synthetic images from latent diffusion models conditioned on learned representations from DINOv2, DINOv3, and CLIP. Representation-conditioned generation significantly outperforms class-conditioned generation (+10.76 points top-1 on ImageNet100).

entry.title: Disentangling Language Roles in Multilingual LLM Task Execution

author.name: Qishi Zhan, Minxuan Hu, Seoyeon Jang, Lei Zhao, Ziheng Chen, Man Liang, Xinyue Xiang, Jiaxin Liu, Guansu Wang, Liang He

entry.summary: Introduces MTM-Bench, a controlled benchmark that fully crosses instruction language, content language, and response language across English, Spanish, and Chinese (27 triplets). It evaluates 20 LLMs to disentangle the three language roles in multilingual task execution.

entry.title: Soft Specialists: $\alpha$-R\'enyi Ensembles for Uncertainty-Aware LLM Post-Training

author.name: Paula Cordero-Encinar, Georgy Tyukin, Andrew B. Duncan

entry.summary: Proposes an alpha-Renyi variational framework for learning distributions over LLM post-training parameters, offering an uncertainty-aware alternative to deep ensembles. The objective interpolates between variational Bayes and predictively oriented posterior learning to balance plausible models against complementary specialists.

entry.title: Learning to target with network interference

author.name: Xiaomeng Wang, Hamsa Bastani, Osbert Bastani, Zhimei Ren

entry.summary: Studies adaptive targeting under network interference in a bandit setting where treatments spill over to others, establishing a regret lower bound and analyzing regimes with varying knowledge of the interference structure. It shows ignoring network structure leads to inefficient learning in large populations.

entry.title: How VLAs Fail Differently: Black-Box Action Monitoring Reveals Architecture-Specific Failure Signatures

author.name: Krishnam Gupta

entry.summary: This paper shows that different VLA architectures fail in predictable, architecture-specific ways at the motor-command level, finding direction reversal rate is a universal failure predictor while jerk monitoring works only for discrete-token policies. It critiques velocity-checking as the common but ineffective safety mechanism in deployment.

entry.title: UNIQUE: Universal Top-k Sparse Attention for Training-free Inference and Sparsity-aware Training

author.name: Keqi Deng, Shaoshi Ling, Ruchao Fan, Jinyu Li

entry.summary: UNIQUE is a universal top-k sparse attention framework operating at KV-page granularity, estimating per-page importance with a simple score combining key means and standard deviations for both training-free inference and sparsity-aware training. It addresses the KV cache bottleneck in long-context LLMs.

entry.title: Building Community-Centred NLP Resources for Puno Quechua

author.name: Elwin Huaman, Adrian Gamarra Lafuente, Johanna Cordova, Anna Korhonen

entry.summary: This work presents the first dedicated ASR resources for Puno Quechua, including a 66-hour speech corpus collected via participatory design and a systematic benchmark fine-tuning Whisper, wav2vec2, and XLS-R. It matters for low-resource language preservation and community-centred NLP.

entry.title: FABSVer: Faster Training and Better Self-Verification for LLM Mathematical Reasoning

author.name: Haihui Pan, Junwei Bao, Hongfei Jiang, Yang Song

entry.summary: FABSVer fuses solution generation and self-verification into a single generation pass to reduce training overhead for LLM mathematical reasoning. It also identifies and addresses a convergence bottleneck caused by a fixed reference model.

entry.title: The Abstraction Gap in Vision-Language Causal Reasoning

author.name: Chinh Hoang, Mohammad Rashedul Hasan

entry.summary: This paper introduces a dual-probe methodology and Abstraction Gap metric to distinguish linguistic plausibility from faithful causal reasoning in VLMs, evaluated on the 49,500-question CAGE benchmark across Pearl's causal hierarchy. Seven of eight models show large abstraction gaps.

entry.title: Long Live the Librarian! A Persistent Search Sub-Agent for Energy-Efficient Multi-Agent Software Engineering Systems

author.name: Seunghyuk Cho, Sunghyun Choi, Jaeseung Heo, Youngbin Choi, Saemi Moon, MoonJeong Park, Dongwoo Kim

entry.summary: Librarian is a persistent search sub-agent that tracks repository-search history to suppress redundant output tokens in multi-agent software engineering systems. It addresses energy inefficiency, noting output tokens cost 30-1000x more energy than input/cached tokens.

entry.title: Skill-as-Pseudocode: Refactoring Skill Libraries to Pseudocode for LLM Agents

author.name: Xinze Li, Yuhang Zang, Yixin Cao, Aixin Sun

entry.summary: Skill-as-Pseudocode automatically converts free-form markdown skill libraries into typed pseudocode with a four-check deterministic verifier for LLM agents. It addresses the confused-re-retrieve loop caused by agents re-deriving schemas and invocation syntax.

entry.title: MaskClaw: Edge-Side Personalized Privacy Arbitration for GUI Agents with Behavior-Driven Skill Evolution

author.name: Yanqiu Zhao, Dongying Zheng, Kaibo Huang, Yukun Wei, Zhongliang Yang, Linna Zhou

entry.summary: MaskClaw is an edge-side privacy arbitrator for GUI agents that decides Allow, Mask, or Ask on screenshots before raw screen data leaves a trusted environment. It uses local visual evidence and user-specific policy memory with behavior-driven skill evolution.

entry.title: Every9D-21M: Large-Scale Real-World 9D Canonicalization of Everyday Objects

author.name: Leonhard Sommer, Emil Akopyan, Adam Kortylewski

entry.summary: Every9D-21M is a large-scale real-world 9D pose dataset with annotations for 21.8M images across 700 everyday object categories, generated by reconstructing object-centric videos. It is two orders of magnitude larger than prior real-world 9D pose benchmarks.

entry.title: EgoRelight: Egocentric Human Capture and Illumination Recovery for Relightable and Photoreal Avatar Rendering

author.name: Jianchun Chen, Yinda Zhang, Rohit Pandey, Thabo Beeler, Marc Habermann, Christian Theobalt

entry.summary: EgoRelight is a holistic framework for egocentric telepresence that simultaneously captures full-body human performance, synthesizes relightable photorealistic appearance, and estimates lighting from a head-mounted display's constrained viewpoint. It unifies tasks previously treated in isolation.

entry.title: GEM: Generative Supervision Helps Embodied Intelligence

author.name: Ruowen Zhao, Bangguo Li, Zuyan Liu, Yinan Liang, Junliang Ye, Fangfu Liu, Diankun Wu, Zhengyi Wang, Xumin Yu, Yongming Rao, Han Hu, Jun Zhu

entry.summary: GEM integrates a depth-map generation task into vision-language model pretraining for embodied intelligence, bridging the gap between high-level semantics and low-level spatial knowledge. The generative supervision substantially improves embodied task performance within VLA frameworks.

entry.title: OSP-Next: Efficient High-Quality Video Generation with Sparse Sequence Parallelism, HiF8 Quantization, and Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Yunyang Ge, Xianyi He, Zezhong Zhang, Bin Lin, Bin Zhu, Xinhua Cheng, Li Yuan

entry.summary: OSP-Next is an efficient text-to-video generation model integrating sparse attention (Skiparse-2D), sparse sequence parallelism, HiF8 quantization, and reinforcement learning to reduce the quadratic cost of full attention. It maintains FlashAttention compatibility while improving efficiency.

entry.title: Colosseum V2: Benchmarking Generalization for Vision Language Action Models

author.name: Jeremy Morgan, Prajwal Vijay, Hyeonho Oh, Jincen Song, Ashvin Arora, Alina Du, Gaurav Sukhatme, Jesse Thomason, Ishika Singh

entry.summary: Colosseum V2 is a large-scale simulation benchmark for evaluating the generalization of vision-language-action models in robotic manipulation across 28 tasks, 13 categories, and two robot morphologies under diverse distribution shifts. It systematically reveals gaps between VLA perception/language abilities and robust behavior.

entry.title: What Frozen VLAs Already Know About Success: A Probing Study of Value-Like Structure in Foundation Robot Policies

author.name: Jiachen Zhang (Peking University, China Agricultural University), Junnan Nie (Peking University), Junyi Lao (Peking University), Wei Cheng (Peking University), Chenghao Liu (Peking University), Jiaxin Jiang (China Agricultural University), Songfang Huang (Peking University)

entry.summary: A probing study showing that frozen VLA policy representations (OpenVLA, Pi0.5, DINOv2, CLIP) implicitly encode value-like information about task success, recoverable via lightweight linear probes despite never being trained on reward. The signal exceeds baselines based on progress, time-to-go, or proprioception, suggesting reward structure can guide action choice without retraining.

entry.title: PEAM: Parametric Embodied Agent Memory through Contrastive Internalization of Experience in Minecraft

author.name: Yuchen Guo, Junli Gong, Hongmin Cai, Yiu-ming Cheung, Weifeng Su

entry.summary: Presents PEAM, an embodied Minecraft agent that converts retrieval-based memory into parameter-resident skills via a multimodal MoE-LoRA architecture, pairing a slow deliberative LLM with a fast reflexive module and treating failures as first-class training signals. It enables continual skill internalization without catastrophic forgetting.

entry.title: EAPO: Entropy-Driven Adaptive Positive-Negative Sample Weighting for Policy Optimization in Open-Ended QA

author.name: Yunsheng Zeng, Gen Li, Yuwei Miao, Xiandong Li, Yujin Wang, Siyu Chen, Luning Wang, Yunhao Qiao, Junfeng Wang, Jianwei Lv, Bo Yuan

entry.summary: Proposes EAPO, an entropy-driven adaptive weighting of positive and negative samples for RLVR in open-ended QA, finding negative samples govern diversity and the performance ceiling while positives drive quality and convergence. It generalizes verifiable-reward RL beyond closed-form tasks.

entry.title: Dr-CiK: A Testbed for Foresight-Driven Agents

author.name: Yihong Tang, Andrew Robert Williams, Arjun Ashok, Vincent Zhihao Zheng, Lijun Sun, Alexandre Drouin, Issam H. Laradji, \'Etienne Marcotte, Valentina Zantedeschi

entry.summary: Introduces Dr-CiK, a benchmark testing whether forecasting agents can autonomously retrieve, filter, and distill external context from a document corpus and produce evidence-supported forecasts, rather than assuming context is provided. It evaluates deep-research and forecasting agents under context ablations.

entry.title: MIRA: A Bilingual Benchmark for Medical Information Response Audit

author.name: Mengyu Xu, Qiaoxin Yang, Qianqian Wang, Xiwei Dai, Weiyi Wu, Chongyang Gao

entry.summary: Introduces MIRA, a bilingual benchmark auditing whether LLMs provide comparable medical information across user phrasing, register, and health-literacy signals, finding low-health-literacy phrasings consistently receive less complete information. It surfaces an equity gap in health-information responses.

entry.title: Look on Demand: A Cognitive Scheduling Framework for Visual Evidence Acquisition in Multimodal Reasoning

author.name: Yang Zhang, Xiaoshuai Sun, Rui Zhao, Wujin Sun, Yidong Chen, Jiayi Ji, Qian Chen, Rongrong Ji

entry.summary: This work proposes a cognitive scheduling framework that decides how and when to introduce visual evidence into multimodal reasoning, avoiding both static visual-to-text loss and linguistic dominance. It addresses faithfulness to visual evidence in multimodal models.

entry.title: Plan Before Search: Search Agents Need Plan

author.name: Zhipeng Qian, Zihan Liang, Yufei Ma, Ben Chen, Huangyu Dai, Jiayi Ji, Chenyi Lei, Wenwu Ou, Xiaoshuai Sun, Qibin Hou

entry.summary: Plan Before Search argues that retrieval-augmented reasoning agents benefit from explicitly decomposing questions into ordered sub-questions before retrieval, anchoring each search step to avoid drift. It questions whether SFT distillation is the only route to acquiring this planning skill.

entry.title: Do Agents Know What They Can't Do? Evaluating Feasibility Awareness in Tool-Using Agents

author.name: Liang Cheng, Mingsheng Cai, Jiuming Jiang, Luo Mai

entry.summary: FeasiGen is an automatic pipeline that constructs infeasible agent tasks by identifying critical tools required for success, enabling evaluation of whether tool-using agents recognize tasks they cannot complete. Detecting infeasibility early can reduce wasted execution cost.

entry.title: MUSE: Benchmarking Manufacturable, Functional, and Assemblable Text-to-CAD Generation

author.name: Xiaoyu Dong, Zhi Li, Xiao-Ming Wu

entry.summary: MUSE is a Text-to-CAD benchmark focused on complex editable boundary-representation assemblies, evaluating manufacturability, functionality, and assemblability through a three-stage code, geometry, and design-intent protocol. It moves beyond single-part geometric-similarity evaluation toward industrial design realism.

entry.title: VeriTrip: A Verifiable Benchmark for Travel Planning Agents over Unstructured Web Corpora

author.name: Yuting Xu, Jiayi Tian, Jian Liang, Xin Xiong, Hang Zhang, Mu Xu, Xiao-Yu Zhang

entry.summary: VeriTrip is a verifiable benchmark for travel-planning agents that shifts evaluation to evidence-grounded reasoning over unstructured multimodal web corpora, incorporating information noise, source contradictions, and visual grounding. It moves beyond API-centric tool-execution paradigms.

entry.title: Modeling Community Attitude through Reaction Tone: A Human-AI Collaborative Framework for Evaluating LLM Alignment with Linguistic Behaviors in Online Communities

author.name: Nuan Wen, Xuezhe Ma

entry.summary: CARE is a reaction-centered framework benchmarking whether LLM-simulated discourse matches authentic community responses to real-world news, using a fine-grained spectrum of illocutionary tones validated through human-AI collaboration. It moves beyond static social-identity labels in computational social analysis.

entry.title: FD-RAG: Federated Dual-System Retrieval-Augmented Generation

author.name: Tianhao Gao, Kai Yang, Yiyang Li

entry.summary: FD-RAG is a federated dual-system RAG framework that decouples lightweight memory access from on-demand LLM reasoning for edge deployment, learning adaptive hypergraphs over local corpora distilled into compact QA memories. It addresses fragmented knowledge and expensive LLM calls in decentralized settings.

entry.title: Beyond Motion Primitives: Behavioral Activity Recognition from Head-Mounted IMU

author.name: Chung-Ta Huang, Leopold Das, Jeffrey Zhou, Faizaan Siddique, Julia Seungjoo Baek, Serena Liu, Andrew Rusli, Todd Y. Zhou, Freddy Yu, Sinclair Hansen, Ziling Hu, Arnav Sharma, Mengyu Wang

entry.summary: This work pushes beyond motion primitives to behavioral-level activity recognition from head-mounted IMU sensors for AR smart glasses, building a 160K-sample Ego4D dataset and a 703K-parameter hierarchical HiT-HAR model. It maps the observability frontier of head-mounted IMU sensing.

entry.title: BIRDS: Characterizing and Understanding Biodiversity Impact of Large Language Model Serving

author.name: Tianyao Shi, Yi Ding

entry.summary: BIRDS is a framework quantifying the biodiversity impact of request-driven LLM serving, defining request-level functional units, operational and embodied impacts, and a Quality-Normalized Biodiversity Impact metric. It exposes quality-aware serving tradeoffs across models, GPUs, and regions.

entry.title: UserHarness: Harnessing User Minds for Stronger Agent Theory-of-Mind

author.name: Cheng Qian, Jiayu Liu, Heng Ji

entry.summary: UserHarness is a framework for improving agent Theory-of-Mind by explicitly reconstructing a user's mental state—beliefs updated through observations, intentions, and nested beliefs—rather than modeling behavior indirectly. It targets more effective agent assistants.

entry.title: ReSAE: Residualized Sparse Autoencoders for Multi-Layer Transformer Interventions

author.name: Prathyush Poduval, Calvin Yeung, Neel Desai, Mohsen Imani

entry.summary: ReSAEs fit affine maps between transformer layers and train each later-layer sparse autoencoder on the unexplained residual rather than the full activation, addressing the redundancy and interaction problems of layerwise dictionaries. This enables more coherent multi-layer interventions.

entry.title: Where Does Toxicity Live? Mechanistic Localization and Targeted Suppression in Language Models

author.name: Himanshu Beniwal, Mayank Singh

entry.summary: This paper introduces two retraining-free frameworks (Meow2X and TRNE) that localize toxicity to specific layers and neurons via activation differentials and suppress it through inference-time scaling or minimal rank-one weight edits. It reduces toxicity across five models without gradient descent while preserving language modeling quality.

entry.title: Extracting Small Translation Specialists from LLMs by Aggressively Pruning Experts

author.name: Liu O. Martin, Lucas Bandarkar, Nanyun Peng

entry.summary: This paper aggressively prunes experts from mixture-of-experts LLMs to extract small translation specialists, exploiting expert specialization and the separability of multilingual capabilities. The pruning requires no retraining and incurs negligible translation quality loss.

entry.title: Learning the Error Patterns of Language Models

author.name: Jinwoo Kim, Taylor Berg-KirkPatrick, Loris D'Antoni

entry.summary: This work introduces prefix filters, learned symbolic functions that capture the focused error patterns of LLMs in constrained-validity domains (like generating valid TypeScript), with an algorithm called Palla to learn them efficiently. The filters both quantify error patterns and constrain model outputs via constrained sampling.

entry.title: Measuring Form and Function in Language Models

author.name: H\'ector Javier V\'azquez Mart\'inez, Charles Yang

entry.summary: This paper introduces quantitative child-language-acquisition metrics to evaluate language models on the syntactic and discourse properties of English determiners, proposing a Contextual Alternative Choice prompting method. It enables direct comparison of models against children and independently established empirical benchmarks, finding only very large models meet both formal and functional benchmarks.

entry.title: MemTrace: Tracing and Attributing Errors in Large Language Model Memory Systems

author.name: Xinle Deng, Ruobin Zhong, Hujin Peng, Xiaoben Lu, Yanzhe Wu, Guang Li, Buqiang Xu, Yunzhi Yao, Jizhan Fang, Haoliang Cao, Junjie Guo, Yuan Yuan, Ziqing Ma, Yuanqiang Yu, Rui Hu, Baohua Dong, Hangcheng Zhu, Ningyu Zhang

entry.summary: MemTrace studies error tracing and attribution in LLM memory systems by transforming memory pipelines into executable memory evolution graphs for fine-grained tracing of information flow. It introduces MemTraceBench collected from systems like Long-Context, RAG, Mem0, and EverMemOS to study memory failure modes.

entry.title: Explicit Critic Guidance for Aligning Diffusion Models

author.name: Zhengyang Liang, Qihang Zhang, Ceyuan Yang

entry.summary: Proposes a state-aligned latent actor-critic framework for aligning diffusion models via online RL, where the diffusion model serves as its own timestep-conditioned value function predicting on noisy latents. This enables trajectory-level PPO and reusable critic guidance for inference-time steering.

entry.title: Revisiting ML Training under Fully Homomorphic Encryption: Convergence Guarantees, Differential Privacy, and Efficient Algorithms

author.name: Yvonne Zhou, Mingyu Liang, Ivan Brugere, Danial Dervovic, Yue Guo, Antigoni Polychroniadou, Min Wu, Dana Dachman-Soled

entry.summary: Provides the first theoretical convergence analysis of ML training under fully homomorphic encryption combined with a differentially private algorithm tailored to encrypted computation, using polynomial approximations of activations. It improves efficiency over standard DP-GD while preserving privacy without per-sample gradient clipping.

entry.title: Measure-to-measure Regression with Transformers

author.name: Matthew Vandergrift, Martha White, Yury Polyanskiy, Philippe Rigollet, Lazar Atanackovic

entry.summary: Studies measure-to-measure regression, learning maps between probability measures (point clouds) from observed input-output measure pairs using transformers, treating whole distributions as data points. This is motivated by applications like cell populations that evolve collectively rather than independently.

entry.title: Chreode: A Cell World Model for One-Step Temporal Dynamics and Perturbation Prediction

author.name: Mufan Qiu, Genhui Zheng, Yinuo Xu, Ruichen Zhang, Ying Ding, Qi Long, Tianlong Chen

entry.summary: Chreode is a one-step cell world model predicting action-conditioned cell-state transitions (developmental signals, genetic perturbations) via a structured residual transition operator with a Waddington-inspired decomposition. It shifts distributional evolution to training time for single-pass generation, generalizing across datasets.

entry.title: Mitigating Adaptive Attacks against Reasoning Models with Activation Consistency Training

author.name: Avidan Shah, Jannik Brinkmann, Rico Angell

entry.summary: Studies consistency training to defend reasoning models against adaptive jailbreaks and prompt injection, comparing output-level (BCT) and activation-level (ACT) variants across five reasoning models. Finds ACT competitive with other training-based defenses while requiring only self-supervised clean/wrapped prompt pairs and remaining more robust under adaptive attacks.

entry.title: Thinned Mean Field Langevin Dynamics

author.name: Zonghao Chen, Heishiro Kanagawa, Fran\c{c}ois-Xavier Briol, Chris J. Oates, Lester Mackey

entry.summary: Proposes KT-MFLD, which reduces the quadratic cost of mean-field Langevin dynamics by having each particle interact only with a thinned coreset of size order square-root N. This leverages kernel thinning to cut computational complexity while preserving convergence properties.

entry.title: Affective Music Recommendation: A Rollout-Based World Model for Offline Preference Optimization

author.name: Audrey Chan, Aaron Labb\'e, Jacob Lavoie, Jordan Bannister, Ars\`ene Fansi Tchango, Guillaume Lajoie, Laurent Charlin

entry.summary: Describes AMRS, a deployed affective music recommendation system built around a rollout-based causal transformer world model for offline preference optimization. It serves clinical and consumer wellness users where online emotional experimentation is ethically constrained.

entry.title: A Unified Structured Query Understanding Framework for Industrial Semantic Search

author.name: Ping Liu, Qianqi Shen, Jianqiang Shen, Chunnan Yao, Kevin Kao, Rajat Arora, Dan Xu, Baofen Zheng, Yunxiang Ren, Benjamin Le, Ali Hooshmand, Igor Lapchuk, Juan Bottaro, Raghavan Muthuregunathan, Caleb Johnson, Liangjie Hong, Jingwei Wu, Wenjing Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes and deploys a unified structured query understanding system consolidating fragmented industrial search components into a single small language model performing schema-constrained generation. It introduces Query Illuminator, a teacher model for auto-annotation and distillation.

entry.title: Semiparametrically Efficient Inference for Kernel Measures of Noise Heterogeneity

author.name: Jakub Wornbard, Zikai Shen, Dimitri Meunier, Arthur Gretton

entry.summary: Develops semiparametrically efficient inference for kernel measures of noise heterogeneity in additive noise models, constructing a Hilbert-valued one-step estimator that corrects first-stage ML regression bias. It yields bootstrap-calibrated tests for residual independence and goodness of fit.

entry.title: {\Omega}-QVLA: Robust Quantization for Vision-Language-Action Models via Composite Rotation and Per-step Scaling

author.name: Xinyu Wang, Mingze Li, Sicheng Lyu, Dongxiu Liu, Kaicheng Yang, Ziyu Zhao, Yufei Cui, Xiao-Wen Chang, Peng Lu

entry.summary: Omega-QVLA is a training-free post-training quantization framework that compresses both the language backbone and the entire diffusion action head of VLA models to uniform W4A4 precision using composite rotation and per-step scaling. It challenges the belief that uniformly quantizing action heads is unstable.

entry.title: ReverseMath: Answer Inversion for Scalable and Verifiable Mathematical Problem Generation

author.name: Raoyuan Zhao, Yihong Liu, Yupei Du, Hinrich Sch\"utze, Michael A. Hedderich

entry.summary: ReverseMath scalably generates new math problems by masking a numerical value, treating the original answer as a known condition, and rewriting so the masked value becomes the new answer with verifiable correctness. It mitigates benchmark contamination and memorization issues in LLM math evaluation.

entry.title: Escape the Language Prior: Mitigating Late-Stage Modality Collapse in Audio Reasoning via Modality-Aware Policy Optimization

author.name: Cihan Xiao, Yiwen Shao, Chenxing Li, Xiang He, Zhenwen Liang, Steve Yves, Sanjeev Khudanpur, Liefeng Bo

entry.summary: MAPO is a modality-aware policy optimization framework that addresses late-stage modality collapse in audio reasoning models, where extended chain-of-thought generation progressively abandons the audio signal for textual priors. It applies non-uniform policy gradients accounting for tokens' dependence on the source modality.

entry.title: Beyond One Path: Evaluating and Enhancing Divergent Thinking in Interactive LLM Agents

author.name: Jihyeong Park, Ingeol Baek, Jeonghyun Park, Hwanhee Lee

entry.summary: MUTATE is an interactive benchmark evaluating divergent thinking in LLM agents at path-level and action-level, scoring both completed and off-path attempts. It reveals structural blind spots in frontier models for creative iterative reasoning.

entry.title: Mobile-Aptus: Confidence-Driven Proactive and Robust Interaction in MLLM-based Mobile-Using Agents

author.name: Zheng Wu, Pengzhou Cheng, Zongru Wu, Yuan Guo, Tianjie Ju, Aston Zhang, Gongshen Liu, Zhuosheng Zhang

entry.summary: Mobile-Aptus introduces a confidence integration framework for mobile-using MLLM agents to balance over-execution and over-soliciting of human help. It enables confidence-driven proactive and robust interaction.

entry.title: VLMs May Not Globally Enhance Human Alignment over LLMs During Natural Reading

author.name: Jinzhou Wu, Zhengwu Ma, Jixing Li, Baoping Tang, Zitong Lu

entry.summary: This study compares matched LLM and VLM pairs in a text-only setting against human fMRI and eye-tracking data to test whether multimodal training makes text representations more human-like. It finds multimodal pretraining does not confer a uniform global alignment advantage.

entry.title: Personal Visual Memory from Explicit and Implicit Evidence

author.name: Viet Nguyen, Thao Nguyen, Vishal M. Patel, Yuheng Li

entry.summary: This work introduces a benchmark for personal visual memory targeting both explicit and implicit evidence carried by images, and proposes VisualMem, a hybrid visual-text memory architecture. It addresses the text-centric limitation of existing memory systems for personalized agents.

entry.title: Rethinking Video-Language Model from the Language Input Perspective

author.name: Xiang Fang, Wanlong Fang, Changshuo Wang, Xiaoye Qu, Daizong Liu

entry.summary: SIGMA is a semantic-difference instruction-grounding mask annotator that automatically recovers pixel-level masks from existing edited image pairs for training image manipulation localization models. It overcomes diffusion-induced perturbations and missed unintended editor side-effects.

entry.title: Uni-LaViRA: Language-Vision-Robot Actions Translation for Unified Embodied Navigation

author.name: Hongyu Ding, Sizhuo Zhang, Ziming Xu, Jinwen Guo, Hongxiu Liu, Xingzhi Cheng, Zixuan Chen, Haifei Qi, Duo Wang, Hao Xu, Jieqi Shi, Yifan Zhang, Jing Huo, Jian Cheng, Yang Gao, Jiebo Luo

entry.summary: Uni-LaViRA argues that navigation generality can be obtained structurally rather than solely through data scale, reducing navigation to a single language-vision-robot actions translation. It emits semantic directional commands and pixel-level visual targets within the natural output manifold of pretrained multimodal LLMs.

entry.title: Cross-Entropy Games and Frost Training

author.name: Arthur Renard, Franck Gabriel, Valentin Hartmann, Cl\'ement Hongler

entry.summary: Introduces Frost Training, which exploits the reward gradient in embedding space (the same signal used in GCG jailbreaking) to boost Monte Carlo policy optimization for LLM-as-a-judge tasks framed as Cross-Entropy Games. It improves best-of-k scores and training speed in GRPO infilling.

entry.title: Diagnosing Live Within-Policy Instruction Conflicts in LLM Agents with Witnessed Resolution Profiles

author.name: Lu Yan, Xuan Chen, Xiangyu Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces WIRE, a pipeline for diagnosing live intra-policy rule conflicts in LLM agent prompt policies by extracting rules, encoding them as logic clauses, using satisfiability checks to find collisions, and judging model resolutions. It surfaces hidden conflicts among individually reasonable standing rules.

entry.title: Revealing Algorithmic Deductive Circuits for Logical Reasoning

author.name: Phuong Minh Nguyen, Tien Huu Dang, Naoya Inoue

entry.summary: Uses mechanistic interpretability to localize attention heads responsible for individual reasoning steps in symbolic-aided chain-of-thought, aligning reasoning steps with token logits to characterize information flow. It probes how LLMs understand abstract algorithmic reasoning from few demonstrations.

entry.title: MolLingo: Molecule-Native Representations for LLM-Powered Scientific Agents

author.name: Thao Nguyen, Heng Ji

entry.summary: Presents MolLingo, a multi-agent system emulating a chemist's reasoning for molecular design, coordinating Literature, Chemist, and Orchestrator agents via shared memory with domain tools and a BRICS-based fragment enumeration method. It enables iterative, evidence-driven molecular reasoning.

entry.title: Geometry of Human Perceptual Domains Emerges Transiently in LLM Representations

author.name: Simardeep Singh, Paras Chopra

entry.summary: Investigates whether LLM internal representations exhibit geometric structure resembling human perceptual organization across color, pitch, emotion, and taste, finding layer-wise transient emergence of such structure despite purely textual training. It connects model geometry to human perceptual domains.

entry.title: AsyncTool: Evaluating the Asynchronous Function Calling Capability under Multi-Task Scenarios

author.name: Kou Shi (University of Science and Technology of China), Ziao Zhang (University of Science and Technology of China), Shiting Huang (University of Science and Technology of China), Avery Nie (University of Toronto), Zhen Fang (University of Science and Technology of China), Qiuchen Wang (University of Science and Technology of China), Lin Chen (University of Science and Technology of China), Huaian Chen (University of Science and Technology of China), Zehui Chen (University of Science and Technology of China), Feng Zhao (University of Science and Technology of China)

entry.summary: Proposes AsyncTool, a benchmark evaluating asynchronous function-calling where agents must use idle time during tool-response latency to handle multiple concurrent tasks. It introduces the temporal dimension of tool use overlooked by single-task benchmarks.

entry.title: Zipping the Thought: When and How Compressed Reasoning Data Works in LLM Post-Training

author.name: Kohsei Matsutani, Gouki Minegishi, Takeshi Kojima, Yusuke Iwasawa, Yutaka Matsuo

entry.summary: Proposes a taxonomy of chain-of-thought (Explicit, Composed, Implicit) and studies how compressed reasoning data affects LLM post-training using a controlled synthetic compositional task. It clarifies when and how shortened CoT traces help or hurt the performance-token-cost trade-off.

entry.title: Relevant Is Not Warranted: Evidence-Force Calibration for Cited RAG

author.name: Pin Qian, Su Wang, Xiaoyuan Wang, Yihang Chen, Wenxuan Xu, Qiaolin Yu, Shuhuai Lin, Sipeng Zhang, Junxian You, Xinpeng Wei

entry.summary: Studies citation laundering in cited RAG, where a topically relevant source is used to warrant an over-strong claim, and introduces FORCEBENCH, a contrastive stress test pairing evidence-calibrated claims with force-raised variants across five axes. It probes evidence-force calibration beyond mere citation presence.

entry.title: MemCog: From Memory-as-Tool to Memory-as-Cognition in Conversational Agents

author.name: Zihan Li, Xingyu Fan, Feifei Li, Wenhui Que

entry.summary: Proposes MemCog, a memory-as-cognition system that integrates memory access into reasoning via a navigable memory store with associative link graphs, a cross-dimensional navigation interface, and a proactive reasoning protocol. It moves beyond one-shot passive retrieval in conversational agents.

entry.title: ZipRL: Adaptive Multi-Turn Context Compression with Hindsight Response Replay

author.name: Zhexin Hu, Li Wang, Xiaohan Wang, Jiajun Chai, Xiaojun Guo, Wei Lin, Guojun Yin

entry.summary: Proposes ZipRL, an adaptive multi-turn context compression framework for RLVR with multi-granularity non-uniform reduction and Hindsight Response Replay to densify sparse long-horizon training signals. It balances information retention and token efficiency for agentic tasks.

entry.title: Localizing Input Uncertainty Quantification for Large Language Models via Shapley Values

author.name: Seongjun Lee, Suwan Yoon, Changhee Lee

entry.summary: This paper uses Shapley values to localize input-level uncertainty in LLMs, identifying which parts of a user input drive uncertainty rather than producing only scalar scores. It aims to give actionable clarification guidance for safe high-stakes use.

entry.title: AI, Take the Wheel: What Drives Delegation and Trust in Human-Computer Cooperative Question Answering?

author.name: Maharshi Gor, Yoo Yeon Sung, Yu Hou, Eve Fleisig, Irene Ying, Tianyi Zhou, Jordan Boyd-Graber

entry.summary: This study examines two distinct human reliance decisions on AI in a question-answering game: delegation (acting autonomously) versus adoption (evaluating suggestions), studied together with the same users. It advances understanding of when and why humans trust AI in collaborative settings.

entry.title: Prompt Codebooks: Discrete Compositional Optimization for Language Model Instruction Refinement

author.name: Jyotirmoy Nath, Neeraj Kumar, Brejesh Lall

entry.summary: Prompt Codebooks recast automatic prompt optimization as compositional discrete learning over a finite vocabulary of reusable instruction units routed per input, rather than monolithic string editing. It enables reuse of learned sub-behaviors and more robust prompt updates.

entry.title: ProvMind: Provenance-grounded reasoning for materials synthesis

author.name: Yiming Zhang, Ryo Tamura, Koji Tsuda

entry.summary: ProvMind introduces MatProcBench, a provenance-grounded benchmark from literature-mined synthesis graphs, and a process-memory reasoning framework that retrieves analogous processes for materials synthesis reasoning. It evaluates route continuity and causal consistency under distribution shift.

entry.title: BioELX: Cross-lingual Biomedical Entity Linking via Alias-based Retrieval and LLM Ranking

author.name: Yi Wang, Corina Dima, Liangyu Zhong, Steffen Staab

entry.summary: BioELX is a two-stage cross-lingual biomedical entity linking framework that requires no task-specific annotated data, using Wikidata-derived multilingual aliases for retrieval plus LLM reranking. It improves generalization to non-English mentions over SapBERT baselines.

entry.title: StoryMI: Steerable Multi-Agent Therapeutic Dialogue Generation

author.name: Qingyu Meng, Min Chen, Dingming Liu, Yifan Mo, Yue Su, Xin Sun, Koen Hindriks, Jiahuan Pei

entry.summary: StoryMI is a multi-LLM-agent framework for controllable motivational interviewing dialogue generation, expanding questionnaire-based client profiles into situational stories and coordinating MI-coded utterances via an interaction agent. It proposes a two-level evaluation aligned with clinical MI standards.

entry.title: Informing AI Policy Assessment using Large-Scale Simulation of Interventions

author.name: Julia Barnett, Kimon Kieslich, Natali Helberger, Nicholas Diakopoulos

entry.summary: This work proposes a methodology combining participatory policy evaluation, expert cost assessment, and LLM-based harm-mitigation assessment, using a genetic algorithm to explore vast spaces of AI policy combinations. It helps policymakers prioritize interventions against AI harms.

entry.title: REC-CBM: Rubric-Aware Error-Correction Concept Bottleneck Models for Trustworthy Open-Ended Grading

author.name: Chengshuai Zhao, Fan Zhang, Kumar Satvik Chaudhary, Yiwen Li, Lo Pang-Yun Ting, Ying-Chih Chen, Huan Liu

entry.summary: REC-CBM extends concept bottleneck models for trustworthy open-ended grading by explicitly modeling fine-grained rubric dimensions, ordinal structure, and error correction. It aims to provide interpretable, verifiable automated grading that educators can trust.

entry.title: Advancing Direct Training for Spiking Neural Networks with Circulate-Firing Neurons and Learnable Gradients

author.name: Feifan Zhou, Xiang Wei, Yang Liu, Qiang Yu

entry.summary: This paper advances direct training of Spiking Neural Networks with a circulate-firing neuron model that better leverages membrane potential dynamics and learnable surrogate gradients across time steps. It aims to close the performance gap between SNNs and ANNs.

entry.title: MGRetrieval: Memory-Guided Reflective Retrieval for Long-Term Dialogue Agents

author.name: Tan Wang, Yunwei Dong

entry.summary: MGRetrieval is a memory-guided reflective retrieval strategy for long-term dialogue agents that grounds reflective retrieval to reduce unstable retrieval paths and latency caused by one-shot or LLM-generated retrieval. It improves evidence retrieval from redundant memory contexts.

entry.title: Checking Fact with Better Retrieval: Dynamic Contrastive Learning for Evidence Retrieval

author.name: Zhongtian Hua, Yi Luo, Meijia Yu, Yingjie Han

entry.summary: DACLR is a dynamic adaptive contrastive learning method for multimodal fact-checking evidence retrieval that converts multimodal evidence to text via an MLLM and extracts event-level features to retrieve relevant rather than merely similar evidence. It improves downstream claim verification.

entry.title: Aligning LLMs with Human Uncertainty: A Beta-Bernoulli Calibrator for LLM Forecasting

author.name: Hui Dai, Ryan Teehan, Parsa Torabian, Mengye Ren

entry.summary: The Beta-Bernoulli Calibrator converts an LLM point forecast into a distribution over event likelihood, learning from both binary outcomes and aggregated human forecasts (crowd probability and agreement). It aims to align LLM forecasting uncertainty with human uncertainty.

entry.title: Worker Disagreement Reveals Sharp Directions in Local SGD

author.name: Tolga Dimlioglu, Kristi Topollai, Anna Choromanska

entry.summary: This paper shows that worker disagreement in Local SGD reveals the sharp dominant Hessian directions of the loss landscape, providing a cheap Hessian-free estimate of curvature geometry. It theoretically links worker-average gap covariance to gradient noise and Hessian curvature.

entry.title: Do Models Know Why They Changed Their Mind? Interpretability and Faithfulness of Chain-of-Thought Under Knowledge Conflict

author.name: Pruthvinath Jeripity Venkata

entry.summary: This paper tests whether chain-of-thought faithfully reports the mechanism by which models resolve knowledge conflicts between training and a contradicting document. It finds CoT is highly stable across opposite decisions (96% similarity on flip pairs), but self-rated confidence carries a faint genuine signal for obscure facts.

entry.title: Geometry-Correct Diffusion Posterior Sampling with Denoiser-Pullback Curvature Guidance and Manifold-Aligned Damping

author.name: Seunghyeok Shin, Minwoo Kim, Dabin Kim, Hongki Lim

entry.summary: This work replaces hand-tuned scalar guidance in diffusion posterior sampling with a per-noise-level damped Gauss-Newton correction computed in diffusion-state coordinates, using matrix-free GMRES and manifold-aligned damping. It improves stability under stiff, operator-dependent curvature in inverse problems.

entry.title: Learning Compositional Latent Structure with Vector Networks

author.name: Niclas Pokel, Benjamin F. Grewe

entry.summary: The Vector Network replaces fixed weight matrices with libraries of reusable rank-1 weight atoms, inferring a sparse active set per input via layer-local energy minimization with bottom-up and top-down constraints. This composes input-specific low-rank weight matrices for compositional, reusable computation.

entry.title: Mind the Gap: Mixtures of Gaussians in Approximate Differential Privacy

author.name: Huikang Liu, Aras Selvi, Wolfram Wiesemann

entry.summary: This paper designs mixture mechanisms for approximate differential privacy by mixing multiple Gaussians with shared variance but different means and weights, deriving tight variance conditions for (epsilon, delta)-DP. It focuses on improving moderate and low-privacy regimes over the analytic Gaussian mechanism.

entry.title: GUI Agents for Continual Game Generation

author.name: Yixu Huang, Bo Li, Na Li, Zhe Wang, Kaijie Chen, Haonan Ge, Qingyi Si, Yuanzhe Shen, Ruihan Yang, Guangjing Wang, Hongcheng Guo

entry.summary: This work argues game generation requires a player to detect interaction-level failures, introducing PlaytestArena where GUI agents evaluate 200 browser games against in-play behavior rubrics, plus a subjective playtesting role. It reframes game generation evaluation beyond one-shot code translation.

entry.title: Routing-Aligned Fine-Tuning for Multilingual Downstream Tasks in Mixture-of-Experts Models

author.name: Guanzhi Deng, Kuan Wu, Haibo Wang, Shing Yin Wong, Sichun Luo, Linqi Song

entry.summary: RA-MoE proposes routing-aligned fine-tuning for multilingual downstream tasks in MoE models, exploiting the finding that middle layers form a language-universal alignment zone where routing divergence predicts per-language performance gaps. It uses a four-way correctness taxonomy across English and target languages to guide adaptation.

entry.title: Functional Entropy: Predicting Functional Correctness in LLM-Generated Code with Uncertainty Quantification

author.name: Dylan Bouchard, Mohit Singh Chauhan, Zeya Ahmad, Ho-Kyeong Ra

entry.summary: This paper systematically evaluates how uncertainty quantification techniques transfer to code generation across three languages, five LLMs, and over 1,700 problems, introducing functional entropy. It finds token-probability methods generalize while NLI-based sampling methods fail because NLI models cannot distinguish functionally different code.

entry.title: Efficient Pre-Training of LLMs through Truncated SVD Layers

author.name: Kaivan Kamali, Kajetan Schweighofer, Hormoz Shahrzad, Olivier Francon, Babak Hodjat, Risto Miikkulainen

entry.summary: TSVD is a framework for efficient LLM pretraining that maintains low-rank and strict orthonormality throughout training using a spectral energy-based heuristic for adaptive rank selection and caching to enforce orthonormality. It aims to reduce the cost-prohibitive expense of pretraining at scale.

entry.title: Rethinking Memory as Continuously Evolving Connectivity

author.name: Jizhan Fang, Buqiang Xu, Zhixian Wang, Haoliang Cao, Xinle Deng, Baohua Dong, Hangcheng Zhu, Ruohui Huang, Gang Yu, Ying Wei, Guozhou Zheng, Feiyu Xiong, Haofen Wang, Huajun Chen, Ningyu Zhang

entry.summary: FluxMem is a connectivity-evolving memory framework that models LLM agent memory as a heterogeneous graph and progressively refines its topology through initial connection formation, feedback-driven refinement, and long-term consolidation. It repairs missing links, prunes interference, aligns abstraction granularity, and distills successful trajectories during execution rather than treating memory as a static repository.

entry.title: OmniVerifier-M1: Multimodal Meta-Verifier with Explicit Structured Recalibration

author.name: Xinchen Zhang, Bowei Liu, Jiale Liu, Chufan Shi, Yizhen Zhang, Junhong Liu, Youliang Zhang, Zhiheng Li, Yujiu Yang, Ling Yang

entry.summary: OmniVerifier-M1 is a multimodal meta-verifier that leverages verifier-generated rationales rather than decision-only signals, finding that symbolic verifier outputs like bounding boxes outperform textual explanations and enable efficient rule-based RL rewards. It also decouples reinforcement learning for structured recalibration of verification feedback.

entry.title: Can Entry-Wise Clipping Give Spectral Control of Stochastic Gradients?

author.name: Zitao Song, Cedar Site Bai, Zhe Zhang, Brian Bullins, David F. Gleich

entry.summary: Investigates whether cheap entry-wise gradient clipping can provide spectral control over heavy-tailed stochastic gradient noise, normally requiring costly spectral normalization (e.g., Muon). A first-order perturbation analysis shows a localization property under which entry-wise clipping achieves spectral control.

entry.title: Knowing When to Ask: Segment-Level Credit Assignment for LLM Tool Use

author.name: Abhijit Kumar, Zoey Wu, Mohit Suley

entry.summary: CARL (Competence-Aware RL) trains a critic on a model's own rollouts to perform segment-level credit assignment for LLM tool use, learning when parametric knowledge suffices versus when external tools are needed. This addresses the failure of trajectory-level rewards to isolate which tool call helped.

entry.title: Reward Transfer from Inverse Reinforcement Learning: A Coupled Minimax Approach

author.name: Guang-Yuan Hao, Lars van der Laan, Aur\'elien Bibaut, Nathan Kallus

entry.summary: Studies transferring rewards learned via inverse RL from a source environment to RL in a different target environment, formulating a coupled minimax system of Bellman equations solved jointly rather than sequentially. The coupled approach removes first-order influence of source-reward estimation error, improving robustness.

entry.title: RW-TTT: Batched Serving for Request-Owned Test-Time Training State

author.name: Jian Yang, Zhizhuo Kou, Yao Tian, Hao Zhang, Han Chen, Sirui Han, Yike Guo

entry.summary: RW-TTT enables batched serving of test-time training LLMs where each request owns and updates its own state (fast weights, low-rank deltas), by tagging decode steps with owner/version/READ-WRITE effects and batching only compatible phases. It achieves large throughput gains while preserving correctness.

entry.title: Self-Consistency via Marginal Sharpening

author.name: Aleksei Arzhantsev, Otmane Sakhi, Nicolas Chopin

entry.summary: Reframes self-consistency as an inference-time objective by sharpening the answer marginal rather than the full-output distribution, arguing that what matters is answers supported by many plausible reasoning paths. It offers an efficient approximation to this marginal target.

entry.title: Compositional Generalization in Autoregressive Models via Logit Composition

author.name: Aakash Kumar, Maria Sofia Bucarelli, Emanuele Natale

entry.summary: Introduces a principled logit-composition strategy for composing autoregressive models, inspired by diffusion composition methods, proving that under factorized conditionals the composition is projective with each component controlling its own output subspace without interference. It further shows composition preserves length-generalization.

entry.title: LEIA: Learned Environment for Interactive Architected Materials

author.name: Haiqian Yang, Yuan Cao, Markus J. Buehler

entry.summary: LEIA is a world model for interactive architected materials that lets engineers apply boundary conditions step by step and observe resulting deformation and stress fields in real time, handling large 3D unstructured meshes and history-dependent nonlinear material dynamics. It introduces the MicroPlate benchmark for architected plates.

entry.title: Universal Time Series Generation with Neural Controlled Differential Equations

author.name: Torben Berndt, Elyes Farjallah, Leif Seute, Raeid Saqur, Benjamin Walker, Jan St\"uhmer

entry.summary: Extends sequence-universality results of state space models to generative time-series modeling, proving Structured Linear Controlled Differential Equations (SLiCEs) are universal time-series generators in a Wasserstein sense and proposing Generative SLiCEs for flow matching on path space. It provides both theory and empirical expressivity for continuous-time generation.

entry.title: A Generalized Tikhonov Layer for Interpretable-by-design Graph Neural Networks

author.name: Nicolas Tremblay, Benjamin Ricaud, Filippo Maria Bianchi

entry.summary: Proposes the Tikhonov layer, an interpretable-by-design graph neural network layer whose closed-form propagation matrix directly reveals which features and topology aspects drive predictions. The layer output is the exact minimizer of a generalized graph Tikhonov regularization problem.

entry.title: Expressive Power of Floating-Point Neural Networks with Arbitrary Reduction Orders and Inexact Activation Implementations

author.name: Yeachan Park, Geonho Hwang, Wonyeol Lee, Sejun Park

entry.summary: Studies the expressive power of floating-point neural networks under realistic execution semantics including arbitrary reduction orders and inexact activations with bounded ulp errors. This extends expressivity theory beyond idealized exact-arithmetic assumptions.

entry.title: Identifiable Bayesian Deep Generative Copulas with Unknown Layer Widths for Data with Arbitrary Marginal Distributions

author.name: Joseph Feldman, Yuqi Gu

entry.summary: Introduces the Deep Discrete Encoder Copula, an identifiable and interpretable deep generative model for multivariate data with arbitrary marginals, using a hierarchical binary latent network within a copula framework. Rank likelihoods decouple marginal modeling from posterior inference.

entry.title: Structure over Pixels: Learning Variable-Length Visual Programs

author.name: Piotr Wyrwi\'nski, Kacper Dobek, Krzysztof Krawiec

entry.summary: Proposes STROP, a discrete visual tokenizer that forms structural scene representations and simultaneously learns the appropriate per-image sequence length using a four-phase curriculum supervised against frozen DINOv3 features. It emphasizes structure over pixel reconstruction.

entry.title: Structure-Guided Visual Perturbation Neutralization for LVLMs

author.name: Yuanhe Zhang, Xueting Wang, YanBin Ren, Haoran Gao, Xinhan Zheng, Zhenhong Zhou, Fanyu Meng, Li Sun, Sen Su

entry.summary: Proposes SIGN, a lightweight plug-and-play defense for large vision-language models that neutralizes pixel-level adversarial perturbations while respecting cross-modal alignment. It avoids the heavy image modifications and overhead of prior LVLM defenses.

entry.title: Learning Logical Operations for Arbitrary Quantum Error Correction Codes

author.name: Nico Meyer, Christopher Mutschler, Dominik Seu{\ss}, Andreas Maier, Daniel D. Scherer

entry.summary: Presents a general learning-based framework that constructs physical implementations of logical operations for arbitrary quantum error-correcting codes given only an encoding circuit, enforcing transversality or shallow depth. It extends to co-designing non-additive encodings tailored to noise models.

entry.title: LCO: LLM-based Constraint Optimization for Safer Agentic LLMs in Real-world Tasks

author.name: Jiayong Wan, Jiawei Chen, Zhaoxia Yin, Liu Shuyuan, Hang Su

entry.summary: LCO reduces in-context reward hacking in agentic LLMs through a self-thought module for proactive safety deliberation and constraint optimization, without model fine-tuning. It targets harmful side effects from agents over-optimizing proxy objectives during environment interaction.

entry.title: Beyond Input Understanding: Diagnosing Multilingual Mathematical Reasoning with Directed Acyclic Trace Graphs

author.name: Jiaqiao Zhang, Zhoujun Li, Raoyuan Zhao, Jian Lan, Thomas Seidl, Michael A. Hedderich, Hinrich Sch\"utze, Yihong Liu

entry.summary: This paper introduces DATG, a Directed Acyclic Trace Graph framework that maps reasoning traces to language-independent mathematical anchors to diagnose multilingual reasoning failures, showing that controlling reasoning language affects accuracy even on English problems. It reveals language affects reasoning execution, not just input understanding.

entry.title: Narrative Flattening: How Post-Training Compresses Thematic, Affective, and Stylistic Variation in LLM Fiction

author.name: Zehan Li, Yutong Zhu, Siyang Wu, Honglin Bao, James A. Evans

entry.summary: This paper investigates where LLM fiction flatness originates in training by comparing OLMo 32B checkpoints (Base, SFT, DPO, RLVR) against human text across three story domains, isolating post-training effects on thematic, affective, and stylistic variation. It finds post-training compresses narrative diversity.

entry.title: GeneralThinker: Domain-General Reasoning through Likelihood-Guided Answer-Conditioned Optimization

author.name: Shengmin Piao, Sanghyun Park

entry.summary: GeneralThinker reformulates reasoning supervision as dense answer-conditioned optimization, evaluating reasoning trajectories via ground-truth answer likelihood for token-level credit assignment without domain-specific verifiers. It aims to generalize RLVR-style training to arbitrary domains.

entry.title: Beyond pass@k: Redundancy-Aware RLVR for Multi-Sample Code Generation

author.name: Le Bronnec Florian, Alexandre Verine, Rio Yokota, Benjamin Negrevergne

entry.summary: This work studies implementation-level redundancy in code generation using a plagiarism-detection tool, showing correctness-only RLVR concentrates generations around repeated implementations while Pass@k-aware objectives maintain diversity and improve larger-budget performance. It moves beyond Pass@k to redundancy-aware training.

entry.title: Framing Matters: Addressing Framing Sensitivity in Decision-Making through Behaviorally-Grounded Value Alignment

author.name: Seojin Hwang, Minju Kim, Junhyuk Choi, JeongHyun Park, Hwanhee Lee

entry.summary: This work introduces Fragile, a benchmark isolating fact-preserving semantic framing across value-tinted narration, temporal slice, and narrative vividness in high-stakes decision-making, revealing a 28.6% average decision flip rate in LLMs. It finds simple prompt and activation interventions fail to suppress framing sensitivity.

entry.title: When Helpful Context Leaks: Privacy Risks in Domain-Adapted ASR

author.name: Maike Z\"ufle, Jan Niehues

entry.summary: This paper identifies a privacy risk in domain-adapted ASR where a model customized for domain terminology can be nudged into transcribing a phonetically similar context or training-data word instead of what was actually spoken, leaking private information. It measures leakage across prompting and fine-tuning customization mechanisms.

entry.title: On Compositional Learning Behaviours in Formal Mathematics

author.name: Kevin Yandoka Denamgana\"i

entry.summary: This paper adapts the Symbolic Behaviour Benchmark to study compositional learning behaviors in formal mathematics, removing numerical confounds and adding chain-of-thought scaffolding. It cross-evaluates ten Lean 4 theorem provers, finding a hierarchical necessity structure between search and compositional competency.

entry.title: GraphLit: Learning Text-Enriched Dynamic Character Network Representations for Literary Study

author.name: Gaspard Michel, Elena V. Epure, Romain Hennequin, Christophe Cerisara, Mirella Lapata

entry.summary: GraphLit introduces Dynamic Heterogeneous Character Networks aligning characters with textual context in novels, learned via a masked graph autoencoder. It improves over text-only and graph-only baselines across 12 character-related literary tasks.

entry.title: Human Label Variation as Stable Signal: Learning Annotator-Specific Explanation Behavior via Cross-Annotator Preference Optimization

author.name: Beiduo Chen, Pingjun Hong, Ziyun Zhang, Benjamin Roth, Anna Korhonen, Barbara Plank

entry.summary: This work studies whether LLMs can learn annotator-specific label and explanation behavior, finding individual patterns are weak per-annotation but detectable after content reduction and aggregation. It proposes cross-annotator preference optimization to capture human label variation.

entry.title: Asynchronous Remote Sensing Time-Series Fusion for Cloud Removal and Anytime Reconstruction

author.name: Forouzan Fallah, Chia Yu Hsu, Wenwen Li, Anna Liljedahl, Yezhou Yang

entry.summary: AGFlow is a spatiotemporal flow-matching model for Sentinel-1/Sentinel-2 fusion enabling cloud removal and anytime reconstruction from irregular asynchronous acquisitions. It supports timestamp-conditioned internal alignment and on-demand synthesis under long gaps.

entry.title: Self-Prophetic Decoding to Unlock Visual Search in LVLMs

author.name: Zhendong He, Qiyuan Dai, Guanbin Li, Liang Lin, Sibei Yang

entry.summary: This paper proposes self-prophetic decoding to unlock visual search in large vision-language models, leveraging self-regulation between pre- and post-trained models to mitigate capability deterioration and long-context interference. It uses probability-based prophetic sampling instead of naive prompting.

entry.title: GE-Sim 2.0: A Roadmap Towards Comprehensive Closed-loop Video World Simulators for Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Boxiang Qiu, Liliang Chen, Yue Liao, Nan Wang, Lintao Wang, Jiayi Luo, Wenzhi Zhao, Shengcong Chen, Di Chen, Ye Li, Chen Gao, Shuicheng Yan, Si Liu, Maoqing Yao, Guanghui Ren

entry.summary: This deployment case study at a Siemens factory examines adapting a pretrained Pi0.5 VLA policy to a real industrial packaging task through iterative fine-tuning and deployment-driven refinement. It documents the workflow, failures, and lessons of moving VLA pipelines to the factory floor.

entry.title: Eval Cooperativeness May Be a Scalable Mitigation for Eval Gaming

author.name: Jasmine Li

entry.summary: Proposes eval cooperativeness, instilling in models a situational desire to help developers acquire the information evaluations seek, as a more scalable mitigation for eval gaming than reducing eval awareness in misaligned models. It argues this preserves the predictive value of behavioral evaluations.

entry.title: Eval Cooperativeness May Be a Scalable Mitigation for Eval Gaming

author.name: Jasmine Li

entry.summary: Cross-posting on the AI Alignment Forum of the eval cooperativeness proposal, suggesting models be trained with a situational desire to help developers obtain the information evaluations seek as a scalable mitigation for eval gaming. It argues this is more robust than trying to reduce eval awareness.

entry.title: DeepSciVerify: Verifying Scientific Claim--Citation Alignment via LLM-Driven Evidence Escalation

author.name: Shaghayegh Sadeghi, Khashayar Khajavi, Rise Adhikari, Alexander Tessier

entry.summary: Presents DeepSciVerify, a two-stage pipeline verifying scientific claim-citation alignment by reasoning over abstracts first and escalating to full-text passages only for uncertain cases. It achieves 86.7 Micro-F1 on the SCitance benchmark by leveraging complementary LLM behaviors.

entry.title: SkillGrad: Optimizing Agent Skills Like Gradient Descent

author.name: Hanyu Wang, Yifan Lan, Bochuan Cao, Lu Lin, Jinghui Chen

entry.summary: Proposes SkillGrad, a gradient-descent-inspired framework that optimizes agent skill packages by treating them as structured parameters, using trajectory-level loss and text-based gradients from automatic diagnoses. It improves the reliability of reusable procedural skills for LLM agents.

entry.title: Towards Faithful Agentic XAI: A Verification Method and an Open-World Benchmark for Better Model Faithfulness

author.name: Jaechang Kim, Sunung Mun, Seungjoon Lee, Jaewoong Cho, Jungseul Ok

entry.summary: Proposes FAX, a framework improving agentic explainable-AI faithfulness by decomposing draft explanations into claims and cross-checking them against inherently faithful tools to filter unsupported claims, plus a CRAFTER-XAI-Bench benchmark. It addresses the risk of LLMs amplifying unfaithful explanations.

entry.title: SKILLC: Learning Autonomous Skill Internalization in LLM Agents via Contrastive Credit Assignment

author.name: Hongxiang Lin, Zhirui Kuai, Erpeng Xue, Lei Wang

entry.summary: Proposes SkillC with Contrastive Skill Credit Assignment, which converts skill-helpfulness contrast into a direct learning signal by sampling paired skill-injected and skill-free rollouts to distinguish skill-dependent from autonomous success. It improves skill internalization in long-horizon agentic RL.

entry.title: The Shape of Overthinking: Backtracking Bursts in Long Reasoning Traces

author.name: Navid Rezazadeh, Arash Gholami Davoodi

entry.summary: Analyzes backtracking dynamics in long reasoning traces, annotating 6,000 Qwen3-8B AIME traces to distinguish productive self-correction from unproductive revision, finding incorrect traces show moderate-to-severe backtracks that cluster late. It uses backtrack patterns as a reliability signal.

entry.title: Confidence-Orchestrated Self-Evolution against Uncertain LLM Feedback

author.name: Bowen Wei, Nan Wang, Yuqing Zhou, Jinhao Pan, Ziwei Zhu

entry.summary: Proposes COSE, which uses an LLM's intrinsic confidence as an uncertainty signal to modulate self-evolution learning via confidence-weighted PPO updates and confidence-prior mechanisms, mitigating erroneous self-judgments becoming bad gradients. It improves self-evolving training without external verifiers.

entry.title: Examining Agents' Bias Amplification versus Suppression in Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Zejian Eric Wu, Zhongyi Jiang, Yuan Zhuang, Paul Jen-Hwa Hu

entry.summary: Examines whether multi-agent systems amplify or suppress group-favoring biases, proposing the zero-centered Favor Bias Strength metric that decomposes bias change into favored-group uplift and disfavored-group suppression. It analyzes system-wide fairness consequences of agent-level biases.

entry.title: Defending LLM-based Multi-Agent Systems Against Cooperative Attacks with Sentence-Level Rectification

author.name: Yaoyang Luo, Zhi Zheng, Ziwei Zhao, Tong Xu, Zhao Jielun, Wenjun Xue, Yong Chen, Enhong Chen

entry.summary: This paper introduces a cooperative attack framework where malicious agents in LLM multi-agent systems coordinate to inject misinformation, then proposes a sentence-level rectification defense. It matters because real-world multi-agent deployments are vulnerable to colluding adversaries that prior independent-attacker assumptions miss.

entry.title: When Does Memory Help Multi-Trajectory Inference for Tool-Use LLM Agents?

author.name: Xinzhe Li, Yaguang Tao

entry.summary: This paper proposes a unified framework decomposing cross-trajectory memory for tool-use agents along scope and abstraction axes, clarifying when memory actually helps multi-trajectory inference. It disentangles memory effects from inference-strategy effects that prior single-setting evaluations conflated.

entry.title: Tree of Thoughts as a Classical Heuristic Search Problem: Formal Foundations and Design Patterns

author.name: Guni Sharon

entry.summary: This paper unifies fragmented Tree-of-Thoughts research under a classical heuristic search taxonomy, mapping LLM reasoning components to search elements and synthesizing design patterns. It bridges NLP and automated planning communities with consistent terminology.

entry.title: Unlocking Fine-Grained and Within-Utterance Speaking Style Control in Prompt-Based Text-to-Speech Models

author.name: Jaehoon Kang, Yejin Lee, Yoonji Park, Kyuhong Shim

entry.summary: This work adds fine-grained, within-utterance speaking style control to prompt-based TTS using direction vectors between contrastive style prompts for inter-utterance interpolation and time-varying intra-utterance transitions. It expands the controllability of natural-language-driven speech synthesis.

entry.title: STARS: Spike Tail-Aware Relational Synthesis for ANN-to-SNN Data-Free Knowledge Distillation

author.name: Shuhan Ye, Yi Yu, Qixin Zhang, Hui Lu, Jiaming He, Qinggang Zhang, Li Shen, Xudong Jiang

entry.summary: STARS is a plug-and-play data-free knowledge distillation method for ANN-to-SNN transfer that augments BN-guided synthesis with spike-tail-aware relational constraints, better matching SNN threshold-crossing dynamics. It addresses the under-constraint of ANN-oriented synthesis for SNN students.

entry.title: RE-TRIANGLE: Does TRIANGLE Enable Multimodal Alignment Beyond Cosine Similarity in Retrieval?

author.name: Arijit Ghosh, Aritra Bandyopadhyay, Chiranjeev Bindra, Jingfen Qiao

entry.summary: This reproducibility study evaluates the TRIANGLE framework, which minimizes modality-triplet area on a hypersphere to enforce multimodal alignment beyond pairwise cosine similarity. It confirms zero-shot retrieval gains up to +8.7 Recall@1 but fails to reproduce some claims.

entry.title: HEAL: Resilient and Self-* Hub-based Learning

author.name: Mohamed Amine Legheraba (NPA), Stefan Galkiewicz (NPA), Maria Gradinariu Potop-Butucaru (NPA), S\'ebastien Tixeuil (NPA, IUF, LINCS)

entry.summary: HEAL is a cross-layer decentralized learning framework using an optimized self-organizing, self-healing hub-based topology to overcome the single-point-of-failure of federated learning while converging faster than gossip-based approaches. It aims for resilience, privacy, and scalability.

entry.title: CiteCheck: Retrieval-Grounded Detection of LLM Citation Hallucinations in Scientific Text

author.name: Khashayar Khajavi, Shaghayegh Sadeghi, Rise Adhikari, Alexander Tessier

entry.summary: CiteCheck is a retrieval-grounded framework for detecting LLM citation hallucinations, verifying whether a cited work exists and whether its metadata is faithful. It includes a 982-citation physics benchmark with controlled corruptions and a structured LLM verifier.

entry.title: Can Segmentation Models Understand the World? Towards Proactive Affordance Reasoning via Visual Chain-of-Thought

author.name: Yuchen Guo, Junli Gong, Hongmin Cai, Yiu-ming Cheung, Weifeng Su

entry.summary: SegWorld introduces proactive affordance reasoning where a segmentation model observes a scene via multi-level visual chain-of-thought before committing to a mask, handling intent-level instructions that don't name the target region. It bridges the gap between target-referential segmentation and embodied intent understanding.

entry.title: Residualized Temporal Sparse Autoencoders for Interpreting Diffusion Models

author.name: Calvin Yeung, Prathyush Poduval, Ali Zakeri, Zhuowen Zou, Mohsen Imani

entry.summary: This work introduces residualized temporal sparse autoencoders for interpreting diffusion model activation trajectories, learning from full denoising trajectories via linear predictors between timesteps and residual representations. It improves interpretability of how diffusion features evolve over time rather than at single timesteps.

entry.title: DecomposeRL: Learning to Ask Useful, Informative, and Diverse Questions for Semi-Supervised, Traceable Claim Verification

author.name: Shubhashis Roy Dipta, Ankur Padia, Francis Ferraro

entry.summary: DecomposeRL frames claim decomposition as an RL policy trained with GRPO and a multi-faceted reward ensemble, producing accurate yet inspectable verification traces. It uses a data-curation funnel distilling 115K claims into a learning-dense 5K subset for cost-efficient training.

entry.title: Let the Results Speak: A Replication-First Paradigm for LLM Behavioral Benchmarking

author.name: Yuming (Rapheal), Huang, Yao Liu, Lei Wang, Junchen Wan
