entry.summary: This paper proposes a replication-first paradigm for subjective LLM behavioral benchmarking, certifying instruments via reliability across runs, cross-instrument replication across distinct judges, historical-footprint calibration, and pre-registration. It addresses the circularity risk of single LLM-as-judge evaluations of qualities like empathy and restraint.

entry.title: Semantic Flow Regularization: Teaching LLMs to Generate Diverse Yet Coherent Responses

author.name: Kerui Peng, Feifei Li, Xingyu Fan, Wenhui Que

entry.summary: Semantic Flow Regularization combats Cross-Style Collapse in persona/tone-conditioned LLMs by supervising the backbone with continuous future-segment embeddings via conditional flow matching, preserving multi-modality. The flow-matching head is discarded at inference for zero deployment cost.

entry.title: SPARD: Defending Harmful Fine-Tuning Attack via Safety Projection with Relevance-Diversity Data Selection

author.name: Shuhao Chen, Weisen Jiang, Yeqi Gong, Shengda Luo, Chengxiang Zhuo, Zang Li, James T. Kwok, Yu Zhang

entry.summary: SPARD defends against harmful fine-tuning attacks via safety-projected alternating optimization (alternating utility updates and explicit safety projections) plus a relevance-diversity determinantal point process for selecting compact safe data. It preserves safety alignment under adversarial fine-tuning on GSM8K and OpenBookQA.

entry.title: BenGER: Benchmarking LLM Systems on Subsumption-Based Legal Reasoning in German Law

author.name: Sebastian Nagl, Ann-Kristin Mayrhofer, Martin Heidebach, Aleyna Ko\c{c}ak, Anne Zettelmeier, Elly Breu, Angelina Greiner, Sofija Milijas, Matthias Grabmair

entry.summary: BenGER is a benchmark for evaluating LLM systems on subsumption-based legal reasoning in German law, comprising exam-style case tasks and doctrinal reasoning tasks with human baselines and a rubric-aligned LLM-as-judge framework. It enables rigorous contextualization of model performance against timed human-written legal solutions.

entry.title: Hybrid Neural World Models

author.name: Pranav Lakshmanan, Paras Chopra

entry.summary: Hybrid Neural World Models train multi-horizon physical-dynamics surrogates with continuous horizon conditioning supervised against reference solvers, predicting any future state in one forward pass. Notably, the trained surrogate implicitly encodes sharp dynamical events like shocks recoverable as per-trajectory error maps despite no explicit supervision for them.

entry.title: ADWIN: Adaptive Windows for Horizon-Aware On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Kun Liang, Chenming Tang, Clive Bai, Weijie Liu, Saiyong Yang, Yunfang Wu

entry.summary: ADWIN is an adaptive-window framework for on-policy distillation that trains students on short teacher-anchored prefixes rather than full rollouts, using delayed full-rollout probes to audit the useful supervision horizon. It reduces costly completions while preserving long-horizon update direction.

entry.title: The Cases LJP Never Sees: Prosecution Decision Prediction for More Complete Criminal Liability Assessment

author.name: Junyu Lu, Qi Wei, Peishuo Zheng, Jie Zhang, Hui Huang, Qianru Wang, Chuan Xiao, Jianbin Qin, Shuyuan Zheng

entry.summary: This work introduces Prosecution Decision Prediction, a legal AI task built around prosecutorial review that classifies cases as prosecution or one of three non-prosecution decisions, filling a blind spot left by Legal Judgment Prediction which only sees indicted cases. It enables more complete criminal liability assessment including evidence evaluation and value-based discretion.

entry.title: Learn from Weaknesses: Automated Domain Specialization for Small Computer-Use Agents

author.name: Suji Kim, Kangsan Kim, Sung Ju Hwang

entry.summary: LearnWeak is an annotation-free specialization framework for small computer-use agents that uses a stronger reference agent to identify the student's domain-specific weaknesses, synthesize targeted tasks, and construct supervision automatically. It targets practical, cheaper specialization than deploying a large expert per software domain.

entry.title: Gradient Transformer: Learning to Generate Updates for LLMs

author.name: Binh-Nguyen Nguyen, Khang Tran, NhatHai Phan, Issa Khalil

entry.summary: The Gradient Transformer learns to map fine-tuning update vectors from small TinyLMs into update vectors for large LLMs in a data-free knowledge distillation setting, enabling private-data adaptation without LLM fine-tuning. This targets resource-constrained organizations unable to fine-tune large models.

entry.title: BPPO: Binary Prefix Policy Optimization for Efficient GRPO-Style Reasoning RL with Concise Responses

author.name: Qingfei Zhao, Huan Song, Shuyu Tian, Jiawei Shao, Xuelong Li

entry.summary: BPPO improves GRPO-style reasoning RL efficiency by using only the shortest correct and shortest incorrect completions per prompt group as a compact contrastive update unit, motivated by gradient-similarity analysis showing same-class completions give redundant signals. This reduces cost and curbs verbose reasoning.

entry.title: Long Live The Balance: Information Bottleneck Driven Tree-based Policy Optimization

author.name: Hao Jiang, Shurui Li, Tianpeng Bu, Bowen Xu, Xin Liu, Qihua Chen, Hongtao Duan, Lulu Hu, Bin Yang, Minying Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces IB-Score, an Information Bottleneck-based metric quantifying the exploration-exploitation balance in LLM RL by trading off step-level reasoning diversity against mutual information with correct answers. It shows popular methods like GRPO fail to maintain balance and proposes a tree-based policy optimization to address it.

entry.title: Joint Training of Multi-Token Prediction in Reinforcement Learning via Optimal Coefficient Calibration

author.name: Zili Wang, Jiajun Chai, Lin Chen, Xiaohan Wang, Shiming Xiang, Guojun Yin

entry.summary: Revisits why multi-token prediction harms RLVR when jointly trained, decomposing MTP's per-step RL effect into a first-order correlation and second-order perturbation penalty, unifying detach/cross-entropy/policy regimes. It proposes optimal coefficient calibration to enable beneficial joint MTP-RL training.

entry.title: Semi-Supervised Hypothesis Testing by Betting on Predictions

author.name: Yaniv Tenzer, Elad Tolochinsky, Yaniv Romano

entry.summary: Introduces a testing-by-betting framework that uses predictions on unlabeled data to enhance the power of sequential hypothesis testing, with anytime-valid guarantees under label or concept shift. It constructs an e-statistic that remains valid even with imperfect predictors.

entry.title: Optimal Data Acquisition for Reinforcement Learning: A Large Deviations Perspective

author.name: Mingjie Hu, Jian-Qiang Hu, Enlu Zhou

entry.summary: Develops a large deviations framework for optimal data acquisition in infinite-horizon reinforcement learning, using the exponential decay rate of policy-selection error as an efficiency metric. It derives a variational characterization yielding a nested optimization problem.

entry.title: Automating Formal Verification with Agent-Guided Tree Search

author.name: Leo Yao

entry.summary: A thesis evaluating LLM-driven verified-code generation (vericoding) in Lean and developing agent-guided tree search methods to improve verification performance. It reproduces benchmark results and analyzes open versus closed model performance trends.

entry.title: Machine learning enables experimental access to photon-by-photon arrival times in scintillation detectors

author.name: Yuya Onishi, Ryosuke Ota, Fumio Hashimoto, Kibo Ote, Go Akamatsu, Hideaki Tashima, Taiga Yamaya

entry.summary: Uses deep learning to enable experimental access to photon-by-photon arrival times in scintillation detectors, overcoming a fundamental structural limitation of photodetectors. This improves timing resolution relevant to PET imaging for cancer and dementia diagnosis.

entry.title: ProgVLA: Progress-Aware Robot Manipulation Skill Learning

author.name: Seungsu Kim, Jinyoung Choi, Seungmin Baek, Jean-Michel Renders

entry.summary: ProgVLA is a compact vision-language-action model for robot manipulation that uses Perceiver-based token compression and progress-tracking heads trained with offline RL to handle long horizons under tight compute budgets. It targets reliable on-device robot control.

entry.title: Bias Leaves a Gradient Trail: Label-Free Bias Identification via Gradient Probes on Concept Decompositions

author.name: Thomas Vitry, Kieran Edgeworth, Stefan Wermter, Jae Hee Lee

entry.summary: This paper presents a bias-label-free post-hoc method to identify spurious concepts in frozen vision models using non-negative matrix factorization of activations and gradient probes, requiring only standard class labels. It enables bias discovery without curated group annotations or retraining.

entry.title: Playing with Words, Improving with Rewards: Training Language Models for Creative Association

author.name: Vijeta Deshpande, Namrata Shivagunde, Sherin Muckatira, Hadrien Glaude, Mikhail Gronas, Claire Stevenson, Roger Beaty, Anna Rumshisky

entry.summary: This work trains LLMs on the word-association game Codenames using RLVR to exercise divergent and convergent thinking with verifiable outcomes, bypassing subjective human judgment of creativity. It trains Qwen3 models and evaluates across creativity and reasoning benchmarks.

entry.title: The Missing Piece in Pre-trained Model Evaluation: Reward-Guided Decoding Unlocks Task-Oriented Behavior Without Parameter Updates

author.name: Shaobo Wang, Guo Chen, Ziyue Wang, Zhengyang Tang, Qingyang Liu, Xingzhang Ren, Dayiheng Liu, Linfeng Zhang

entry.summary: This paper proposes Energy-Based Decoding, a reward-guided decoding method that unlocks task-oriented behavior in base pretrained LLMs without parameter updates, addressing how standard decoding conflates capability with formatting failures. It enables fairer evaluation of base model capabilities.

entry.title: Ask Now, Use Later: Benchmarking the Proactivity Gap in Long-Lived LLM Agents

author.name: Bin Wu, Guanyun Zou, Bingbing Wang, Huan Zhao, Chuan Shi

entry.summary: This paper introduces Ask-to-Remember, benchmarking the proactivity gap in long-lived LLM agents that keep volunteered preferences but rarely ask for unspoken ones needed in later sessions. It isolates whether an agent decides to proactively ask for reusable preferences not needed for the current task.

entry.title: The Harder Text Embedding Benchmark (HTEB): Beyond One-dimensional Static Robustness

author.name: Manuel Frank, Haithem Afli

entry.summary: HTEB is a dynamic text embedding benchmark that challenges robustness along lexical/stylistic, length, and language axes by stochastically transforming inputs at evaluation time with an LLM, arguing robustness is multidimensional rather than scalar. It evaluates 16 embedding models across 42 languages with human validation.

entry.title: HardMTBench: Stress-Testing Chinese-English Translation on Knowledge-Intensive Domains

author.name: Zheng Li, Mao Zheng, Mingyang Song, Tianxiang Fei

entry.summary: HardMTBench is a difficulty-aware diagnostic benchmark for Chinese-English translation across 12 knowledge-intensive domains, addressing saturation of benchmarks like FLORES-200. It contains 10,000 hand-curated sentences across finance, healthcare, law, and science.

entry.title: Roles with Rails: Contract-Preserving Role Evolution in Multi-Agent Structured Reasoning

author.name: Ling-Yue Ge, Lan-Zhe Guo

entry.summary: This work formalizes contract-preserving role evolution in multi-agent LLM systems, requiring every role edit to maintain five structural contracts. The SERO system enables adaptive role pools without breaking answer aggregation or output protocols.

entry.title: ForestHG-Trace: Traceable Long-Horizon Ecological Reasoning over Large-Scale Forest Scenes

author.name: Zihang Cheng, Duanchu Wang, Cheng Li, Jing Huang, Huanzhao Fu, Di Wang

entry.summary: ForestHG-Trace enables traceable long-horizon ecological reasoning over forest scenes by representing multimodal NEON data as ecological hypergraphs and using an LLM-guided agent with deterministic tools. It produces replayable execution traces with verifiable evidence.

entry.title: Janus-LoRA: A Balanced Low-Rank Adaptation for Continual Learning

author.name: Cheng Chen, Pengpeng Zeng, Yuyu Guo, Lianli Gao, Hengtao Shen, Jingkuan Song

entry.summary: Janus-LoRA addresses catastrophic forgetting in continual learning by identifying that LoRA's composite low-rank update systematically violates orthogonality to prior task subspaces. It restores the stability-plasticity balance while avoiding the plasticity loss of naive orthogonality enforcement.

entry.title: SeeGroup: Multi-Layer Depth Estimation of Transparent Surfaces via Self-Determined Grouping

author.name: Hongyu Wen, Jia Deng

entry.summary: SeeGroup performs multi-layer depth estimation of transparent surfaces by letting the model adaptively assign surfaces to depth maps via a point process, rather than imposing a predefined front-to-back grouping. This addresses the ambiguity of layered geometry groupings.

entry.title: Tabero: Learning Gentle Manipulation with Closed-Loop Force Feedback from Vision, Touch, and Language

author.name: Qiwei Wu, Rui Zhang, Xin Xiang, Tao Li, Weihua Zhang, Junjie Lai, Renjing Xu

entry.summary: Tabero is a benchmark and model suite for gentle, language-conditioned robotic manipulation requiring fine-grained contact force perception via closed-loop force feedback from vision, touch, and language. It introduces a data-efficient pipeline repurposing open-source trajectories into vision-tactile-language tasks.

entry.title: Full automation of AI R&D probably yields a large speed up even without a software-only singularity

author.name: ryan_greenblatt

entry.summary: Argues that even without a software-only singularity (where r exceeds 1 sustainably), full automation of AI R&D would still produce a large speedup via a one-time automation boost, using parameterized intelligence-explosion modeling. It quantifies effects under sub-critical parameters like r=0.7.

entry.title: Full automation of AI R&D probably yields a large speed up even without a software-only singularity

author.name: ryan_greenblatt

entry.summary: Alignment Forum cross-post arguing that full automation of AI R&D yields a large speedup even absent a software-only singularity, via a one-time automation boost modeled with parameterized takeoff dynamics. It quantifies the effect under sub-critical r values.

entry.title: Prefix-Safe Bayesian Belief Tracking for LLM Reasoning Reliability:Separating Calibration from Ranking

author.name: Zhenghan Song, Yunyi Li, Yulong Liu

entry.summary: Introduces Sequential Bayesian Belief Tracking for estimating eventual reasoning success from prefix-safe observations during long reasoning traces, separating calibration quality from ranking quality. It shows that score-only tracking improves calibration while ranking gains require structure-aware evidence.

entry.title: A Fixed-Budget, Cluster-Aware Standard for LLM-as-a-Judge Evaluation: A Multi-Hop RAG Stress Test

author.name: Camilo Chac\'on Sartori, Jos\'e H. Garc\'ia

entry.summary: Proposes a minimum measurement standard for LLM-as-a-judge comparisons in multi-hop RAG, fixing candidate pools, evidence budgets, and prompts while requiring pre-registered hypotheses, cluster-aware inference, and second-judge replication. It aims to make RAG evaluations reproducible and statistically sound.

entry.title: From Talking to Singing: A New Challenge for Audio-Visual Deepfake Detection

author.name: Ke Liu, Jiwei Wei, Wenyu Zhang, Shuchang Zhou, Ruikun Chai, Yutao Dai, Chaoning Zhang, Yang Yang

entry.summary: Constructs the Singing Head DeepFake dataset and proposes T-AVFD, a text-guided audio-visual forgery detection framework that generalizes across talking and singing where rhythmic vocalization weakens cross-modal coupling. It addresses a domain shift that degrades existing deepfake detectors.

entry.title: CIVIC: End-to-End Sequence Compactness for Efficient Vision-Language Models

author.name: Fengze Yang, Bo Yu, Xuewen Luo, Cathy Liu, Chenxi Liu

entry.summary: CIVIC presents a path-consistent compact visual inference framework that maintains compressed sequence representations across the full VLM pipeline to achieve real wall-clock speedups, not just FLOP savings. It matters for deploying vision-language models under memory and latency constraints.

entry.title: Bandwidth-Efficient and Privacy-Preserving Edge-Cloud Many-to-Many Speech Translation

author.name: Yexing Du, Kaiyuan Liu, Youcheng Pan, Bo Yang, Ming Liu, Bing Qin, Yang Xiang

entry.summary: ESRT is a privacy-preserving, bandwidth-efficient edge-cloud framework for many-to-many speech translation that splits inference by keeping a lightweight speech encoder and adapter on-device to avoid transmitting raw voice data. It also addresses English-centric biases for many-to-many scaling.

entry.title: Personalized Observation Normalization for Federated Reinforcement Learning in Simulation Environments with Heterogeneity

author.name: Yiran Pang, Zhen Ni, Xiangnan Zhong

entry.summary: This paper proposes Personalized Observation Normalization (PON) for federated reinforcement learning in heterogeneous environments, letting each agent locally normalize state inputs to prevent imbalanced aggregation. It addresses non-identical input distributions across agents.

entry.title: Ocean4Rec: Offline LLM-Derived OCEAN Profiles for Request-Time VOD Reranking

author.name: Wonkyun Kim, Sehyun Bae, Kwanki Ahn, Mungyu Bae, Saeun Choi, Soyeon You, Chandra Prabhakar, Sehyun Kim

entry.summary: Ocean4Rec uses an LLM offline to materialize OCEAN personality profiles from VOD content metadata, mapping items to Big Five trait scores and building time-decayed user profiles for request-time reranking. It avoids costly per-request LLM invocation in latency-sensitive recommenders.

entry.title: Architecture-driven Shift: towards a lightweight selector for capturing the trends of logit shift

author.name: Zhong Ye, Yu Hu, Ruilin Tang

entry.summary: This work proposes a lightweight selector for predicting logit shift trends to enable efficient pre-trained model selection for continual learning, addressing the high cost of computing logit shifts directly. It accounts for structural heterogeneity in real architectures with variable width and depth.

entry.title: Clinical Validation of the Melanoscope AI Mobile Dermoscopy Clinical Decision Support System

author.name: Elena Sergeevna Kozachok, Sergey Sergeevich Seregin

entry.summary: This work develops a quantitative interpretability assessment method for cascade deep learning models and a three-zone patient routing algorithm, with preliminary single-center prospective clinical validation of the Melanoscope AI mobile dermoscopy decision support system. It targets early skin cancer detection amid dermatologist shortages.

entry.title: Reading or Guessing? Visual Grounding Failures of Vision-Language Models for OCR in Ancient Greek Editions

author.name: Antonia Karamolegkou, Nicolas Angleraud, Beno\^it Sagot, Thibault Cl\'erice

entry.summary: This study shows that vision-language models used for OCR of Ancient Greek critical editions often produce fluent but visually unsupported text, relying on language priors. Using image perturbations and token-level grounding measures, it demonstrates VLMs diverge from ground truth where traditional OCR engines produce local recognition noise.

entry.title: SPAR: Support-Preserving Action Rectification

author.name: Jiaxin Zhao, Weihang Pan, Xun Liang, Binbin Lin

entry.summary: SPAR reframes offline policy improvement as local residual rectification anchored to a frozen behavior-cloning policy, performing fine-grained fitting in residual space to resolve the conflict between value maximization and staying on the data manifold. It contracts the search space to mitigate over-conservatism and off-manifold drift.

entry.title: Periodic RoPE for Infinite Context LLMs

author.name: Simin Huo

entry.summary: Periodic RoPE (P-RoPE) addresses position exhaustion in ultra-long-context LLMs by combining a periodic positional encoding with sliding window attention for local layers and NoPE-style global attention layers. It aims to enable truly infinite context beyond the pre-trained positional range.

entry.title: VCap: Hypergeometric Rewards for Weak-to-Strong Visual Captioning

author.name: Xingyu Lu, Jinpeng Wang, Yi-Fan Zhang, Yankai Yang, Yancheng Long, Yiyang Fan, Xuanyu Zheng, Haonan Fan, Kaiyu Jiang, Tianke Zhang, Changyi Liu, Bin Wen, Fan Yang, Tingting Gao, Han Li, Chun Yuan

entry.summary: VCap is a Witness-Adjudicator reward for RL-based visual captioning that pairs the reference caption (witness) with the visual signal (adjudicator) to verify factual consistency, providing fine-grained reward signals. It reduces both omission and hallucination in weak-to-strong captioning.

entry.title: Whose Name Comes Up? III: Persona Prompting Effects in LLM-Based Scholar Recommendation

author.name: Annabella S\'anchez-Guzm\'an, Lukas Eberhard, Denis Helic, Lisette Esp\'in-Noboa

entry.summary: This audit examines how persona prompts (language, location, role) and context affect LLM-based scholar recommendations across 43 models and six disciplines, comparing outputs to Semantic Scholar for quality and representativeness. It finds technical quality is driven by model choice while social representativeness varies with prompting.

entry.title: VITAL: Visual-Semantic Dual Supervision for Enhanced and Interpretable Latent Reasoning in Medical MLLMs

author.name: Qiaoru Li, Shaotian Liang, Jintao Chen, Haoran Sun, Yuxiang Cai, Jianwei Yin, Yankai Jiang

entry.summary: VITAL is a latent-space reasoning framework for medical multimodal LLMs using visual-semantic dual supervision: a text decoder reconstructs reasoning chains and a visual projector regresses ROI features, both discarded at inference. It addresses modality collapse, weak visual supervision, and interpretability needs in clinical VQA.

entry.title: Efficient and Scalable Provenance Tracking for LLM-Generated Code Snippets

author.name: Andrea Gurioli, Davide D'Ascenzo, Federico Pennino, Maurizio Gabbrielli, Stefano Zacchiroli

entry.summary: SOURCETRACKER is a 300M-parameter encoder plus a hybrid two-stage pipeline for efficient, scalable provenance tracking of LLM-generated code, addressing verbatim reproduction of training data and license/plagiarism concerns at billion-scale corpora. It overcomes the impracticality of linear-time fingerprint search.

entry.title: Sense Representations Are Inducible Interfaces

author.name: Jan Christian Blaise Cruz, Alham Fikri Aji

entry.summary: ACROS induces an explicit sense pathway (per-token meaning decompositions) into a frozen pretrained decoder LM via a gated residual addition, without requiring pretraining with sense structure. It supports zero-shot word-sense disambiguation, low-KL lexical steering, and cross-lingual adaptation using the same induced variables.

entry.title: A Paired Testing Protocol for Batch-Conditioned Refusal Robustness in LLM Serving

author.name: Sahil Kadadekar

entry.summary: Introduces a paired testing protocol revealing that batch serving configuration (solo, synchronized batch, continuous batching) is an untested treatment variable affecting LLM safety behavior. Finds safety-label changes more frequently than capability changes across batch conditions, with adjudication confirming genuine cases.

entry.title: Continual Learning in Modern Hopfield Networks with an Application to Diffusion Models

author.name: Ken Takeda, Masafumi Oizumi, Ryo Karakida

entry.summary: Analyzes continual learning in modern Hopfield networks and transfers the analysis to diffusion models via known MHN-diffusion links, introducing intrinsic forgetting as Hopfield energy increase after task changes. It proves high-energy samples are most easily forgotten and should be prioritized for replay.

entry.title: Unification and Optimization of Robust Supervised Learning

author.name: Jonas Hanselle, Valentin Margraf, Clemens Damke, Eyke H\"ullermeier

entry.summary: Unifies a broad class of robust supervised learning methods (distributionally robust optimization, label smoothing, vicinal risk minimization, Mixup) along three design axes and derives a tractable staged training procedure. This lets practitioners avoid committing a priori to a single failure mode.

entry.title: Outer-Momentum Restarting in High-Dimensional Two-Phase Optimization

author.name: Kristi Topollai, Allan Ma, Tolga Dimlioglu, Sui Jiet Tay, Anna Choromanska

entry.summary: Studies periodic restarting of outer momentum in communication-efficient distributed optimizers like DiLoCo, deriving mode-wise restart contraction in a linearized NTK model. It offers a complementary mechanism for controlling outer-loop memory in two-phase distributed training.

entry.title: Probabilistic Data-Driven Modelling of Astrophysical Transients: The Neural Process Family for Ultrafast and Class-Agnostic Light Curve Reconstruction with NightLANP

author.name: Siddharth Chaini, Federica B. Bianco, Ashish Mahabal

entry.summary: Introduces NightLANP, applying the neural process family to ultrafast, class-agnostic light curve reconstruction for astrophysical transients ahead of the Rubin Observatory survey. It overcomes Gaussian process limitations in cross-band correlation and scalability.

entry.title: Robust Moment-Based Estimation via Spectral Gradient Reweighting

author.name: Liu Zhang, Amit Singer

entry.summary: Proposes the SGR-GMM algorithm, a robust generalized method of moments procedure using spectral gradient reweighting to soft-reweight per-observation gradients against outliers. The analysis formulates the primitive as an entropy-regularized spectral game.

entry.title: Latent-Conditioned Parameterized Quantum Circuits as Universal Approximators for Distributions over Quantum States

author.name: Quoc Hoan Tran, Koki Chinzei, Yasuhiro Endo, Hirotaka Oshima

entry.summary: This work introduces latent-conditioned parameterized quantum circuits, a hybrid framework where classical neural networks map latent variables to quantum circuit parameters, and proves they are universal approximators for distributions over quantum states. It enables generative modeling of quantum state ensembles.

entry.title: Keyphrase Generative Representation of Youth Crisis Conversations Beyond Static Taxonomies

author.name: Abeer Badawi, Will Aitken, Lydia Sequeira, Jocelyn Rankin, Maia Norman, Elham Dolatabadi

entry.summary: This work analyzes over 700,000 youth crisis text conversations, expanding a 19-label taxonomy to 39 hierarchical labels and introducing Keyphrase Generative Representation, a constrained LLM that produces conversation-specific keyphrases beyond static taxonomies. It achieves expert-validated reliability for mental health concern identification.

entry.title: Beyond Chunk-Local Extraction: Cross-Chunk Graph Augmentation for GraphRAG

author.name: Jiaming Zhang, Yibo Zhao, Jing Yu, Jianxiang Yu, Xiang Li

entry.summary: CrossAug is a GNN-guided cross-chunk graph augmentation method that enriches GraphRAG indices with relational structure spanning multiple passages, addressing the systematic absence of cross-chunk relations. It uses self-supervised graph corruption to derive training supervision as an offline step.

entry.title: SuperValid: Capability-Aligned OOD Validation for Generalizable Downstream Scaling

author.name: Quanen Sun, Changxin Tian, Ke Shi, Cai Chen, Cunyin Peng, Jia Liu, Kunlong Chen, Zhiqiang Zhang

entry.summary: SuperValid proposes studying downstream scaling at the capability level rather than benchmark level, synthesizing out-of-distribution capability-aligned validation data to track skill improvements when training distributions vary. It addresses limitations of IID validation loss and benchmark-specific artifacts in scaling laws.

entry.title: Why We Need Speech to Evaluate Speech Translation

author.name: Maike Z\"ufle, Danni Liu, Vil\'em Zouhar, Jan Niehues

entry.summary: This work argues that speech translation evaluation needs the speech signal, showing both text- and speech-based quality estimation metrics fail to assess speech-specific phenomena like gender agreement and prosody. It trains SpeechCOMET models with speech encoders and identifies three causes of the evaluation gap.

entry.title: When Discourse Pressures Conflict: Information Structure in Vision-Language Model Outputs

author.name: Marcell Fekete, Johannes Bjerva, Tam\'as K\'aldi

entry.summary: This study tests whether vision-language models express visual content in discourse-appropriate forms using information structure in Hungarian, where Topic and Focus map to syntactic positions. Models produce relevant constructions but over-regularize compared to humans.

entry.title: OphIn-500K: Curating Web-Scale Visual Instructions for Scaling Ophthalmic Multimodal Large Language Models

author.name: Xuanzhao Dong, Wenhui Zhu, Xiwen Chen, Hao Wang, Xin Li, Yujian Xiong, Jiajun Cheng, Jingjing Wang, Xiaobing Yu, Haiyu Wu, Shao Tang, Zhipeng Wang, Langechuan Liu, Shan Lin, Oana Dumitrascu, Yalin Wang

entry.summary: OphIn-500K is a web-scale ophthalmic visual instruction dataset built via the OphIn-Engine curation pipeline to scale ophthalmology-specific multimodal LLMs. It addresses the scarcity of large domain-specific instruction-tuning data using real-world clinical complexity.

entry.title: D$^2$Turb: Depth-Aware Simulation and Decoupled Learning for Single-Frame Atmospheric Turbulence Mitigation

author.name: Zixiao Hu, Tianyu Li, Guoqing Wang, Wei Li, Guoguo Xin, Xun Liu, Peng Wang

entry.summary: D2Turb is a unified framework for single-frame atmospheric turbulence mitigation combining depth-aware physics-grounded simulation with decoupled restoration of texture and geometry. It introduces depth-dependent degradation synthesis with tilt supervision.

entry.title: Deformable Gaussian Occupancy: Decoupling Rigid and Nonrigid Motion with Factorized Distillation

author.name: Yang Gao, Wuyang Li, Po-Chien Luan, Alexandre Alahi

entry.summary: DeGO is a deformable Gaussian occupancy framework for autonomous driving that decouples rigid and nonrigid motion to better model human-centric agents, using factorized 4D foundation-model distillation. It enables each Gaussian primitive to evolve through both deformation and offset updates under weak supervision.

entry.title: Compositional Text-to-Image Generation Via Region-aware Bimodal Direct Preference Optimization

author.name: Zhuohan Liu, Wujian Peng, Yitong Chen, Zuxuan Wu

entry.summary: BiDPO enhances compositional text-to-image generation by extending Diffusion DPO to jointly optimize image and text preferences plus region-level fine-grained alignment. It builds BiComp, a large-scale quality-controlled preference dataset for attribute bindings, relationships, and counting.

entry.title: POINav: Benchmarking and Enhancing Final-Meters Arrival in Real-World Vision-Language Navigation

author.name: Ruiyan Gong, Meisheng Zhang, Yuxiang Zhao, Mingchao Sun, Yanfen Shen, Zedong Chu, Zhining Gu, Wei Guo, Xiaolong Cheng, Qiming Li, Kangning Niu, Yanqing Zhu, Xiaolong Wu, Tianlun Li, Mu Xu

entry.summary: POINav-Bench is the first benchmark for closed-loop evaluation of real-world point-of-interest goal navigation, reconstructed from real captures via 3D Gaussian Splatting across 11 commercial areas and 163 POIs. It targets the precise final-meters arrival challenge in vision-language navigation.

entry.title: Provably Guaranteed Polytopic Uncertainty Quantification for SLAM

author.name: Guangyang Zeng, Yulong Gao, Yuan Shen, Lingpeng Chen, Haoying Li, Guodong Shi, Junfeng Wu

entry.summary: This paper presents provably guaranteed polytopic uncertainty quantification algorithms for 3D-3D landmark-based SLAM, with forward UQ for mapping, backward UQ for pose tracking, and pose compounding modules. Each module produces certified uncertainty sets that provably contain true poses and landmarks under deterministic input bounds.

entry.title: Quantitative AI risk assessment: a starting point

author.name: Henry Papadatos

entry.summary: Proposes shifting AI risk management from qualitative to quantitative probabilistic modeling, drawing an analogy to nuclear safety's 1975 WASH-1400 transition, and demonstrates with nine probabilistic models of AI-enabled cyber attacks. It offers a methodology starting point inviting iterative community improvement.

entry.title: A Policy-Driven Runtime Layer for Agentic LLM Serving

author.name: Rui Zhang, Chaeeun Kim, Liting Hu

entry.summary: Argues for inserting a dedicated agent runtime layer between agent frameworks and serving engines to handle cross-cutting policies (prefix caching, batching, speculation, fairness, safety) that depend on both agent identity and engine events. It proposes an architectural rather than patch-based solution for agentic serving.

entry.title: TCP-MCP: Landscape-Guided Co-Evolution of Prompts and Communication Topologies for Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Yi Ding, Zijie Xuan, Haowei Zhou, Zhenyu Ju, Xiaoxiao Dong, Jingwen Zhang, Xingyu Zhu, Leixin Sun, Haochi Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes TCP-MCP, a co-evolution framework that jointly searches agent prompts and communication topologies as a unified genome, using landscape probing and Pareto-front diagnostics across task performance, token cost, and structural complexity. It treats prompt and topology design as coupled rather than separable.

entry.title: C-MIG: Multi-view Information Gain-based Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Clinical Diagnosis Reasoning

author.name: Yuwei Miao, Gen Li, Yunsheng Zeng, Xiandong Li, Yujin Wang, Siyu Chen, Luning Wang, Yunhao Qiao, Junfeng Wang, Jianwei Lv, Bo Yuan

entry.summary: Proposes C-MIG, a multi-view information-gain-based RAG framework with RL for clinical diagnosis that replaces exact-match binary rewards with information-gain rewards from retrieved-document and document-refinement views. It addresses sparse and uni-dimensional reward limitations in medical reasoning.

entry.title: STAB: Specification-driven Testing for Algorithmic Bottlenecks

author.name: Soohan Lim, Joonghyuk Hahn, Hyundong Jin, Yo-Sub Han

entry.summary: Introduces STAB, a specification-driven pipeline that generates test cases exposing algorithmic worst-case bottlenecks from natural-language problem specs alone, separating constraint-bound maximization from adversarial structure injection. It targets structural input conditions that drive runtime worst cases.

entry.title: Explaining is Harder Than Predicting Alone: Evaluating Concept-based Explanations of MLLMs as ICL Visual Classifiers

author.name: Carmen Quiles-Ram\'irez, Leticia L. Rodr\'iguez, Nicol\'as Martorell, Natalia D\'iaz-Rodr\'iguez

entry.summary: This study evaluates concept-based explainability of multimodal LLMs as in-context visual classifiers across conditions of increasing formal rigor up to Description Logic axioms, finding explaining is harder than predicting. It probes whether MLLM explanations reflect genuine internal computation.

entry.title: CyberJurors: A Multi-Agent Simulation Task for E-Commerce Disputes Verdict

author.name: Yanhui Sun, Wu Liu, Haifeng Ming, Xinru Wang, Hantao Yao, Yongdong Zhang

entry.summary: CyberJurors introduces the E-commerce Dispute Verdicts task and VerdictBench, a multimodal benchmark of 6,000 real cases, plus a multi-agent framework for grounding clues from redundant multimodal evidence. It targets crowdsourced jury decision-making for platform disputes.

entry.title: Can Quantum Federated Learning Withstand Circuit-Level Backdoors?

author.name: Aakar Mathur, Mohammed Ruknuddin, Ashish Gupta

entry.summary: This paper proposes CULT, a circuit-level backdoor threat model for Quantum Federated Learning, formalizing four stealthy quantum-aware attacks (Grover, Pauli, Bit-flip, Sign-flip) with theoretical stealthiness guarantees. It demonstrates vulnerabilities on MNIST and CIFAR-10 with non-IID splits.

entry.title: RAGe: A Retrieval-Augmented Generation Evaluation Framework

author.name: Larissa Guder, Jo\~ao Pedro de Moura, Arthur Accorsi, Gustavo Losch do Amaral, Maur\'icio Cec\'ilio Magnaguagno, Felipe Meneguzzi, Marcio Sorraglia Pinho, Dalvan Griebler

entry.summary: RAGe is a modular framework for benchmarking and guiding efficient RAG application development, focusing on resource telemetry and recommending optimal pipeline components (chunking, vector DB, embedding, retriever) for domain-specific datasets. It evaluates accuracy-efficiency-scalability trade-offs.

entry.title: Comparative Analysis of Liquid Neural Networks and LSTM for Sequential Pattern Recognition: Robustness, Efficiency, and Clinical Utility

author.name: Ye Kyaw Thu, Thazin Myint Oo, Thepchai Supnithi

entry.summary: This paper benchmarks Liquid Neural Networks (CfC) against LSTMs across four sequential modalities including neuromorphic, drawing, handwriting, and physiological data, with temporal dropout stress tests for robustness. It assesses efficiency and clinical utility.

entry.title: Simulation-Informed Diffusion for Decentralized Multi-robot Motion Planning

author.name: Jinhao Liang, Sven Koenig, Ferdinando Fioretto

entry.summary: Simulation-Informed Diffusion (SID) is a decentralized multi-robot motion planner using constraint-aware diffusion models to simulate neighboring robots' future trajectories before planning collision-free paths. It addresses the limitation of planning from static snapshots in cluttered, multi-agent settings.

entry.title: Locality-Aware Redundancy Pruning for LLM Depth Compression

author.name: Vincent-Daniel Yun, Youngrae Kim, Woosang Lim, YoungJin Heo, Minkyu Kim, Sunwoo Lee

entry.summary: Locality-Aware Redundancy Pruning (LoRP) is a training-free one-shot depth pruning method guided by a Representation Locality Score derived from inter-layer hidden-state similarity. It adapts to whether redundancy is localized or globally distributed across different LLM architectures.

entry.title: VibeSearchBench: Benchmarking Long-horizon Proactive Search in the Wild

author.name: Xiaohongshu Inc

entry.summary: VibeSearchBench is a benchmark of 200 bilingual tasks across 20 domains for evaluating long-horizon, multi-turn proactive search where users and agents collaboratively refine vague intent. It targets the evaluation-experience gap left by over-specified single-turn search benchmarks.

entry.title: Multi-Teacher Knowledge Distillation via Teacher-Informed Mixture Priors

author.name: Luyang Fang, Yongkai Chen, Jiazhang Cai, Ping Ma, Wenxuan Zhong

entry.summary: MT-BKD is a Bayesian multi-teacher knowledge distillation framework with a teacher-informed mixture prior, capturing uncertainty during distillation from diverse teacher expertise. It provides principled statistical grounding and uncertainty evaluation for model compression.

entry.title: Unified Synthesis of Compositional Speech and Sound from Free-Form Text Prompts

author.name: Yuyue Wang, Xihua Wang, Xin Cheng, Yijing Chen, Ruihua Song

entry.summary: This paper introduces Free-Form-Text-Prompt-to-Unified-Audio generation and PlanAudio, an autoregressive LLM-based framework that directly synthesizes unified audio with naturally composited speech and sound from unconstrained natural language. It avoids disjoint pipelines and structured-input requirements.

entry.title: LegalGraphRAG: Multi-Agent Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Reliable Legal Reasoning

author.name: Zerui Chen, Qinggang Zhang, Zhishang Xiang, Zhimin Wei, Linfeng Gao, Xiao Huang, Zhihong Zhang, Jinsong Su

entry.summary: LegalGraphRAG is a multi-agent graph retrieval-augmented generation framework for legal reasoning that structures heterogeneous legal corpora into multi-granular relational graphs and adds verification for transparent, evidence-based reasoning. It addresses flat-graph limitations and opaque RAG in high-stakes legal judgment.

entry.title: SSR3D-LLM: Structured Spatial Reasoning via Latent Steps for Fine-Grained Grounding in Unified 3D-LLMs

author.name: Jiawei Li, Ziyi Liu, Weijie Shi, Long Chen, Jiajie Xu, Xiaofang Zhou

entry.summary: SSR3D-LLM is a structured spatial reasoning interface for unified 3D-LLMs that replaces single pointer-style grounding with a sequence of latent spatial reasoning steps and memory tokens read by a geometry-aware scorer. It improves fine-grained 3D object grounding for relational queries with multiple same-class candidates.

entry.title: Stochastic Gradient Descent with Momentum is Algorithmically Stable

author.name: Yunwen Lei, Zimeng Wang, Xiaoming Yuan

entry.summary: This paper provides a comprehensive generalization analysis of stochastic gradient descent with momentum via algorithmic stability, covering both Polyak's and Nesterov's schemes, and establishes tight on-average stability bounds. It addresses the conjecture that momentum may degrade generalization despite accelerating training.

entry.title: Towards Reliable Multilingual LLMs-as-a-Judge: An Empirical Study

author.name: Irune Zubiaga, Aitor Soroa, Rodrigo Agerri

entry.summary: This empirical study explores strategies for building reliable multilingual LLM-as-a-judge evaluators across high-, mid-, and low-resource languages (English, Spanish, Basque), considering instruction translation, monolingual versus multilingual supervision, and model size. It addresses the English-centric bias of most automatic evaluation work.

entry.title: Reverse Probing: Supervised Token-level Uncertainty Quantification for Large Language Models in Clinical Text

author.name: Bushi Xiao, Sarvesh Soni, Daisy Zhe Wang

entry.summary: Reverse Probing is a supervised token-level uncertainty quantification framework specialized for clinical summarization that estimates uncertainty from pre-existing labeled summaries by treating text as a probe into the model's internal activations. It localizes uncertainty at the token/span level rather than sampling new outputs, outperforming baselines on two expert-annotated datasets.

entry.title: Skill-Conditioned Gated Self-Distillation for LLM Reasoning

author.name: Jiazhen Huang, Xiao Chen, Xiao Luo, Yong Dai, Senkang Hu, Yuzhi Zhao

entry.summary: SGSD (Skill-Conditioned Gated Self-Distillation) reformulates skill-based self-distillation for LLM reasoning as teacher hypothesis validation rather than unconditional imitation, retrieving skill-mistake pairs into a multi-teacher pool where skill-conditioned teachers score the same student rollout. It handles potentially irrelevant or misleading retrieved skills via gating.

entry.title: Test-Time Collective Action: Proxy-Based Perturbations for Correcting Algorithmic Harms

author.name: Meghana Bhange, Ulrich A\"ivodji, Elliot Creager

entry.summary: Test-Time Collective Action (TTCA) lets coordinated users with only query access correct algorithmic harms to subgroups via proxy-based input perturbations, without needing the provider to retrain. It empowers affected users to fix disparities without platform cooperation.

entry.title: Commit to the Bit: Reactive Reinforcement Learning Done Right

author.name: Onno Eberhard, Claire Vernade, Michael Muehlebach

entry.summary: Introduces Committed Q-learning for learning optimal reactive policies in non-Markovian/partially-observable finite environments with deterministic observations, proving almost-sure convergence under a rewire-robustness assumption that is weaker than prior q*-realizability. It addresses the unrealistic Markov assumption common in RL analysis.

entry.title: Bilinear Coordinate Alignment for Training-Free Task-Vector Transfer

author.name: Jungyong Son, Jinwook Jung, Minhee Park, Sungyong Baik

entry.summary: Proposes Bilinear Coordinate Alignment for training-free transfer of task vectors (fine-tuning expertise) across different pre-trained model versions, avoiding costly re-fine-tuning when a model is updated. It improves on activation- or gradient-matching methods that leave a gap relative to direct fine-tuning.

entry.title: Learning High-Dimensional Parity Functions with Product Networks using Gradient Descent

author.name: Guillaume Larue (Orange Research, Meylan, France), Louis-Adrien Dufr\`ene (Orange Research, Meylan, France), Quentin Lampin (Orange Research, Meylan, France), Hadi Ghauch (T\'el\'ecom Paris, Institut Polytechnique de Paris, Palaiseau, France), Ghaya Rekaya (T\'el\'ecom Paris, Institut Polytechnique de Paris, Palaiseau, France)

entry.summary: Demonstrates that compact product-based neural architectures with stochastic data sparsity enable efficient learning of high-dimensional parity functions, with convergence guarantees validated up to 100,000 dimensions. This tackles the classic exponential sample complexity barrier for parity learning.

entry.title: Stage-wise Distortion-Perception Traversal in Zero-shot Inverse Problems with Diffusion Models

author.name: Jiawei Zhang, Ziyuan Liu, Leon Yan, Zhenyu Xiao, Yuantao Gu

entry.summary: Proposes MAP-RPS, a stage-wise framework for traversing the distortion-perception trade-off using a single diffusion model in zero-shot inverse problems. It begins with a MAP estimation stage that approximates the MMSE solution.

entry.title: Iterative Causal Discovery: Per-Edge Impossibility Certificates, Tier-Aware Oracle Queries, and the $1+K$ Lower Bound

author.name: Eichi Uehara

entry.summary: Introduces a causal discovery protocol that attaches per-edge impossibility certificates distinguishing data-identified edge directions from unidentifiable ones, with tier-aware oracle queries and a 1+K lower bound. This adds principled rigor to interpreting causal discovery outputs.

entry.title: Quantum principal component analysis without eigenvector recovery

author.name: Yewei Yuan, Michele Minervini, Mark M. Wilde, Nana Liu

entry.summary: Introduces a measurement-based soft PCA framework that replaces hard top-k projection with an entropy-regularized Fermi-Dirac filter, avoiding explicit eigenvector recovery for quantum PCA. This suits score-based downstream tasks like anomaly detection and spectral profiling.

entry.title: SPRINT: Efficient Spectral Priors for Humanoid Athletic Sprints

author.name: Yantong Wei, Kaihong Huang, Hainan Pan, Jiawei Luo, Jiawei Zhou, Ziyan Mai, Zhiwen Zeng, Yaonan Wang, Huimin Lu

entry.summary: SPRINT enables humanoid robot sprinting by using frequency-adaptive spectral priors derived from a small library of motion sequences to generate kinematically feasible joint trajectories beyond reference speeds. It achieves zero-shot sim-to-real transfer in field experiments.

entry.title: Chain-based Adaptive Reconfiguration Over Lattices for Hallucination Reduction

author.name: Joan Vendrell Gallart, Solmaz Kia, Russell Bent, Michael Grosskopf

entry.summary: CAROL is a probabilistic test-time hallucination reduction framework that defines a semantic uncertainty measure based on response-context consistency and casts mitigation as a Markov chain accept-reject process with provable convergence. It operates at the level of meaning rather than tokens.

entry.title: KSAFE-MM: A Multimodal Safety Benchmark via Localized Contextualization for Korean Cultural Risks

author.name: Yongwoo Kim, Sojung An, Yunjin Park, Jungwon Yoon, Dujin Lee, HyunBeom Cho, Jaewon Lee, Wonhyuk Lee, Youngchol Kim, JeongYeop Kim, Donghyun Kim

entry.summary: KSAFE-MM is a multimodal safety benchmark for Korean cultural risks, covering both globally shared risks via linguistic contextualization and culture-specific vulnerabilities. It addresses English-centric and culturally-generic limitations in current MLLM safety evaluation.

entry.title: Risk-aware Selective Prompting for Hallucination Mitigation in Large Vision-Language Models

author.name: Yuang Huang, Yafeng Zhang, Yu Zilan

entry.summary: This paper systematically studies verification prompting for hallucination mitigation in large vision-language models, finding it is a risk-bearing intervention that helps hard inputs but harms easier ones, and proposes risk-aware selective prompting. It shows verification prompts redistribute attention from visual to instruction tokens.

entry.title: When Confidence Misleads: Suffix Anchoring and Anchor-Proximity Confidence Modulation for Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Jungwon Park, Jimyeong Kim, Jungmin Ko, Nojun Kwak, Wonjong Rhee

entry.summary: This paper studies when confidence misleads decoding in diffusion language models, showing EOT tokens can receive high confidence causing incomplete generation and that suffix anchors introduce local overconfidence. It proposes Suffix-Anchored Confidence Modulation to address these issues.

entry.title: When Seekers Are Hard to Help: Evaluating Emotional Support Dialogue Systems in Worst-Case Interactions

author.name: Jiajie Yang, Yangchun Li, Guanyi Chen, Rui Fan, Xin Bai, Tingting He

entry.summary: This paper evaluates emotional support dialogue systems under worst-case interactions where seekers are hard to help due to low engagement, resistance, or emotional volatility, contrasting with overly cooperative LLM-simulated seekers. It conducts an expert simulation study with eight counselling professionals.

entry.title: PubMedCausal: A Span-Level Annotated Corpus for Causal Relation Extraction in Biomedical Text

author.name: Ifeoluwa Kunle-John, Josiah Paul, Oluwatosin Agbaakin, Peter Aina, Ikenna Odezuligbo, Sydney Anuyah

entry.summary: PubMedCausal is a span-level annotated corpus for biomedical causal relation extraction with 30,000 paragraph-level rows and adjudicated cause-effect pairs. It distinguishes causal relations from broader associations beyond sentence-level explicit cues.

entry.title: Reflective Dialogue between Teacher and Solver Agents for Video Question Answering

author.name: Takuya Murakawa, Toru Tamaki

entry.summary: This work proposes a Reflective Dialogue between Teacher and Solver agents for video question answering that achieves domain adaptation purely through inference-time context injection without fine-tuning. The dialogue history provides correctness feedback and visual grounding for both correct and incorrect answers.

entry.title: SIGMA: Bridging Structural and Distributional Gaps for Vision Foundation Model Adaptation

author.name: Lingyu Xiong, Jinjin Shi, Xuran Xu, Cong Luo, Runyu Shi, Ying Huang

entry.summary: SIGMA is a lightweight parameter-efficient fine-tuning method for adapting vision foundation models to dense prediction tasks, bridging structural and distributional gaps with scale-adaptive fusion and semantic modulation. It aims for full fine-tuning performance at minimal cost.

entry.title: Category-Level 3D Correspondence in Camera Space via Morphable Object Priors

author.name: Leonhard Sommer, Artur Jesslen, Basavaraj Sunagad, Adam Kortylewski

entry.summary: This paper studies category-level 3D correspondence in camera space, predicting consistent 3D locations across object instances from a single image, and shows it can emerge without explicit correspondence supervision via a shared morphable object prior. It introduces HouseCorr3D, a large benchmark with 178k images.

entry.title: REVEAL: Reference-Grounded Reasoning for Multimodal Manipulation Detection

author.name: Jun Zhou, Bingwen Hu, Yaxiong Wang, Zhedong Zheng, Yongzhen Wang, Yuchen Zhang, Ping Liu

entry.summary: REVEAL reformulates multimodal manipulation detection as reference-grounded verification, comparing query image-text pairs against retrieved authentic evidence rather than memorizing artifacts. It builds a 170K-pair authentic news reference library to support comparative reasoning.

entry.title: ClothTransformer: Unified Latent-Space Transformers for Scalable Cloth Simulation

author.name: Yu Zhang, Yidi Shao, Wenqi Ouyang, Yushi Lan, Zhexin Liang, Chengrui Wu, Xudong Xu, Xingang Pan

entry.summary: ClothTransformer reformulates cloth simulation as autoregressive sequence modeling in a learned latent space, addressing the specialization, mesh-coupling, and collision-handling limitations of prior neural cloth simulators. It aims for unified and scalable simulation across scenarios.

entry.title: SANTS: A State-Adaptive Scheduler for World Action Models

author.name: Yirui Sun, Guangyu Zhuge, Keliang Liu, Jie Gu, Xinyu Bing, Zhongxue Gan, Chunxu Tian

entry.summary: SANTS is a state-adaptive scheduler for World Action Models that selects a state-dependent denoising depth along the video noise trajectory for action conditioning, rather than always using fully denoised video. It is motivated by the finding that full video refinement can sometimes reduce action relevance.

entry.title: Imitation Learning for Robot Assistance in Open Surgery: A Multi-Policy Evaluation on Suture Following

author.name: Xucheng Wang, Zhizhou Yang, Xiaoman Zhang, Sung Eun Kim, Romain Hardy, Pranav Rajpurkar

entry.summary: First evaluation of general-purpose imitation learning for surgeon-robot collaborative assistance in open surgery, benchmarking four policies (ACT, Diffusion Policy, SmolVLA, pi0) on suture-following across dataset size, viewpoint, and background variation. Under ideal conditions policies reach 50-75% success, with depth estimation error the dominant failure mode.

entry.title: Asking Is Not Enough: Protocol Sensitivity in LLM Confidence Calibration

author.name: Hankyeol Kim, Pilsung Kang

entry.summary: Shows that LLM confidence calibration comparisons between token-probability and verbalized confidence are highly sensitive to measurement choices (which answer string is scored, how it is read, and conditioning context). It evaluates this across four QA benchmarks and three small models.

entry.title: Constrained Auto-Bidding via Generative Response Modeling

author.name: Eunseok Yang, Xingdong Zuo, Kyung-Min Kim

entry.summary: Introduces the Generative Response Model for constrained auto-bidding, shifting the learning target from actions to responses by jointly predicting future traffic and cost/value curves as functions of a bid multiplier. It improves robustness over control-based and RL methods under non-stationary auction dynamics.

entry.title: AIBuildAI-2: A Knowledge-Enhanced Agent for Automatically Building AI Models

author.name: Ruiyi Zhang, Peijia Qin, Qi Cao, Li Zhang, Pengtao Xie

entry.summary: Introduces AIBuildAI-2, a knowledge-enhanced agent that automatically builds AI models for scientific applications by augmenting LLM parametric knowledge with external knowledge to overcome static, outdated, sparse internal knowledge. It targets non-AI-expert scientists building high-performing models.

entry.title: MACReD: A Multi-Agent Collaborative Reasoning Framework for Reaction Diagram Parsing

author.name: Chuang Tang, Chenhao Lin, Yin Xu, Hao Wang, Jinrui Zhou, Xin Li, Mingjun Xiao, Enhong Chen

entry.summary: Presents MACReD, a hierarchical multi-agent framework for parsing chemical reaction diagrams that coordinates specialized agents for molecular perception, arrow understanding, text extraction, and reaction reconstruction within a VLM-guided architecture. It addresses heterogeneous layouts and intertwined visual elements.

entry.title: Deconstructing Spatial Complexity: Hierarchical Decomposition for LLM Spatial Reasoning

author.name: Yi Wang, Haojie Lu, Zhaofan Zhang, Li Chen, Sihong Xie

entry.summary: This paper proposes hierarchical task decomposition to improve LLM spatial reasoning by breaking complex tasks into sub-tasks with simplified sub-environments, addressing models' weak spatial priors. It targets a known weakness limiting embodied AI applications.

entry.title: Global Policy-Space Response Oracles for Two-Player Zero-Sum Games

author.name: Junyu Zhang, Feihong Yang, Jian Wang, Chao Wang, Xudong Zhang

entry.summary: This paper guides PSRO population expansion by directly evaluating post-expansion population quality via Population Exploitability rather than best-responding to restricted-game meta-strategies. It improves equilibrium computation efficiency in large two-player zero-sum games.

entry.title: Efficient Post-training of LLMs for Code Generation With Offline Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Mingze Wu, Abhinav Anand, Shweta Verma, Mira Mezini

entry.summary: This paper explores offline reinforcement learning for code-generation post-training using existing code datasets to avoid the cost of online RL inference and verification. It finds offline RL especially beneficial for small models and challenging problems.

entry.title: Let Relations Speak: An End-to-End LLM-GNN Soft Prompt Framework for Fraud Detection

author.name: Zhixing Zuo, Huilin He, Jiasheng Wu, Dawei Cheng

entry.summary: LGSPF is an end-to-end LLM-GNN soft prompt framework for fraud detection that bridges graph structure and semantic space via soft prompts, avoiding feature distortion from hard-prompt textualization and capturing multi-relational complexity. It targets text-sparse fraud graphs.

entry.title: Utility-Aware Multimodal Contrastive Learning for Product Image Generation

author.name: Xiaohang Feng, Yiling Xie

entry.summary: This work introduces utility-aware multimodal contrastive learning with a novel Utility-Aware InfoNCE loss that incorporates consumer demand into product image generation, optimizing for marketplace sales rather than just semantic alignment. It bridges the gap between generation quality and commercial performance.

entry.title: Using Zero-Shot LLM-Generated Survey Data for Geographically Explicit Population Synthesis

author.name: Taylor Anderson, Sara Von Hoene, Orhan Yagizer Cinar, Emma Von Hoene, Amira Roess, Andrew Crooks, Hamdi Kavak

entry.summary: This study evaluates whether zero-shot LLM-generated health survey data from GPT-4.1 and Gemini-2.5-Pro can feed an iterative proportional fitting workflow for geographically explicit population synthesis. It tests synthetic survey records against BRFSS for Colorado and Mississippi.

entry.title: Diffusion-Based Ukrainian Handwritten Text Generation with Cross-Domain Style Transfer

author.name: Andrii Ahitoliev, Pavlo Berezin

entry.summary: This work constructs a 126,177-image Ukrainian handwritten word dataset from 308 writers and retrains DiffusionPen with cross-domain style transfer for low-resource Cyrillic handwriting generation. It addresses the underexploration of HTG beyond Latin scripts.

entry.title: How the Optimizer Shapes Learned Solutions in Equivariant Neural Networks

author.name: Teodor-Mihai Stupariu, Andrei Manolache

entry.summary: This work studies how optimizer choice shapes solutions in equivariant neural networks, comparing Muon and Adam across geometric architectures. On ModelNet40, Muon consistently outperforms Adam, with analysis via Hessian estimates and loss surface visualization.

entry.title: High-Fidelity Industrial Crash Dynamics Prediction via Geometry-Aware Operator Learning with Memory-Efficient Low-Rank Attention

author.name: Deepak Akhare, Mohammad Amin Nabian, Corey Adams, Sudeep Chavare, Sanjay Choudhry

entry.summary: This paper applies the GeoTransolver operator-learning framework with memory-efficient low-rank attention to predict industrial-scale automotive crash dynamics. It demonstrates a viable surrogate for computationally prohibitive finite element crash simulations.

entry.title: LoSATok: Low-dimensional Semantic-Acoustic Tokenizer for Cross-Domain Audio Understanding and Generation

author.name: Zhisheng Zhang, Xiang Li, Yixuan Zhou, Jing Peng, Guoyang Zeng, Zhiyong Wu

entry.summary: LoSATok is a low-dimensional audio tokenizer for cross-domain understanding and generation, using a semantic bottleneck that compresses 1280-dim semantic features to 128 dims with a time-relation loss. It reduces the modeling burden on diffusion transformers for generation while preserving understanding.

entry.title: Learning to Assign Prediction Tasks to Agents with Capacity Constraints

author.name: Shang Wu, Saatvik Kher, Padhraic Smyth

entry.summary: This paper studies sequential learning of agent expertise and assignment policies for routing prediction tasks to human or AI agents under capacity constraints. It provides theoretical characterization and explore-exploit policy-learning algorithms validated on tabular, image, and text tasks.

entry.title: PromptEmbedder:: Efficient and Transferable Text Embedding via Dual-LLM Soft Prompting

author.name: Yu-Che Tsai, Kuan-Yu Chen, Yuan-Hao Chen, Yu-Han Chang, Ching-Yu Tsai, Yu-Hsiang Chuang, Shou-De Lin

entry.summary: PromptEmbedder is a dual-LLM framework that decouples embedding knowledge from backbone weights by using a Prompting LLM to generate instruction-aware soft prompts for a frozen Embedding LLM via differentiable continuous relaxation. It improves efficiency and cross-architecture transferability compared to LoRA-based adaptation.

entry.title: FLORO: A Multimodal Geospatial Foundation Model for Ecological Remote Sensing Across Sensors and Scales

author.name: Jorge L. Rodriguez, Victor Angulo Morales, Areej Alwahas, Mariana Elias Lara, Fida Mohammad Thoker, Kasper Johansen, Bernard Ghanem, Fernando T. Maestre, Matthew F. McCabe

entry.summary: FLORO is a multimodal geospatial foundation model for ecological remote sensing trained via masked autoencoding on a small but diverse mix of satellite, drone, and elevation data across varied sensors and resolutions. It targets transferable representations under the sensor-variable conditions common in environmental applications.

entry.title: Revisiting Anthropomorphic Reflection Markers in Large Language Model Reasoning

author.name: Yahan Yu, Noa Nakanishi, Fei Cheng

entry.summary: This study revisits anthropomorphic reflection markers like 'wait' and 'hmm' in LLM reasoning traces, suppressing them via prompt- and token-level interventions to test whether they are necessary for reasoning. It finds the markers are not uniformly necessary and relates them to overthinking and redundant reflection.

entry.title: Learning Theory of the SVRG: Generalization and Convergence Analysis

author.name: Yunwen Lei, Zimeng Wang, Xiaoming Yuan

entry.summary: This paper develops the first non-vacuous generalization analysis of the SVRG variance-reduction method through algorithmic stability, establishing sharp stability bounds in convex and strongly convex settings. It fills a gap where prior work focused only on convergence.

entry.title: A Multi-dimensional Framework for Evaluating Generalization in EEG Foundation Models

author.name: Aditya Kommineni, Emily Zhou, Kleanthis Avramidis, Tiantian Feng, Shrikanth Narayanan

entry.summary: This work proposes a multi-dimensional evaluation framework for EEG foundation models under realistic low-resource conditions like limited labels, reduced sensor coverage, and parameter-efficient adaptation, rather than the usual full fine-tuning on curated data. It better reflects biomedical deployment constraints.

entry.title: Do Agents Need Semantic Metadata? A Comparative Study in Agentic Data Retrieval

author.name: Shiyu Chen, Tarfah Alrashed, Alon Halevy, Natasha Noy

entry.summary: This comparative study asks whether semantic metadata like schema.org is still necessary for agentic data discovery, comparing a baseline agent searching the open web against a semantic-metadata-aware agent. It evaluates whether LLM agents can reliably retrieve actionable data directly from unstructured web content.

entry.title: Information-theoretic Multimodal Representation Learning for Electrocardiogram Signals

author.name: Phu X. Nguyen, Konstantinos Kontras, Wei Dai, Huy Phan, Christos Chatzichristos, Paul Pu Liang, Bert Vandenberk, Maarten De Vos

entry.summary: MERIT is an information-theoretic multimodal framework for ECG representation learning that jointly preserves waveform physiological structure across abstraction levels while integrating clinical-report semantics. It addresses the loss of fine-grained morphology in prior text-aligned ECG models.

entry.title: Where LLM Annotators Fail: Label-Free Learning on Graphs with LLMs

author.name: Safal Thapaliya, Jiatan Huang, Chuxu Zhang

entry.summary: Shows that LLM annotation errors on graphs are not just class-dependent but also region-dependent, varying across feature-space clusters within a class. Proposes Cluster-Aware Noise Estimation (CANE) for label-free graph learning that models this localized noise structure.

entry.title: Sign-Aware Gated Sparse Autoencoders: Modeling Anticorrelated Features with Bi-Jump-ReLU Activations

author.name: Bartosz Wieciech, Zmnako Awrahman, Marcin Czelej, Victor Hugo Jaramillo Velasquez, Wioletta Stobieniecka

entry.summary: Proposes Sign-Aware Gated Sparse Autoencoders with a Bi-Jump-ReLU activation that allow one latent to encode both polarities of anticorrelated concepts along a shared direction, avoiding wasted dictionary capacity from non-negativity constraints. This improves SAE interpretability for opposed concepts.

entry.title: Geometry-First Generative Spatial Single-Cell Reconstruction

author.name: Ehtesamul Azim, Muhtasim Noor Alif, Tae Hyun Hwang, Yanjie Fu, Wei Zhang

entry.summary: GEARS is a geometry-first framework reconstructing intrinsic single-cell spatial geometry guided by spatial transcriptomics without cell-type labels, histology, or cell-to-spot assignment, including unpaired settings. It learns a domain-invariant encoder aligning ST spots and dissociated single cells.

entry.title: PhAME: Phenotype-Aware Molecular Editing via Latent Diffusion

author.name: {\L}ukasz Janisi\'ow, Sebastian Musia{\l}, Bartosz Zieli\'nski, Dawid Rymarczyk, Tomasz Danel

entry.summary: PhAME is a latent diffusion framework for phenotype-aware molecular editing that guides molecules toward desired biological signatures (cell morphology, transcriptomic perturbations) while preserving structural proximity to a known hit. It recasts molecular optimization as editing in latent space.

entry.title: Random Process Flow Matching: Generative Implicit Representations of Multivariate Random Fields

author.name: Julien Lalanne, David Picard, Lionel Boillot, Lina-Mar\'ia Guayac\'an-Carrillo, Leon Barens, Jean-Michel Pereira

entry.summary: Introduces Random Process Flow, a flow-matching framework that represents the vector field as a neural implicit function using Random Fourier Features to model multivariate random fields from sparse measurements. It enables uncertainty-aware generative reconstruction from limited observations of a single field.

entry.title: Context Features Are Cheap: Rank-Aware Decomposition for Efficient Feature Interaction in Recommender Systems

author.name: Yevgeny Tkach

entry.summary: Presents a rank-aware decomposition that moves redundant context-only computations from once-per-candidate to once-per-request in industrial recommender ranking models. It applies to factorization machines, DCNv2, self-attention, and FC layers via an exact algebraic block decomposition.

entry.title: Stop Suppressing the Tail: Causal Inference for Extreme Events

author.name: Eichi Uehara

entry.summary: Argues that standard robust double machine learning suppresses extreme outcomes that are the actual target in high-stakes settings like financial or climate losses, and proposes an ADRF estimator that emits a structured tail estimate. It addresses circular dependence in residual-based tail inference.

entry.title: A Methodology to Assess Power Modeling in Energy-Aware Federated Learning on Heterogeneous Mobile Devices

author.name: Chaimae Jallouli, Karim Boubouh, Robert Basmadjian

entry.summary: Proposes a reproducible CPU power estimation methodology with rail-to-cluster mapping for energy-aware federated learning on heterogeneous ARM devices, achieving under 10% error versus up to 959% for approximate models. It corrects major inaccuracies in current energy-aware FL frameworks.

entry.title: Learning to Translate from Soft to Hard LLM Prompts

author.name: Pitipat Kongsomjit, Suryansh Goyal, Jacob Whitehill

entry.summary: Explores training a dedicated translation model from soft prompts to natural language, producing fluent verbalizations that outperform training-free methods like InSPEcT. It suggests soft prompts optimized on small open-source models could transfer to other models.

entry.title: Variance-Adaptive Optimal Algorithm for Reinforcement Learning with Multinomial Logit Function Approximation

author.name: Wonyoung Kim, Min-Hwan Oh, Garud Iyengar, Assaf Zeevi

entry.summary: This paper provides variance-adaptive regret bounds for reinforcement learning with multinomial logit function approximation, achieving instance-optimal rates that capture environment variability. It narrows the gap between upper and lower bounds in MNL-based MDPs.

entry.title: PAST2HARM: A Simple Adaptive Past Tense Attack for Jailbreaking Multimodal AI

author.name: Snehasis Mukhopadhyay

entry.summary: PAST2HARM is an adaptive jailbreak framework that bypasses refusal training in multimodal text-to-image models by using past-tense reformulations and temporal deepening to erode safety boundaries. It exposes immature defenses in multimodal generative AI.

entry.title: TARQ: Tail-Aware Reconstruction Quantization for Rare-Word Robust Automatic Speech Recognition

author.name: Xinyu Wang, Ziyu Zhao, Ke Bai, Silin Meng, Dongming Shen, Xiao-Wen Chang, Yixuan HE

entry.summary: TARQ is a label-free post-training quantization framework for ASR that shifts calibration mass toward rare lexical tail items (names, numerals, domain words) using a closed-form per-layer rule with residual correction. It improves rare-word robustness without entity labels or curated calibration sets.

entry.title: DisasterBench: Benchmarking LLM Planning under Typed Tool Interface Constraints

author.name: Zhitong Chen, Kai Yin, Weifeng Zhang, Zhiyuan Wang, Xiangjue Dong, Chengkai Liu, Zhewei Liu, Yiming Xiao, Ali Mostafavi, James Caverlee

entry.summary: DisasterBench evaluates LLM planning over typed tool interfaces for disaster response, requiring executable workflows with correct parameter binding and dependency propagation across semantically similar but operationally distinct tools. It introduces First-Point-of-Failure for step-level failure attribution.

entry.title: Auditing Stance Asymmetry in Generative Explanations

author.name: Jiarui Han

entry.summary: This paper introduces Symmetry Decomposition Evaluation to audit stance-bearing asymmetry in generative explanations, where models avoid hostile language but assign responsibility, legitimacy, or fault asymmetrically across groups. It tests paired situations with group labels and structural-role rewrites.

entry.title: HELEA: Hard-Negative Benchmark and LLM-based Reranking for Robust Entity Alignment

author.name: Yoonjin Jang, Junwoo Kim, Youngjoong Ko

entry.summary: HELEA introduces a same-name hard-negative augmentation strategy for entity alignment benchmarks plus a two-stage retrieval-and-rerank framework using LLMs. It targets the problem of models exploiting name overlap rather than relational structure in knowledge graph fusion.

entry.title: Towards Unified Vision-Language Models with Incomplete Multi-Modal Inputs

author.name: Xiang Fang, Wanlong Fang, Changshuo Wang, Keke Tang, Daizong Liu, Siyi Wang, Wei Ji

entry.summary: This paper makes the first attempt at a unified vision-language model robust to incomplete multimodal inputs such as deactivated sensors, addressing safety and trustworthiness risks. It studies modality-incomplete data inconsistency between training and testing.

entry.title: EchoAvatar: Real-time Generative Avatar Animation from Audio Streams

author.name: Bohong Chen, Yumeng Li, Yinglin Xu, Youyi Zheng, Yanlin Weng, Kun Zhou

entry.summary: EchoAvatar is a real-time framework generating continuous full-body 3D character motion from streaming speech and music with low latency. It uses a unified streaming architecture and a training strategy enforcing strong audio dependency for generalization.

entry.title: HarmoVid: Relightful Video Portrait Harmonization

author.name: Jun Myeong Choi, Jae Shin Yoon, Luchao Qi, Roni Sengupta, Joon-Young Lee

entry.summary: HarmoVid harmonizes the lighting of a foreground video to match a target background, adjusting shadows, color tone, and intensity, while introducing a lighting deflickering model to handle temporal jitter. It overcomes the infeasibility of acquiring paired video relighting data.

entry.title: SAFEVPR: Patch-Based Conformal Verification for Safe Cross-Condition Sequence Visual Place Recognition

author.name: Ha Sier, Jiaqiang Zhang, Zhuo Zou, Xianjia Yu, Tomi Westerlund

entry.summary: SAFEVPR is a non-trainable verification-and-calibration pipeline for safe cross-condition sequence visual place recognition, using mutual-nearest-neighbour patch matching on frozen DINOv2 features and Mondrian conformal calibration. It restores conformal guarantees violated under cross-condition exchangeability breaks.

entry.title: PrimitiveVLA: Learning Reusable Motion Primitives for Efficient and Generalizable Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Yutai Li, Shaohui Peng, Jiaming Guo, Di Huang, Zihao Zhang, Yuxuan Guo, Yunkai Gao, Siming Lan, Ling Li, Xing Hu, Yunji Chen

entry.summary: PrimitiveVLA reframes VLA learning around reusable motion primitives instead of memorizing monolithic trajectories, using a shared multimodal canonical representation to disassemble demonstrations into primitives and reassemble them at inference. It aims to improve data efficiency and generalization in robotic manipulation.

entry.title: PortBench: A Correlation-Aware, Full-Pipeline Benchmark for LLM-Driven Portfolio Management

author.name: Yuxuan Zhao, Sijia Chen, Ningxin Su

entry.summary: Introduces PortBench, a correlation-aware full-pipeline benchmark for LLM-driven portfolio management spanning six asset classes over ten years, with a static QA layer of 6,269 correlation questions and a dynamic five-stage allocation pipeline. It fixes prior benchmarks ignoring cross-asset correlation.

entry.title: BuddyBench: A Privacy-Constrained Multi-Task Benchmark for Pediatric Social-Communication Personalization

author.name: Jeyeon Eo, Joo Young Kim, Ran Ju, Minyoung Jung, Unggi Lee

entry.summary: Introduces BuddyBench, a privacy-constrained multi-task benchmark linking drill-level learning trajectories, clinical assessments, self-reports, and randomized-trial endpoints for pediatric social-communication personalization. It supports knowledge tracing, recommendation, clinical prediction, and causal inference.

entry.title: Benchmarking AI for low-resource contexts: Thinking beyond leaderboards

author.name: Aakash Pant, Kavya Shah, Apoorv Agnihotri, Sneha Nikam, Prasaanth Balraj, Nakul Jain

entry.summary: This position-and-analysis paper argues AI evaluation for low-resource contexts should assess deployed systems under real operational constraints like noisy inputs, code-switching, and intermittent connectivity rather than isolated model leaderboards. It identifies gaps across speech, chat/RAG, and vision benchmarks.

entry.title: GS-FUSE: Granger-Supervised Gated Fusion and Multi-Granularity Alignment for Event-Driven Financial Forecasting

author.name: Yang Zhang, En Chun, Ziyun Mao, Yulu Wu, Jun Wang

entry.summary: GS-Fuse is a multimodal event-based financial forecasting framework with a Granger-supervised causal-aware gated fusion that opens to event text only when it adds predictive value beyond prices, plus multi-granularity alignment. It addresses asymmetric text-price predictive roles.

entry.title: FPMoE: A Sparse Mixture-of-Experts Approach to Functional Code Generation

author.name: Loc Pham, Lang Hong Nguyet Anh, Thanh Le-Cong

entry.summary: FPMoE is a sparse Mixture-of-Experts code generation model with language-specific routed experts for Haskell, OCaml, and Scala plus a shared expert, addressing the underperformance of LLMs on functional programming languages. It avoids both per-language fine-tuning gaps and cross-language interference.

entry.title: ROVER: Routing Object-Centric Visual Evidence for Grounded Multi-Image Reasoning

author.name: Guannan Lv, Ren Nie, Hongjian Dou

entry.summary: ROVER is a lightweight learnable plugin that routes object-centric visual evidence for grounded multi-image reasoning, avoiding the holistic-understanding loss and decoding costs of RoI-cropping approaches. It enables efficient global visual selection without fine-grained supervision.

entry.title: EigeNet: Geometry-Informed Multi-Modal Learning for Few-shot Novel View RIR Prediction

author.name: Chong Jing, Zitong Lan, Junan Zhang, Zhizheng Wu

entry.summary: EigeNet is a geometry-informed multi-modal framework for few-shot novel-view room impulse response prediction, using a cross-view alternate-attention transformer and an acoustic-ray-tracing-inspired modulation block. It addresses the inverse problem of predicting spatially varying RIR from sparse observations for spatial audio.

entry.title: Mining Multi-Modality Spatio-Temporal Cues for Video Important Person Identification

author.name: Xiao Wang, Minglei Yang, Bin Yang, Wenke Huang, Zheng Wang, Xin Xu, Mang Ye

entry.summary: This work introduces the Video Important Person identification task with the Temporal-VIP dataset (9,249 annotated video segments with rationales), addressing Temporal Importance Shift where early-significant individuals are demoted as full context unfolds. It mines multimodal spatio-temporal cues with textual rationales rather than relying on static image cues.

entry.title: FedEHR-Gen: Federated Synthetic Time-Series EHR Generation via Latent Space Alignment and Distribution-Aware Aggregation

author.name: Jun Bai, Ziyang Song, Yue Li

entry.summary: FedEHR-Gen is presented as the first federated framework for synthetic time-series EHR generation across hospitals, using latent-space alignment and distribution-aware aggregation to handle heterogeneity, sparsity, and high dimensionality. It enables privacy-preserving cross-hospital synthetic data without pooling raw records.

entry.title: Adaptive Coarse-to-Fine Subgoal Refinement for Long-Horizon Offline Goal-Conditioned Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Kaiqiang Ke, Shenghong He, Chengdong Xu, Yuheng Luo, Xiangyuan Lan, Chao Yu

entry.summary: CFHRL is a fully offline goal-conditioned RL framework that adaptively refines distant goals into intermediate subgoals before execution, recursively proposing targets and stopping refinement based on reachability. It addresses weak supervision and bootstrapping errors in long-horizon offline GCRL.

entry.title: Refining Multidimensional Video Reward Models via Disentangled Influence Functions

author.name: Muyao Wang, Zeke Xie, Hideki Nakayama

entry.summary: Identifies dimensional heterogeneity in multidimensional video reward models, where a training sample's reliability varies across evaluation dimensions, and uses disentangled influence functions to refine these reward models. It improves reward modeling for text-to-video generation evaluation.

entry.title: Dimensionality Reduction for Robust Federated Learning: A Theoretical Analysis and Convergence Guarantee

author.name: Shiyuan Zuo, Jiashuo Li, Rongfei Fan, Han Hu, Jie Xu
