entry.summary: Proposes Projected Dimensionality Reduction (PDR) to accelerate Byzantine-robust federated aggregation by compressing gradients into a smaller subspace via sparse random projection before distance-based robust aggregation, with theoretical convergence guarantees. It addresses the computational bottleneck of high-dimensional robust aggregation in large models.

entry.title: Calibrated Inference for the Conditional Average Treatment Effect in the Few-Placebo Regime via Gaussian Processes

author.name: Eichi Uehara

entry.summary: Studies calibrated inference for conditional average treatment effects in the few-placebo regime via Gaussian processes, showing that Bayesian X-Learner intervals under-cover and tracing this to a structural cause. It targets unequal-allocation trials and small holdout A/B tests.

entry.title: Benchmarking Ultrasound Foundation Models for Fetal Plane Classification

author.name: Leya Barrientos, Yuexi Du, Nicha C. Dvornek

entry.summary: Provides a comprehensive benchmark of four ultrasound-specific foundation models (USFM, MOFO, UltraSAM, FetalCLIP) against CNN baselines for fetal plane classification. It assesses transferable representation quality under limited labeled data in clinical ultrasound.

entry.title: Exploratory Experience Shapes the Geometry of Predictive Representations

author.name: Kseniia Shilova, Abdelrahman Sharafeldin, Advay Balakrishnan, Hannah Choi

entry.summary: Investigates how exploratory versus exploitative behavioral strategies shape the geometry of predictive representations in a predictive-coding agent navigating a tree-like maze. It links active sensing and the action-perception loop to internal representation structure.

entry.title: Conservative neural posterior estimation via distributionally robust training

author.name: William Laplante, Yuga Hikida, Charita Dellaporta, Fran\c{c}ois-Xavier Briol, Ayush Bharti

entry.summary: DRO-NPE improves simulation-based inference by replacing the standard neural posterior estimation objective with a distributionally robust worst-case loss over a Wasserstein ambiguity set, reducing overconfidence. It introduces KL-based miscoverage metrics and improves calibration across benchmarks.

entry.title: Can Hallucinations Be Useful? Solving Multi-Hop Questions With SLMs By Chaining System-I/II Reasoning

author.name: Saptarshi Sengupta, Suhang Wang

entry.summary: This paper argues that the think-first strategy is unnecessary for small language models in multi-hop QA, showing SLMs are often confidently correct initially and that hallucinations can help home in on true answers. It inverts conventional reasoning by chaining System-I and System-II thinking.

entry.title: Knowledge Dependency Estimation for Reliable Question Answering

author.name: Chaodong Tong, Qi Zhang, Nannan Sun, Lei Jiang, Yanbing Liu

entry.summary: Knot is a structured rank-aware knowledge dependency estimator that quantifies a black-box QA model's sensitivity to different candidate knowledge units (context, retrieval, decomposition, reasoning) while modeling redundancy and substitutability. It estimates fine-grained dependency scores without exhaustive perturbation.

entry.title: IFMTBench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Multilingual Translation Instruction Following

author.name: Mingrui Sun, Mao Zheng, Zheng Li, Mingyang Song

entry.summary: IFMTBench is a benchmark for multilingual translation instruction following covering seven languages with single and multi-constraint items across six constraint dimensions like schema preservation, glossary adherence, and register matching. It addresses gaps where BLEU/xCOMET ignore constraints and general instruction benchmarks ignore cross-lingual nature.

entry.title: A Road-Conditioned Traffic Movie Prediction Network with Spatiotemporal and Structure-Consistent Learning

author.name: Joshua Kofi Asamoah, Blessing Agyei Kyem, Armstrong Aboah

entry.summary: RCSNet is a road-conditioned spatiotemporal network for city-wide traffic movie prediction that enforces structure consistency with road layout, connectivity, and congestion propagation. It addresses cross-city generalization where treating forecasting as image reconstruction fails.

entry.title: DiscoForcing: A Unified Framework for Real-Time Audio-Driven Character Control with Diffusion Forcing

author.name: Kaiyang Ji, Bingsheng Qian, Binghuan Wu, Kangyi Chen, Ye Shi, Jingya Wang

entry.summary: DiscoForcing is a streaming audio-driven diffusion framework for real-time character control under strict causal, bounded-latency constraints with abrupt audio changes. It combines a causal music encoder capturing rhythmic structure with diffusion-forcing sequence modeling under heterogeneous noise levels.

entry.title: Simultaneous Contact Selection and Planning for Contact-Rich Manipulation with Cascaded Optimization

author.name: Zhe Zhang, Xingrong Diao, Haoxiang Liang, Han Yang, Bi-Ke Zhu, Dandan Zhang, Jiankun Wang

entry.summary: This work presents a cascaded optimization framework that simultaneously performs active contact location selection and planning for contact-rich manipulation. It overcomes the limitation of prior contact-implicit methods that require given contact location sequences.

entry.title: Natural Functional Gradients for Smooth Trajectory Optimization

author.name: Kisang Park, Chanwoo Kim, Kyungjae Lee, Sungjoon Choi

entry.summary: This paper proposes a trajectory optimization framework that performs geometry-aware updates directly in function space using natural functional gradients, optimizing a Gaussian-smoothed surrogate objective for collision-free smooth motion. Function-space updates allow trajectory regularity to be controlled independently of time discretization.

entry.title: Leveraging Introspection for Alignment

author.name: Yotam

entry.summary: Discusses how Anthropic's Model Psychology team's three papers on functional emotion vectors and introspective awareness suggest opportunities for inner alignment, where models' self-reports of internal states could be leveraged. It explores using introspection as an alignment tool.

entry.title: Soro: A Lightweight Foundation Model and Chatbot for Tajik

author.name: Stanislav Liashkov, Haitz S\'aez de Oc\'ariz Borde, Azizjon Azimi, Khushbakht Shaymardonov, Shuhratjon Khalitbekov, Bonu Boboeva

entry.summary: Introduces Soro, a family of Tajik-specialized conversational LLMs built on Gemma 3 via continual pretraining on a 1.9B-token corpus plus instruction tuning, along with new Tajik benchmarks. It demonstrates practical low-resource language deployment under tight compute and connectivity constraints.

entry.title: Reasoning and Planning with Dynamically Changing Norms

author.name: Taylor Olson, Roberto Salas-Damian, Kenneth D. Forbus

entry.summary: Presents a defeasible calculus for resolving normative conflicts and using dynamically changing norms as guardrails on AI plans in human-AI settings, validated with formal proofs and a dialogue agent. It addresses norm-guided planning under evolving social norms.

entry.title: MTAVG-Bench 2.0: Diagnosing Failure Modes of Cinematic Expressiveness in Multi-Talker Audio-Video Generation

author.name: Haitian Li, Yanghao Zhou, Heyan Huang, Liangji Chen, YiMing Cheng, Xu Liu, Dian Jin, Jiajun Xu, Jingyun Liao, Tian Lan, Ziqin Zhou, Yueying Liu, Yu Bai, Changsen Yuan, Jinxing Zhou, Xian-Ling Mao, Xuefeng Chen, Yousheng Feng

entry.summary: Introduces MTAVG-Bench 2.0, a benchmark diagnosing failure modes of cinematic expressiveness in multi-talker audio-video generation, targeting scene-level short-drama generation beyond basic lip-sync and audio-visual alignment. It assesses higher-level character performance and cinematic qualities.

entry.title: ResearchLoop: An Evidence-Gated Control Plane for AI-Assisted Research

author.name: Yihan Xia, Taotao Wang

entry.summary: ResearchLoop is an evidence-gated control plane for AI-assisted research that treats research questions, claims, evidence, and paper bindings as durable project state to make claims auditable. It addresses the publication risk that AI-compressed research makes claims easier to state than verify.

entry.title: FedMPT: Federated Multi-label Prompt Tuning of Vision-Language Models

author.name: Xucong Wang, Pengkun Wang, Zhe Zhao, Liheng Yu, Shuang Wang, Yang Wang

entry.summary: FedMPT performs federated multi-label prompt tuning of vision-language models using a causal front-door adjustment to prevent overfitting to spurious label correlations across heterogeneous clients. It improves robustness in decentralized multi-label recognition.

entry.title: Adaptive Multimodal Agents-Based Framework for Automatic Workflow Execution

author.name: Susanna Cifani, Mario Luca Bernardi, Marta Cimitile

entry.summary: This paper proposes a multimodal multi-agent framework for automatic GUI workflow execution with a two-phase pipeline that first discovers transition topology offline rather than treating tasks as discrete linear episodes. It improves agent effectiveness in novel and non-stationary workflow scenarios.

entry.title: LNN-PINN: A Unified Physics-Only Training Framework with Liquid Residual Blocks

author.name: Ze Tao, Hanxuan Wang, Fujun Liu

entry.summary: LNN-PINN augments physics-informed neural networks with a lightweight liquid residual gating mechanism in the hidden layers, improving predictive accuracy on complex PDE problems while keeping the rest of the pipeline unchanged. It isolates architectural gains via controlled ablation.

entry.title: Memory-Based vs. Context-Only Conditioning Produces Distinct Behavioral Patterns in Stateful Personalization

author.name: Junsoo Park, Youssef Medhat, Htet Phyo Wai, Ploy Thajchayapong, Ashok K. Goel

entry.summary: This study compares memory-based versus context-only conditioning in a teacher-facing educational recommender, finding contextual conditioning yields stronger question-level responsiveness while memory-based produces learner-specific history-dependent behaviors. It informs stateful personalization design.

entry.title: A Systematic Evaluation of Retrieval-Augmented Generation and Language Models for Space Operations

author.name: Ruben Belo, Marta Guimar\~aes, Cl\'audia Soares

entry.summary: This paper systematically evaluates RAG pipelines for space operations, comparing retrieval strategies, embedding models, and LLM answers for extracting actionable knowledge from technical space documentation. It assesses impact on information accuracy in a high-stakes domain.

entry.title: Resource-Constrained Affect Modelling via Variance Regularisation Pruning

author.name: Kosmas Pinitas, Konstantinos Katsifis

entry.summary: Variance-Regularised Pruning incorporates cross-participant stability into the sparsification process for affective computing models, evaluating each connection based on robustness across individuals rather than only average error. It targets resource-constrained pervasive affect modeling.

entry.title: Not All NVFP4 QAT Recipes Are Equal: How Architecture and Scale Shape Model Quality for Anomaly Segmentation

author.name: Zijian Du, Oleg Rybakov

entry.summary: This study examines how model architecture, scale, and FP4 quantization-aware training recipes interact on a recall-critical brain tumor segmentation task. It finds attention-based architectures are notably more robust to quantization recipe choices than CNNs at scale.

entry.title: UniMaia: Steering Chess Policies with Language for Human-like Play

author.name: Sherman Siu (University of Waterloo), Lesley Istead (University of Waterloo)

entry.summary: UniMaia steers a frozen Lc0-based chess policy with natural language using a parameter-efficient text encoder and ControlNet-style conditioning, enabling human-like and semantically controllable play. It combines the flexibility of language interfaces with the domain grounding of specialized policy networks.

entry.title: Fine-Tuned LLM as a Complementary Predictor Improving Ads System

author.name: Hui Yang, Daiwei He, Kevin Jiang, Taejin Park, Kungang Li, Jiajun Luo, Yuying Chen, Xinyi Zhang, Sihan Wang, Haoyu He, Yu Liu, Lakshmi Manoharan, David Xue, Shubham Barhate, Runze Su, Duna Zhan, Ling Leng, Siping Ji, Jinfeng Zhuang, Alice Wu, Leo Lu, Han Sun, Zhifang Liu

entry.summary: This Pinterest paper uses a fine-tuned open-source LLM as an ads-specific ancillary predictor—forecasting likely advertisers from user profiles and histories—rather than as a ranker, providing complementary signals to a production ads recommendation system. It demonstrates a practical paradigm for translating LLM advances into production RecSys gains.

entry.title: SmartDirector: Keyframe-Conditioned Cinematic Video Generation with Narrative Pacing Control

author.name: Zhida Zhang, Jie Ma, Zhan Peng, Haoxue Wu, Yang Han, Jun Liang, Jie Cao, Jing Li

entry.summary: SmartDirector generates cinematic video conditioned on multiple keyframes with narrative pacing control, supporting single-shot, multi-shot, and video-extension scenarios via a two-stage director-then-detail pipeline. It improves narrative structure control beyond sparse text or first/last-frame conditioning.

entry.title: KVoiceBench, KOpenAudioBench, and KMMAU: Agent-Driven Korean Speech Benchmarks for Evaluating SpeechLMs

author.name: Haechan Kim, Seungjun Chung, Inkyu Park, Jihoo Lee, Jonghyun Lee

entry.summary: This paper introduces agent-driven frameworks for constructing Korean speech benchmarks (KVoiceBench, KOpenAudioBench, KMMAU) that preserve language-specific instructions, answer constraints, and paralinguistic properties lost in naive benchmark transfer. It addresses the English-centricity of SpeechLM evaluation.

entry.title: StoryLens: Preference-Aligned Story Rewriting via Context-Aware Narrative Enrichment

author.name: Hanwen Cui, Yuting Mei, Yuhang Fu, Dingyi Yang, Qin Jin

entry.summary: StoryLens introduces preference-aligned story rewriting via context-aware narrative enrichment, arguing that enrichment (not just style transfer) drives reader satisfaction, supported by a pilot human study (24.5% vs 2.3% gains). It releases STORYLENSBENCH with structured story books, reader preference profiles, and ranked rewrites.

entry.title: PrunePath: Towards Highly Structured Sparse Language Models

author.name: Zhexuan Gu, Zixun Fu, Yancheng Yuan

entry.summary: PrunePath is a budget-adaptive structured sparsification framework for FFN layers that uses softmax-normalized routing with a cumulative-mass threshold to activate experts, enabling a single inference-time sparsity knob from one checkpoint. It targets hardware-friendly efficiency gains across NLU, NLG, and instruction tuning.

entry.title: Score Based Error Correcting Code Decoder

author.name: Alon Helvits, Eliya Nachmani

entry.summary: SB-ECC is a score-based error-correcting code decoder that frames soft decoding as continuous-time denoising via a probability-flow ODE guided by parity constraints, trained across noise levels without SNR conditioning. It supports a tunable latency-accuracy tradeoff and works across code families and block lengths.

entry.title: The Decision to Verify: How Warmth and User Characteristics Shape Reliance on Conversational Agents for Information Search

author.name: Mert Yazan, Frederik Bungaran Ishak Situmeang, Suzan Verberne

entry.summary: This study runs a mixed-subjects QA experiment to examine whether the hybrid conversational-AI-plus-web-search paradigm curbs overreliance, and which user factors (digital literacy, conversation warmth) drive verification of AI answers. It finds warmth and user characteristics shape the decision to fact-check.

entry.title: SARAD: LLM-Based Safety-Aware Hybrid Reinforcement Learning with Collision Prediction for Autonomous Driving

author.name: Kangyu Wu, Peng Cui, Guoxi Chen, Ya Zhang

entry.summary: SARAD is a safety-aware hybrid framework that synergizes LLMs and deep RL for autonomous driving, replacing unsafe random exploration with retrieval-augmented LLM-guided decisions from a dynamic expert knowledge repository plus collision prediction. An attention discriminator integrates LLM priors into DRL policy optimization.

entry.title: IPO-Mine: A Toolkit and Dataset for Section-Structured Analysis of Long, Multimodal IPO Documents

author.name: Michael Galarnyk, Siddharth Lohani, Vidhyakshaya Kannan, Sagnik Nandi, Aman Patel, Liqin Ye, Arnav Hiray, Rutwik Routu, Prasun Banerjee, Siddhartha Somani, Sudheer Chava

entry.summary: IPO-Mine provides an open-source toolkit and dataset for section-structured analysis of long, multimodal IPO filings that often exceed 500,000 tokens and lack consistent organization. It standardizes parsing of narrative text and images to enable study of these financially important documents with modern language and multimodal models.

entry.title: $E^3$-Agent: An Executable and Evolving Agent for Resource Management of Edge Generative Inference

author.name: Rui Bao, Yaping Sun, Zhiyong Chen, Feng Yang, Meixia Tao, Nan Li, Wenjun Zhang

entry.summary: E3-Agent is an executable and evolving agent for edge generative inference resource management that separates a fast millisecond-level router from a slow event-driven LLM meta-controller handling regime shifts via a small explicit control surface. It addresses unknown and non-stationary per-device per-model performance at deployment time.

entry.title: SparseOpt: Addressing Normalization-induced Gradient Skew in Sparse Training

author.name: Mohammed Adnan, Rohan Jain, Tom Jacobs, Ekansh Sharma, Rahul G. Krishnan, Rebekka Burkholz, Yani Ioannou

entry.summary: SparseOpt identifies that batch normalization induces gradient skew that slows dynamic sparse training, and proposes a sparsity-aware optimizer to fix it. Experiments on ResNet/CIFAR-100/ImageNet show faster convergence and better generalization.

entry.title: Density-aware Sample-specific Attack

author.name: Qiyuan Wang, Yao Li, Raymond K. W. Wong

entry.summary: Derives principled criteria for optimal sample-specific backdoor triggers, showing both attack success and clean-accuracy preservation are simultaneously optimized when triggered samples are steered into low-density regions of clean data. It introduces a bilevel optimization framework yielding attacks resistant to fine-tuning/pruning defenses.

entry.title: Parameter-Efficient Generative Modeling with Controlled Vector Fields

author.name: Peyman Morteza

entry.summary: Introduces a continuous-time generative modeling framework motivated by the Chow-Rashevskii theorem that builds expressive flows by modulating a small set of fixed bracket-generating vector fields with learned scalar controls. This yields a parameter-efficient, geometrically-interpretable alternative to learning full vector fields.

entry.title: Adaptive Bandit Algorithms for Contextual Matching Markets

author.name: Shiyun Lin, Simon Mauras, Vianney Perchet, Nadav Merlis

entry.summary: Develops adaptive bandit algorithms for contextual matching markets where arms arrive with observable contexts and player utilities are linear in contexts, aiming to minimize regret against a stable-matching benchmark. It addresses both stochastic and adversarial contexts despite the instability where small context shifts reconfigure benchmarks.

entry.title: Teacher-Student Representational Alignment for Reinforcement Learning-Driven Imitation Learning

author.name: Meraj Mammadov, Pedro Zuidberg Dos Martires, Johannes Andreas Stork

entry.summary: Addresses the irreducible imitation gap when teacher RL policies use privileged state the student cannot observe, proposing to learn a shared embedding space hiding agent-specific observations so that imitable teacher policies are trained by construction. This avoids costly RL finetuning after imitation learning.

entry.title: History-aware adaptive reduced-order models via incremental singular value decomposition

author.name: Amirpasha Hedayat, Ali Mohaghegh, Laura Balzano, Cheng Huang, Karthik Duraisamy

entry.summary: Develops a projection-based adaptive reduced-order model framework using incremental SVD, where occasional full-order evaluations provide correction snapshots for online basis updates. The method is history-aware, retaining an encoded record of observed dynamics.

entry.title: Frequency-Guided Action Diffusion via Sub-Frequency Manifold Traversal

author.name: Junlin Wang

entry.summary: Presents a frequency-based algorithm for visuomotor policy learning that performs implicit spectral maneuvering to filter high-frequency noise (jerks, jitter) in human demonstrations during diffusion-based behavior cloning. It aims for smoother action generation without inheriting demonstrator artifacts.

entry.title: Geometry of Relaxed Fair Regression: A Unified Framework for Aware and Unaware Settings

author.name: M. Generali Lince, V. Divol, R. Flamary, S. Gaucher, P. Loiseau

entry.summary: This work formulates fair regression under demographic parity as an optimal transport problem, unifying aware and unaware settings where sensitive attributes are unavailable at inference. It characterizes optimal predictors via OT maps under different penalty types.

entry.title: OralAgent: Integrating Reasoning, Tools, and Knowledge for Interactive Dental Image Analysis

author.name: Jing Hao, Siyuan Dai, Yongxin Zhang, Yuci Liang, Jiamin Wu, Jiahao Bao, Yuxuan Fan, Zanting Ye, Yanpeng Sun, Xinyu Zhang, Ming Hu, Liang Zhan, James Kit Hon Tsoi, Linlin Shen, Junjun He, Kuo Feng Hung

entry.summary: OralAgent is a dental-specialized AI agent unifying multimodal reasoning, tool-based decision-making, and knowledge-grounded retrieval with 22 visual tools and 368 dental textbooks. It introduces an OralCorpus dataset for interactive dental image analysis.

entry.title: FinBoardBench: Benchmarking Dynamic Wealth Management and Strategic Financial Reasoning of LLMs via Board Game Simulations

author.name: Xuesi Hu, Peng Wang, Jinpeng Miao, Xilin Tao, Caiwei Li, Yue Ma, Jie He, Qiancheng Zhang, Yuntao Zou, Dagang Li

entry.summary: FinBoardBench evaluates LLMs' dynamic wealth management and strategic financial reasoning using three classic financial board games (Cashflow, Acquire, Monopoly), assessing cash flow management, acquisition forecasting, and trade negotiations. It reveals limitations of LLMs in dynamic financial decision-making beyond static benchmarks.

entry.title: Boundary Suppression Asymmetry in Post-trained Assistants: Over-expansion as a Controllability Cost

author.name: Jiarui Han

entry.summary: This paper studies boundary-suppression asymmetry in post-trained assistants, finding that optimization to avoid under-answering creates asymmetric controllability costs where over-completion and extra-help behaviors resist user requests for narrower answers. It analyzes controllability via controlled assistant-policy variants.

entry.title: Breaking the Script Barrier: Enabling Automatic Alignment for PoS-based ASR Error Analysis in Non-Latin Scripts

author.name: Prasenjit K Mudi, Dahlia Devapriya, Sheetal Kalyani

entry.summary: This paper proposes a language-agnostic alignment mechanism for part-of-speech-based ASR error analysis that works across both Latin and non-Latin scripts. It enables fine-grained error characterization beyond aggregate word error rate metrics.

entry.title: Can Large Language Models Handle Discourse Particles? A Case Study of Colloquial Malay

author.name: Mariah Al Giptiah Binte Yusoff, Jakin Tan, Bocheng Chen, Guangliang Liu, Xi Chen

entry.summary: MalayPrag is a benchmark for evaluating LLM handling of discourse particles in colloquial Malay, with five linguistically grounded attributes. It addresses the under-study of pragmatics in Southeast Asian languages.

entry.title: Bounded-Compute Multimodal Regression for Product-Rating Prediction

author.name: William Leach, Ru He, Sizhuo Ma, Yizhen Jia, Min Cao, Jian Wang, Rick Cao

entry.summary: This work presents a bounded-compute adaptation of SmolVLM2-256M for product-rating regression, replacing the language-modeling head with a lightweight MLP on pooled decoder states under strict latency budgets. It shows feature-based regression outperforms token-based score generation.

entry.title: MangaFlow: An End-to-End Agentic Framework for Controllable Story to Manga Generation

author.name: Muyao Wang, Zeke Xie, Yanhao Chen, Lixin Xiu, Hideki Nakayama

entry.summary: MangaFlow is an agentic framework for end-to-end story-to-manga generation that decomposes the task into planning, character grounding, layout, reference-conditioned rendering, composition, and lettering. It treats layout and references explicitly to improve cross-panel consistency and control.

entry.title: Toward Semantic-Agnostic and Shape-Aware Vision-Language Segmentation Models

author.name: Corentin Seutin, Mohamed Amine Ettaki, Micha\"el Cl\'ement, Pierrick Coup\'e, R\'emi Giraud

entry.summary: SANSA introduces semantic-agnostic and shape-aware vision-language segmentation, requiring models to segment from non-semantic textual descriptions of shape, geometry, or texture rather than object categories. It proposes prompt-generation strategies based on dictionary constraints or example guidance.

entry.title: AURA: Asymptotically Optimal Uncertainty-Robust Replanning Algorithm for Kinodynamic Systems

author.name: Seyedali Golestaneh, Zhuoyun Zhong, Donghyung Lee, Constantinos Chamzas

entry.summary: AURA is an asymptotically optimal, uncertainty-robust replanning meta-planner for kinodynamic systems that interleaves execution with continual replanning to improve path quality and tracking under motion uncertainty. It addresses the offline-only limitation of sampling-based kinodynamic planners.

entry.title: An Operator-Based Approach to STL

author.name: Panagiotis Rousseas, Dimos V. Dimarogonas

entry.summary: This paper introduces an operator-based approach to Signal Temporal Logic, defining an operator acting on reachability value functions to handle complex multi-nested formulae and support online control synthesis. It develops operator-based nesting rules directly rather than designing STL barrier functions.

entry.title: Chance-Constrained MPPI under State and Dynamic Object Prediction Uncertainty and the Evaluation of Collision Risk Calibration

author.name: Benjamin Serfling, Konrad Doll, Kati Radkhah-Lens

entry.summary: This paper develops chance-constrained MPPI control under state and dynamic object prediction uncertainty and evaluates collision risk calibration using proper scoring rules. It analyzes closed-loop failure modes—safety violations from overconfidence and freezing from underconfidence—when upstream estimators are miscalibrated.

entry.title: Constitutional AI Alignment

author.name: RogerDearnaley

entry.summary: A LessWrong post analyzing Anthropic's updated Claude Constitution (Soul Doc), arguing aligned behavior is not the default for distilled LLMs or RL maximizers and that constitutions should explain the reasoning behind rules so capable models extrapolate them out-of-distribution. It proposes improvements for aligning AGI/ASI-level systems.

entry.title: GraD-IBD: Graph Representation Learning from Diagnosis Trajectories for Early Detection of Inflammatory Bowel Disease

author.name: Leo Y. Li-Han, Ellen L. Larson, Elizabeth B. Habermann, Cornelius A. Thiels, Hojjat Salehinejad

entry.summary: Proposes GraD-IBD, a graph model that reformulates longitudinal ICD diagnosis trajectories as visit-bucketized temporally directed graphs with context-aware time-decay message passing for early inflammatory bowel disease detection. It reduces model complexity while capturing temporal dependencies.

entry.title: Clark Hash: Stateless Sparse Johnson-Lindenstrauss Quantization for Neural Embeddings

author.name: Stanislav Kirdey, Clark Labs Inc

entry.summary: Presents Clark Hash, a stateless sparse signed Johnson-Lindenstrauss quantization that stores 384-dim embeddings in 48 bytes (32x smaller) without training, codebooks, or corpus statistics, evaluated on multilingual sentence similarity. It offers a simple plug-and-play embedding compression codec.

entry.title: From paper to benchmark: agentic, framework-based reproduction of under-specified methods in machine health intelligence

author.name: Raffael Theiler, Ludovico Comito, David Leko, Leandro Von Krannichfeldt, Lev Telyatnikov, Olga Fink

entry.summary: This work introduces an agentic, framework-based approach for reproducing under-specified machine-health methods into benchmark-ready, comparable implementations. It addresses the broader challenge of translating papers into executable, comparable code.

entry.title: Entropy-aware Masking for Masked Language Modeling

author.name: Gokul Srinivasagan, Kai Hartung, Munir Georges

entry.summary: This paper proposes entropy-aware masking for masked language modeling, using the model's prediction entropy to target more informative, uncertain tokens for masking instead of random selection. It aims to improve pretraining efficacy of encoder models.

entry.title: A Conflict-Aware Penalty and Statistical Loss Framework for Balancing Modalities and Enhancing Stability in Multimodal Sentiment Analysis

author.name: Jianheng Dai, Jiazhang Liang, Sijie Mai

entry.summary: This paper proposes a Conflict-aware Penalty to detect and penalize gradient-norm conflicts and a Statistical Loss to align predicted and input distribution statistics in multimodal sentiment analysis, preventing the dominant text modality from suppressing weaker modalities. It improves training stability and modality balance.

entry.title: Symmetry Defeats Auditing

author.name: Nick Merrill, Zeke Medley

entry.summary: This very short paper demonstrates a symmetry-based attack defeating Introspection Adapters proposed in prior work. It shows that auditing mechanisms relying on introspection can be circumvented.

entry.title: ESC-Skills: Discovering and Self-Evolving Skills for Emotional Support Conversations

author.name: Jie Zhu, Huaixia Dou, Shuo Jiang, Junhui Li, Lifan Guo, Feng Chen, Chi Zhang, Fang Kong

entry.summary: ESC-Skills is a skill-centric framework for emotional support conversations that models localized interactions as Intervention Units capturing state-action-outcome dynamics and builds a self-evolving bank of executable support skills. It improves interpretability and systematic skill improvement over end-to-end response generation.

entry.title: Integrated and Cross-Architecture Interpretation of LLM Reasoning

author.name: Leonardo Matthew Yauw, Wei-Bin Kou, Yujiu Yang

entry.summary: The IAR framework provides integrated, cross-architecture interpretation of LLM reasoning by combining bandwidth-calibrated Mutual Information Peak detection with Deep-Thinking Ratio analysis to isolate reasoning-crucial tokens. It aims to avoid underestimating inferential structure from single probes.

entry.title: Bayesian Gated Non-Negative Contrastive Learning

author.name: Peng Cui, Jiahao Zhang, Lijie Hu

entry.summary: BayesNCL is a Bayesian gated non-negative contrastive learning method that addresses entangled, opaque representations in contrastive learning by replacing deterministic similarity with gating that resolves an optimization conflict over common background features. It aims for more interpretable, disentangled representations for safety-critical use.

entry.title: Evaluating the Realism of LLM-powered Social Agents: A Case Study of Reactions to Spanish Online News

author.name: Alejandro Buitrago L\'opez, Alberto Ortega Pastor, Javier Pastor-Galindo, Jos\'e A. Ruip\'erez-Valiente

entry.summary: This study evaluates whether LLM-generated reactions to Spanish online news reproduce measurable properties of real audience discourse, pairing 5,631 news items with 58,555 real reactions and a matched synthetic set from five LLMs. It compares across hate speech, sentiment, and semantic alignment to validate social agent realism.

entry.title: Deep Learning Strain Estimation: Is Physics-Based Simulation the Solution?

author.name: Thierry Judge, Nicolas Duchateau, Andreas {\O}stvik, Khuram Faraz, Anders Austlid Task\'en, Sigve Karlsen, Thor Edvardsen, Harald Brunvand, Md Abulkalam Azad, Havard Dalen, Bj{\o}rnar Grenne, Gabriel Kiss, Pierre-Yves Courand, Lasse Lovstakken, Pierre-Marc Jodoin, Olivier Bernard

entry.summary: This paper proposes a novel echocardiography simulation strategy incorporating speckle decorrelation measures to improve deep learning myocardial strain estimation, addressing the lack of reliable motion references. It investigates whether physics-based simulation can serve as the training solution for accurate regional strain estimation.

entry.title: Law of Neural Interaction: Depth-Width Shape, Interaction Efficiency, and Generalization

author.name: Wenjie Sun, Jinning Yang, Shuai Zhang, Mengnan Du

entry.summary: Extends the concept of superposition from parameter space to gradient space (termed neural interaction) using the Neural Feature Ansatz, finding that good generalization accompanies efficient neural interactions tunable via depth-width ratio. It suggests an efficient interaction interval stable across budgets.

entry.title: AOE: Exhaustive Out-of-Distribution Detection via Recalibrating Outlier Labels

author.name: Fengqiang Wan, Qing-Yuan Jiang, Yang Yang

entry.summary: AOE improves outlier-exposure-based out-of-distribution detection by recalibrating outlier labels rather than using uniform labels, theoretically showing uniform labels ignore OOD-to-ID category relations. It enlarges the ID/OOD margin while preserving these relations.

entry.title: Learning to Bid in Repeated Second-Price Auctions with Dynamic Values and Aggregated Feedback

author.name: Benjamin Heymann, Otmane Sakhi

entry.summary: Studies learning to bid in repeated second-price auctions where the bidder's value depends on time since last win, with only aggregated end-of-horizon feedback in continuous time. Derives regret bounds combining plug-in estimators with a differential-equation characterization of the optimal policy.

entry.title: Detecting Diffusion-Generated Time Series Under Generator Shift

author.name: Zhi Wen Soi, Aditya Shankar, Gert Lek, Abele M\u{a}lan, Daniel Neider, Jian-Jia Chen, Lydia Chen

entry.summary: Studies detecting diffusion-generated time series under unknown generators, comparing white-box reconstruction-based detection against black-box classifiers, and finds reconstruction detection breaks down under generator shift because no universal time-series reconstruction prior exists. A simple off-the-shelf classifier is more robust as a black-box detector.

entry.title: Accelerating Reinforcement Learning Training Using Simulation Surrogate Models

author.name: Mohammadmahdi Ghasemloo, David J. Eckman, Yaxian Li

entry.summary: Investigates surrogate models for accelerating reinforcement learning training when reward structure or system dynamics change over time, exploring interactions between simulation models, surrogates, and RL models. It targets high-cost high-fidelity stochastic simulation environments.

entry.title: Sparse POD Mode Selection and Manifold Dimensionality Reduction with Neural Networks

author.name: Tomoki Koike, Prakash Mohan, Marc T. Henry de Frahan, Elizabeth Qian, Julie Bessac

entry.summary: Develops sparse POD mode selection and nonlinear manifold dimensionality reduction with neural networks for model order reduction in advection-dominated and turbulent flows. It addresses POD's failure on slowly decaying Kolmogorov n-widths and energy-based mode discarding.

entry.title: Implicit Regularization in Perturbed Deep Matrix Factorization: Spectral Conditions and Stability

author.name: Jingzhe Wang, Hung-Hsu Chou

entry.summary: This paper studies implicit regularization in perturbed deep matrix factorization, deriving spectral conditions for a low-rank phase under gradient descent and proving its stability under noise. It quantifies how perturbations affect convergence and eigenvalue recovery.

entry.title: MERIT: Matching Expertise via Rubric-Informed Training for Reviewer Assignment

author.name: Zixuan Yang, Yibo Zhao, Weicong Liu, Xiang Li

entry.summary: MERIT is a two-stage framework for reviewer assignment that trains a reviewer assessor via reinforcement learning to identify required expertise dimensions and match them against reviewers' prior work, with rewards from an LLM judge using paper-specific rubrics. It converts criterion-level matching into scalable suitability supervision.

entry.title: ConRAG: Consensus-Driven Multi-View Retrieval for Multi-Hop Question Answering

author.name: Yikai Zhu, Kunfeng Chen, Qihuang Zhong, Juhua Liu, Bo Du

entry.summary: ConRAG is a consensus-driven multi-view RAG framework for multi-hop QA that optimizes both query-side and corpus-side, leveraging relation, entity, and text signals to gather multi-view evidence. It boosts LLM performance on complex multi-hop reasoning.

entry.title: Comonadic Morphophonology: A Compositional Framework for Context-Dependent Morphological Rules in Finnish

author.name: Yongseok Jang

entry.summary: This paper presents a compositional category-theoretic framework using a Writer comonad to model context-dependent Finnish morphophonological rules without finite-state transducer state explosion. It offers a formal account that neural models lack.

entry.title: JECA^2: Judgment-Explanation Consistent Adversarial Attack against Forensic Vision-Language Models

author.name: Jiachen Qian

entry.summary: JECA^2 studies judgment-explanation consistent adversarial attacks against forensic vision-language models, jointly redirecting visual attribution and aligning textual explanations with a target judgment. It exposes a robustness gap where prior attacks leave contradictory explanations.

entry.title: Agentic Language-to-Objective Synthesis for Optofluidic Assembly

author.name: Ivan Saraev, Elena Erben, Weida Liao, Fan Nan, Gerhard Neumann, Eric Lauga, Moritz Kreysing

entry.summary: Speak-to-Objective is a modular agentic pipeline using a conditioned LLM to translate spoken or written commands into fully differentiable objective functions for assembling microparticles via optofluidic manipulation. It bridges human design intent and machine-executable goals in light-based micro-manufacturing.

entry.title: Differentiable Model Predictive Safety for Heterogeneous Mobility at Urban Intersections

author.name: Wenzhe Song, Hao Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces Differentiable Model Predictive Safety (DMPS), embedding model-predictive foresight into an end-to-end RL architecture where agents learn latent dynamics and a differentiable safety critic backpropagated through predicted trajectories. It targets safe coordination of heterogeneous agents at unregulated urban intersections.

entry.title: DynaSchedBench: Calibrated Dynamic Scheduling Benchmarks and Observability Paradox in LLM-based Scheduling Agents

author.name: Shijie Cao, Yuan Yuan, Jing Liu

entry.summary: Presents DynaSchedBench, a calibrated diagnostic benchmark for Dynamic Flexible Job Shop Scheduling with a Schedule Stress Index to stratify instance difficulty, and analyzes an observability paradox in LLM scheduling agents. It aims to reduce benchmark overfitting and stochastic noise in neural combinatorial optimization.

entry.title: Hierarchical Prompt-Domain Control and Learning for Resource-Constrained Agentic Language Models

author.name: Joan Vendrell Gallart, Russell Bent, Michael Grosskopf

entry.summary: Proposes a hierarchical control-and-learning framework for resource-constrained agentic LLMs, distilling a compact model to a schema then supervising it online via an oracle-controller loop that keeps prompts within a feasible domain. It targets reliable agent behavior under memory, latency, and cost constraints.

entry.title: OccuReward: LLM-Guided Occupant-Centric Reward Shaping for Demographic Equity in Grid-Interactive Buildings

author.name: Shadmehr Zaregarizi, Khashayar Yavari

entry.summary: OccuReward investigates how LLM-generated reward functions for building energy management may create or worsen comfort disparities across demographic groups, introducing a Comfort Equity Index. It explores fairness implications of LLM-mediated reward design in DRL.

entry.title: An LLM-Based Assistance System for Intuitive and Flexible Capability-Based Planning

author.name: Luis Miguel Vieira da Silva, Nicolas K\"onig, Felix Gehlhoff

entry.summary: This paper presents a hybrid assistance system augmenting capability-based SMT planning with an LLM to make solver feedback (especially unsatisfiability) interpretable and to adapt knowledge models as conditions change. It targets practical industrial process-sequence planning.

entry.title: Mathematical Modelling of Ethical AI Use in Higher Education: A Coordination Game Framework for Future-Facing Learning

author.name: Ndidi Bianca Ogbo, Zhao Song, Shatha Ghareeb, The Anh Han

entry.summary: This paper reframes student AI use in higher-education assessment as a coordination problem and develops an evolutionary game-theoretic framework capturing learning value, effort, fairness, and transparency. It models how collective norms of responsible or opportunistic AI use stabilize within cohorts.

entry.title: Generic Interpretation Approach for Transformer Models Incorporating Heterogenous Attention Structures

author.name: Yongjin Cui, Xiaohui Fan, Huajun Chen

entry.summary: This paper proposes a generic interpretation approach for Transformer models with heterogeneous (co-attention) structures that process information from different sources, addressing how fused multimodal information can be interpreted. It categorizes attention into homogeneous and heterogeneous types.

entry.title: The Energy Blind Spot: NVIDIA's Flagship Edge AI Hardware Cannot Support Process-Level Energy Attribution

author.name: Deepak Panigrahy, Aakash Tyagi

entry.summary: An energy-observability audit of NVIDIA GB10-based edge AI hardware, finding that the platform cannot support process-level energy attribution for agentic workloads. It quantifies how orchestration structure and CPU-side processing dominate energy costs for multi-step agentic tasks.

entry.title: Transferable Reinforcement Learning via Probabilistic Latent Embeddings and Dynamic Policy Adaptation for Sim-to-Real Deployment

author.name: Gengyue Han, Yiheng Feng

entry.summary: This paper proposes an RL framework for sim-to-real transfer using probabilistic latent embeddings and dynamic policy adaptation, targeting safe deployment of agents like autonomous vehicles. It aims to handle unmodeled dynamics better than zero-shot robust or domain-randomization methods.

entry.title: Tool Forge: A Validation-Carrying Toolchain for Governed Agentic Execution

author.name: Swanand Rao

entry.summary: Tool Forge is a validation-carrying toolchain that converts natural-language capability intent into governed, sandbox-verified, cataloged tool artifacts, exposing them to agents via a token-efficient routing layer. It treats each tool as a capsule containing intent, contract, implementation, tests, and runtime policy.

entry.title: I Hear, Therefore I Trust: A Socio-Technical Investigation of Humans as Synthetic Speech Detectors

author.name: Lelia Erscoi (Computational Speech Group, University of Eastern Finland), Tomi Kinnunen (Computational Speech Group, University of Eastern Finland)

entry.summary: This socio-technical study investigates humans as synthetic speech detectors, with 47 participants localizing suspected synthetic segments under manipulated trust cues (instructional framing, affective priming, provenance labeling). It examines how context and perception shape deepfake detection accuracy.

entry.title: VidPrism: Heterogeneous Mixture of Experts for Image-to-Video Transfer

author.name: Rui Lin, Chuanming Wang, Huadong Ma

entry.summary: VidPrism is a heterogeneous temporal Mixture-of-Experts framework for adapting vision-language models to video understanding, introducing functional division of labor among experts to combat expert homogenization. It improves spatio-temporal modeling for image-to-video transfer learning.

entry.title: Anomaly as Non-Conformity via Training-Free Graph Laplacian Energy Minimization

author.name: Jungwook Seo, Minjeong Kim, Younkwan Lee, Seungho Shin, Sungyong Baik

entry.summary: ANoCo is a training-free unsupervised anomaly detection method that scores visual anomalies by the cost of non-conformity to a fixed normal feature manifold via graph Laplacian energy minimization, going beyond simple feature similarity. It uses a bipartite query-to-normal graph weighted by cosine affinity.

entry.title: BiasEdit: A Training-Free Bias-Detect-and-Edit Framework for Learning Fair Visual Classifiers

author.name: Jungwook Seo, Yoonsik Park, Changmin Lee, Sungyong Baik

entry.summary: BiasEdit is a training-free bias-detect-and-edit framework for learning fair visual classifiers from biased web data containing spurious correlations and social biases. It addresses the imbalance between bias-aligned and bias-conflicting samples without retraining.

entry.title: The Fundamental Limits of Fraud Detection in Card Payment Networks

author.name: Gaurav Dhama

entry.summary: This paper argues that limits in card-payment fraud detection stem from structural information impairments (delayed, censored, corrupted, counterfactually-missing feedback) rather than model capacity, and derives a minimax regret lower bound. It implies that improving data/reporting quality matters more than model improvements.

entry.title: Decentralized Parameter-Free Online Learning with Compressed Gossip

author.name: Tomas Ortega, Hamid Jafarkhani

entry.summary: DECO-EF is a decentralized parameter-free online convex optimization algorithm combining coin-betting predictions with compressed difference-based gossip over communication graphs. It removes the need for horizon- or scale-dependent learning rates while handling compressed-communication disagreement.

entry.title: PINE: Pruning Boosted Tree Ensembles with Conformal In-Distribution Prediction Equivalence

author.name: Haruki Yajima, Yusuke Matsui

entry.summary: PINE prunes boosted tree ensembles while guaranteeing prediction equivalence within a conformally-calibrated in-distribution region, controlled by a single parameter, balancing compression against decision consistency. It improves compression over fully-faithful pruning by restricting equivalence to where data actually lives.

entry.title: Meta-Attention: Bayesian Per-Token Routing for Efficient Transformer Inference

author.name: Alan Ferrari

entry.summary: Meta-Attention dynamically routes each token to full softmax, linear, or sliding-window attention via a Bayesian Meta-Controller treating per-token mechanism selection as posterior inference under a compute-aware Dirichlet prior. This enables adaptive, budget-aware efficient transformer inference.

entry.title: Latent Diffusion for Missing Data

author.name: Alberte Heering Estad, Ignacio Peis, Jes Frellsen

entry.summary: Investigates whether moving diffusion-based missing-data imputation from data space to a learned latent representation improves robustness under heavy MCAR corruption, using a two-stage robust-VAE-imputer plus latent diffusion framework. Shows latent diffusion maintains higher quality than pixel-space diffusion under incomplete training data.

entry.title: Counterfactually Fair Regression via Optimal Transport

author.name: M. Generali Lince, S. Gaucher, J-J. Vie, P. Loiseau

entry.summary: This paper develops a post-processing estimator for counterfactually fair regression using optimal transport, proving fairness equivalence to conditional demographic parity and providing finite-sample guarantees. It contributes theoretical fairness bounds for continuous latent variables.

entry.title: Beyond Lipschitz: Data-Driven Robustness via Discrete Modulus of Continuity

author.name: J\"urgen D\"olz, Michael Multerer, Michele Palma

entry.summary: This paper proposes a data-driven robustness framework based on the discrete modulus of continuity, a nonlinear generalization of Lipschitz continuity that evaluates regularity relative to the data distribution without needing model internals. It offers a finer architecture-agnostic robustness measure.

entry.title: Challenges in Explaining Pretrained Clinical Text Classifiers

author.name: Kristian Miok, Matej Klemen, Blaz \v{S}krlj, Marko Robnik \v{S}ikonja

entry.summary: This paper identifies core limitations of token-level and perturbation-based explanation methods like LIME and SHAP when applied to clinical text classification, showing overemphasis on non-informative tokens, attribution instability, and confident predictions on incoherent inputs. It argues for clinically meaningful, semantically grounded explanation strategies.

entry.title: Argument Quality Assessment with Large Language Models: A Pairwise Bradley-Terry Approach

author.name: Nicol\'as Benjam\'in Ocampo, Agnes Paullate Nyiranziza, Davide Ceolin

entry.summary: This paper evaluates 12 open-weight LLMs on argument quality assessment using pairwise comparisons fed into a Bradley-Terry model across logical, rhetorical, and dialectic dimensions. It finds moderate correlation with human expert judgments.

entry.title: ClinicalEncoder26AM: A Multlilingual Diagnosable ColBERT Model; Evidences from the MultiClinNER Shared Task

author.name: Fran\c{c}ois Remy

entry.summary: ClinicalEncoder26AM is a multilingual diagnosable ColBERT model for clinical and biomedical texts that aligns token-level semantics with a clinical latent space via multi-adapter distillation. It is evaluated on the MultiClinNER shared task as a BIO tagger.

entry.title: Fine-Tuning Vision-Language Models for Understanding Current Damage and Scoring Priority with Quality Guard Agent

author.name: Takato Yasuno

entry.summary: This paper fine-tunes LLaVA-1.5-7B with QLoRA on paired bridge damage images and inspection records to automate damage understanding and repair priority scoring. It targets inter-rater variability and aging engineer capacity in Japanese bridge inspection.

entry.title: DebFilter: Eradicating Biases Stashed in Value

author.name: Seung Hyuk Lee, Songkuk Kim

entry.summary: DebFilter is a training-free framework to mitigate social biases (gender, age) in text-to-image diffusion models by addressing biases encoded in CLIP text embeddings used for guidance. It aims to reduce skewed outputs without retraining.

entry.title: Learning to Label: A Reinforced Self-Evolving Framework for Semi-supervised Referring Expression Segmentation

author.name: Runlong Cao, Ying Zang, Chuanwei Zhou, Tianrun Chen, Tong Zhang, Zhen Cui, Chunyan Xu

entry.summary: Learning to Label (L2L) is a reinforced self-evolving framework for semi-supervised referring expression segmentation that treats pseudo-label construction as a learnable decision process. It uses an MLLM to extract semantic-spatial priors and reinforcement learning to stabilize training under limited annotation.

entry.title: Self-Supervised Online Robot-Agnostic Traversability Estimation for Open-World Environments

author.name: Julia Hindel, Simon Bultmann, Houman Masnavi, Daniele Cattaneo, Abhinav Valada

entry.summary: COTRATE is a self-supervised online learning framework for robot-agnostic traversability estimation in open-world environments, learning continuously from unlabeled multimodal robot experience. It infers robust traversability scores without handcrafted proprioceptive scores or offline clustering, with memory-efficient onboard deployment.

entry.title: VLM-Based Advanced Rider Assistance System for Motorcycle Safety

author.name: Mohamed Elnoor, Francesca Baldini, Ananya Trivedi, Faizan M. Tariq, Jovin D'sa, David Isele, Sangjae Bae, Dinesh Manocha, Yosuke Sakamoto

entry.summary: This paper proposes a VLM-based Advanced Rider Assistance System for motorcycle safety that uses vision-language models for contextual hazard reasoning combined with segmentation to build dense risk maps. The maps encode semantic and physical hazard attributes into per-pixel motorcycle-specific costs for risk-aware planning.

entry.title: Magnet-Based Soft Robotic Skin Using a 3D-Printed Multi-Lattice Structure and CNN-Based Tactile Super-Resolution

author.name: Yunseong Bang, Joowon Park, Suan Sim, Youngjun Ryu, Sukho Park, Kyungseo Park

entry.summary: This paper presents a magnet-based soft robotic skin combining a 3D-printed multi-lattice structure with distributed Hall-effect sensor arrays and a CNN-based tactile super-resolution model. The lattice spreads contact-induced magnetic changes to give overlapping receptive fields and large sensing coverage with few blind spots.

entry.title: Intelligence as Managed Autonomy: Failure, Escalation, and Governance for Agentic AI Systems

author.name: Srini Ramaswamy

entry.summary: Proposes a theory of managed autonomy where intelligent agentic behavior includes detecting epistemic drift, suspending reasoning, attempting recovery, and surrendering control when reliability drops, instantiated as the SMARt architecture. It addresses unbounded autonomy as an architectural vulnerability.

entry.title: GONDOR to the Rescue: Satisficing Planning with Low Memory

author.name: Yonatan Vernik, Alexander Tuisov, Alexander Shleyfman

entry.summary: GONDOR is a memory-efficient extension of Greedy Best-First Search that periodically compresses the search tree while retaining sparse anchor states, then reconstructs paths by re-searching, enabling planning under strict memory limits. It targets edge-device search applications.

entry.title: Trinity: Unifying Class-Agnostic Terrain and Semantic Segmentation for Unstructured Outdoor Environments by Leveraging Synthetic Data

author.name: Marcus G M\"uller, Wout Boerdijk, Maximilian Durner, Riccardo Giubilato, Abel Gawel, Wolfgang St\"urzl, Roland Siegwart, Rudolph Triebel

entry.summary: Trinity is a transformer-based architecture that jointly performs class-specific semantic segmentation and class-agnostic terrain segmentation for outdoor robots, leveraging synthetic data. It improves transferability across robot platforms without costly re-annotation.

entry.title: ChildEval: When large language models meet children's personalities

author.name: Yanyan Luo, Xue Han, Chunxu Zhao, Ruiqiao Bai, Yaxing Zhang, Qian Hu, Lijun Mei, Junlan Feng

entry.summary: ChildEval is a benchmark of 29K synthesized persona profiles of children aged 3-6 to evaluate LLMs' ability to infer and follow child-centered preferences in long-context conversations. Preferences are expressed explicitly or implicitly and may align with, conflict with, or be independent of the persona.

entry.title: SMILE-Next: Teaching Large Language Models to Detect, Classify, and Reason about Laughter

author.name: Lee Jung-Mok, Kim Sung-Bin, Joohyun Chang, Lee Hyun, Tae-Hyun Oh

entry.summary: SMILE-Next is a dataset and specialized LLM for real-world laughter understanding across detection, type classification, and reasoning, with multimodal textual representations and QA annotations. It introduces laughter-specific Self-Instruct and a Mixture-of-Laughter approach.

entry.title: ProRL: Effective Reinforcement Learning for Proactive Recommendation via Rectified Policy Gradient Estimation

author.name: Hongru Hou, Tiehua Mei, Denghui Geng, Jinhui Huang, Ao Xu, Hengrui Chen, Jiaqing Liang, Deqing Yang

entry.summary: ProRL identifies and corrects two deficiencies in policy gradient estimation for proactive recommender systems that guide users toward target items via intermediate recommendation paths. It proposes a rectified policy gradient that removes length-dependent bias and respects reward decomposition structure.

entry.title: Online Irregular Multivariate Time Series Forecasting via Uncertainty-Driven Dual-Expert Calibration

author.name: Haonan Wen, Hanyang Chen, Songhe Feng

entry.summary: This work studies online irregular multivariate time series forecasting and proposes an uncertainty-driven dual-expert calibration method to handle dynamic distribution shifts and evolving missingness patterns. It addresses the breakdown of temporal continuity and periodicity assumptions during online deployment.

entry.title: BIRDNet: Mining and Encoding Boolean Implication Knowledge Graphs as Interpretable Deep Neural Networks

author.name: Tirtharaj Dash

entry.summary: BIRDNet mines Boolean implication relationships between feature pairs in tabular data via a sparse-exception binomial test, forming a typed directed graph equivalent to a 2-literal clause rule base, and encodes it as a sparse, interpretable layered neural network. Each hidden unit corresponds to one mined rule binding only its two features, yielding sparsity and interpretability by construction.

entry.title: NUCLEUS-MoE: Unified Model of Pool Boiling for Liquid Cooling

author.name: Arthur Feeney, Xianwei Zou, Sheikh Md Shakeel Hassan, Siddhartha Rachabathuni, Aparna Chandramowlishwaran

entry.summary: NUCLEUS is a mixture-of-experts surrogate model unifying pool-boiling heat-transfer prediction across fluids and conditions, replacing collections of specialized surrogates. It combines neighborhood attention, signed-distance-field interface handling, and emergent expert specialization.

entry.title: CAREF: Calibration-Aware Regularization for Explanation Faithfulness Without Rationale Supervision

author.name: Naphat Nithisopa, Teerapong Panboonyuen

entry.summary: CAREF is a parameter-efficient fine-tuning framework that jointly optimizes predictive accuracy and explanation faithfulness via calibration-aware regularization with token-level sparsity, without rationale supervision. It outperforms LoRA/AdaLoRA on natural language explanation benchmarks using few trainable parameters.

entry.title: Conveyance: A Versatile Framework for Learning in Structured Class Spaces

author.name: Yasser Taha, Gr\'egoire Montavon, Nils K\"orber

entry.summary: Conveyance is a classification framework and loss function tailored to structured class spaces, letting users encode graph-like relations between classes without defining complex joint distributions or tuning utility matrices, by maximizing two separate margins. It aims to exploit structural relationships under structured noise where symmetric losses like cross-entropy fail.

entry.title: Neural Quantum Spectral Operator Learning for Solving Partial Differential Equations

author.name: Chanyoung Kim, Myeonghwan Seong, Yujin Kim, Daniel K. Park, Youngjoon Hong

entry.summary: Proposes NVQLS, a hybrid quantum-classical operator learning framework using the Legendre-Galerkin weak formulation to solve parametric PDEs, resolving a sign ambiguity in variational quantum linear solver energy minimization. It reduces data dependency of operator learning.

entry.title: On the Equivariant Learning of the $Q$-tensor Order Parameter

author.name: Julia Navarro, Mark Wilkinson

entry.summary: Constructs group-equivariant neural networks for predicting the two-dimensional Q-tensor order parameter of nematic liquid crystals from synthetic microscopic textures. Seven architectures equivariant to cyclic groups of increasing order are evaluated.

entry.title: Bridging Maximum Likelihood and Optimal Transport for Efficient Inference and Model Selection in Stochastic Block Models

author.name: Simon Queric, C\'edric Vincent-Cuaz, Charles Bouveyron, Marco Corneli

entry.summary: This paper connects maximum likelihood variational inference in stochastic block models to semi-relaxed Gromov-Wasserstein projection, and studies unregularized estimators that consistently recover cluster structure. It also addresses model selection in finite samples.

entry.title: AREA: Attribute Extraction and Aggregation for CLIP-Based Class-Incremental Learning

author.name: Zhen-Hao Xie, Yu-Cheng Shi, Da-Wei Zhou

entry.summary: AREA improves CLIP-based class-incremental learning by decomposing classification into attribute extraction and aggregation stages, enabling the model to extract new attributes and adjust their aggregation when learning new classes. It addresses catastrophic forgetting in continual learning.

entry.title: An Evolutionary Approach for Designing Stable and Highly Expressible Low-Immunogenicity Therapeutic mRNA Sequences

author.name: Dhawa Sang Dong, Mausam Gurung, Suraj Kandel

entry.summary: This work presents a two-stage in-silico framework for therapeutic mRNA design, using a pretrained CodonTransformer to generate biologically coherent sequences and a genetic algorithm to evolve them via codon-aware crossover and synonymous mutation. It optimizes for translation efficiency, stability, and low immunogenicity.

entry.title: Prompting Is All You Need: Multi-view Prompting Large Language Models for Aspect-Based Sentiment Analysis

author.name: Nils Constantin Hellwig, Niklas Donhauser, Jakob Fehle, Udo Kruschwitz, Christian Wolff

entry.summary: LLM-MvP adapts the multi-view principle of considering multiple element orderings to LLM prompting for aspect-based sentiment analysis, combining schema-constrained decoding with context-free grammar and prefix batching. It achieves performance competitive with fine-tuned approaches via prompting alone.

entry.title: From Affect to Complex Behavior: Advancing Multimodal Human-Centered AI at the 10th ABAW Workshop & Competition

author.name: Dimitrios Kollias, Panagiotis Tzirakis, Alan Cowen, Stefanos Zafeiriou, Irene Kotsia, Eric Granger, Marco Pedersoli, Simon Bacon, Jens Madsen, Soufiane Belharbi, Muhammad Haseeb Aslam, Chunchang Shao, Guanyu Hu

entry.summary: This is a workshop and competition report for the 10th ABAW at CVPR 2026, covering affect estimation, expression and action unit recognition, and complex behavior tasks like violence detection and ambivalence recognition. It advances multimodal human-centered AI in unconstrained settings.

entry.title: A self-supervised learning approach to deep filter banks for texture recognition

author.name: Joao B. Florindo, Lucas O. Lyra, Antonio E. Fabris

entry.summary: This work proposes a self-supervised pretraining approach using masked autoencoders for deep filter banks in texture recognition, arguing that compact local information makes lighter architectures viable than vision transformers. It addresses limited training data in real-world texture applications.

entry.title: LV-OSD: Language-Vision-Complementary Open-Set Object Detection

author.name: Yupeng Zhang, Ruize Han, Wei Feng, Song Wang, Liang Wan

entry.summary: LV-OSD introduces language-vision-complementary open-set object detection that accepts flexible text and/or image prompts to specify desired categories. It proposes a dual-branch framework with multi-modal prompts to bridge semantic gaps for practical detection.

entry.title: EntroAD: Structural Entropy-Guided Prompt Adaptation for Zero-Shot Anomaly Detection

author.name: Xinyu Zhao, Qingyun Sun, Jiayi Luo, Jianxin Li

entry.summary: EntroAD is a structural entropy-guided framework for zero-shot anomaly detection using CLIP, introducing a dynamic routing mechanism to process heterogeneous anomaly types via multiple adaptation pathways. It addresses the insufficiency of single-pathway adaptation across domains.

entry.title: SCALE-COMM: Shared, Contrastively-Aligned Latent Embeddings for MARL Communication

author.name: Mahmoud Abouelyazid, Eman Hammad

entry.summary: SCALE-COMM is a self-supervised framework for emergent communication in multi-agent reinforcement learning, learning compact, stable, policy-relevant latent messages via contrastive alignment. It decouples communication learning from policy optimization to avoid interference and ungrounded semantics.

entry.title: S-Cheetah: A Novel Quadrupedal Robot with a 3-DOF Active Spine Learning Agile Locomotion

author.name: Zimu Li, Weibang Bai

entry.summary: S-Cheetah is a quadrupedal robot with a 3-DOF bio-inspired serial active spine capable of spatial tri-axial rotation, paired with learned agile locomotion. It addresses prior designs that reduce spinal DOF and fail to replicate biological tri-axial spine motion.

entry.title: Mag-VLA: Vision-Language-Action Model for Bimanual Magnetically Actuated Microrobot Manipulation

author.name: Yongchen Wang, Kangyi Lu, Lan Wei, Dandan Zhang

entry.summary: Mag-VLA is a vision-language-action model for bimanual magnetically actuated microrobot manipulation, using two robotic arms with mounted magnets to create dynamic fields enabling tasks like microrobot reorientation. It addresses coupled control challenges of coordinating two actuators for indirect microscale actuation.

entry.title: Announcing Geodesic Research

author.name: Puria

entry.summary: Announces Geodesic Research, a Cambridge UK non-profit AI safety org focused on building robustly-aligned initializations for capable LLMs, arguing long-horizon capabilities RL is a critical and hard-to-remove source of misalignment. It outlines a research agenda around alignment pretraining that persists through post-training.

entry.title: Cyberbullying Governance on Social Media: A Unified Framework from Content Identification to Intervention

author.name: Yiting Huang, Wenting Zhu, Zekun Wang, Qingpo Yang, Yakai Chen, Zihui Xu, Yueyue Zhang, Sanchuan Guo, Xi Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes a unified full-lifecycle framework for cyberbullying governance on social media spanning content identification, behavioral dynamics, structural diffusion, and proactive intervention. It moves beyond passive post-level detection toward end-to-end mitigation.

entry.title: Auditable Decision Models with Learned Abstention and Real-Time Steering

author.name: Sankaranarayanan Palamadai Chandrasekaran

entry.summary: Presents EvaluatorDPT, a bounded decision-control model that outputs YES, NO, or a learned TBD deferral outcome, enabling auditable, policy-governed abstention and real-time steering under uncertainty. It treats uncertainty as explicitly routable rather than hidden in forced predictions.

entry.title: Picid: A Modular Evaluation Infrastructure for Reproducible PHM Across Tasks and Domains

author.name: Lev Telyatnikov, Raffael Theiler, Leandro Von Krannichfeldt, Olga Fink

entry.summary: Picid is a modular, reproducible evaluation infrastructure for Prognostics and Health Management that formalizes data splits, preprocessing, and metrics into an executable leakage-safe protocol. It addresses pervasive reproducibility gaps in PHM benchmarking.

entry.title: Modeling Vehicle-Type-Specific Pedestrian Crash Avoidance Behavior in Safety-Critical Interactions Using Smooth-Mamba Deep Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Qingwen Pu, Kun Xie, Hong Yang, Di Yang, Junqing Wang

entry.summary: This study uses a Smooth-Mamba Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient framework to model vehicle-type-specific pedestrian crash-avoidance behavior, extracting safety-critical interactions involving automated and human-driven vehicles from real driving data. It supports safe deployment of automated driving.

entry.title: Short-Term Gain, Long-Term Fragility: AI Labor Substitution and the Erosion of Sustainable Capability

author.name: Wolfgang Rohde

entry.summary: This paper develops a mechanism of capability masking and erosion under AI labor substitution, arguing that short-term productivity gains from replacing human labor draw down slow-to-build human capabilities, creating long-term organizational fragility. It frames AI substitution as a burden transfer to the future.

entry.title: Cultural Fidelity in English-to-Hindi Translation: A Preservation-Fluency Frontier for Gender Recoverability

author.name: Samyak Savi, Chavi Gupta, Shreyas Gantayet, Tanay Sodha, Dhruv Kumar

entry.summary: This work studies cultural fidelity in English-to-Hindi translation, focusing on whether gender cues remain recoverable after translation. It introduces a 37K-instance benchmark and two inference-time interventions to preserve gender encoding through ergative and honorific constructions.

entry.title: Disentangling Adversarial Prompts: A Semantic-Graph Defense for Robust LLM Security

author.name: Xiang Fang, Wanlong Fang

entry.summary: The Adversarial Prompt Disentanglement framework defends LLMs against jailbreaking and prompt injection by using mutual-information-based semantic decomposition and a semantic graph to isolate and neutralize malicious prompt components before processing. It aims to proactively detect adversarial elements.

entry.title: Thermodynamic properties of chemically disordered compounds via AI-driven estimation of partition function with the PULSE method

author.name: Baptiste Bernard, Luca Messina, Eiji Kawasaki, Emeric Bourasseau

entry.summary: This article presents an improved PULSE method that uses generative unsupervised learning to estimate the partition function and thermodynamic properties of chemically disordered compounds, reducing Monte Carlo computational cost. It validates on the 2D Ising model showing high precision and efficiency.

entry.title: Preference-Shaped Expected Hypervolume and R2 Improvement: Exact Computation and Monotonicity

author.name: Michael T. M. Emmerich

entry.summary: This paper studies preference-shaped expected improvement criteria for Bayesian multiobjective optimization, comparing the hypervolume indicator (dystopian reference) and R2 indicator (utopian point, Tchebycheff scalarization). It precisely characterizes which preference transformations preserve exact computation, Pareto compatibility, and monotonicity.

entry.title: SYNAPSE: Neuro-Symbolic Visual Thought-to-Text Decoding via Topological Semantic Denoising

author.name: Akshaj Murhekar, Abhijit Mishra

entry.summary: SYNAPSE is a neuro-symbolic framework for EEG-to-imagined-text decoding that stabilizes generation against biological noise using commonsense graph structure and latent exemplars as inference-time symbolic regularization. It reduces hallucinations in frozen language models driven by corrupted neural signals.

entry.title: Patched-DeltaNet: Token-Level Event-Driven Memory for Linear-Time Anomaly Detection

author.name: Tae-Gyun Lee, Junyoung Park, Kyu Won Han

entry.summary: Patched-DeltaNet combines time-series patching with gated delta networks to achieve linear-time anomaly detection, claiming emergent token-level event-driven memory that updates recurrent state only on significant deltas. It targets resource-constrained deployment versus quadratic transformer detectors.

entry.title: Hierarchical Synthetic Tabular Data Generation: A Hybrid Top-Down and Bottom-Up Framework

author.name: Junfeng Nie, Alvin Jin, Xiaohui Chen

entry.summary: H-TDBU is a hierarchical hybrid framework for synthetic tabular data combining a top-down path enforcing logical constraints and cross-modal alignment with a bottom-up path of lightweight generators learning local statistics, consolidated with iterative feedback. It addresses heterogeneity, logical consistency, and rare-event coverage in low-data regimes.

entry.title: Zero-shot Quantum Neural Architecture Search

author.name: Tung Dao, Son Tran, Huynh Thi Thanh Binh

entry.summary: Proposes a zero-shot surrogate metric for quantum neural architecture search by identifying convergence of the Quantum Neural Tangent Kernel Gram matrix, avoiding costly repeated circuit training. This cuts the high computational cost of evolutionary quantum architecture search.

entry.title: Triangular-Reference Schr\"odinger Bridges for Time Series Generation

author.name: Gabriele Bocchi

entry.summary: Introduces Triangular-Reference Schrodinger Bridges for time series generation, replacing the Brownian reference with an intervalwise frozen, possibly degenerate diffusion reference triangular across latent volatility levels. It preserves the variational entropy-projection core of the SBTS framework.

entry.title: Resolution-free neural surrogates for geometric parameterization and mapping with spatially varying fields

author.name: Yanwen Huang, Lok Ming Lui, Gary P. T. Choi

entry.summary: This paper proposes resolution-free neural surrogates for geometric parameterization and mapping problems involving spatially varying fields, replacing repeated expensive PDE solves. It targets imaging tasks like registration and distortion correction.

entry.title: Personality, Role, and Expressive Style in Large Language Models: An Interactionist Analysis

author.name: Moe Nagao, Koichiro Terao, Mikio Nakano, Naoto Iwahashi

entry.summary: This paper analyzes personality expression in LLM dialogue from an interactionist perspective, showing that specifying Big Five traits in prompts does not ensure their expression, which depends on dialogue roles and expressive styles. It uses a factorial design across personality, role, and style conditions.

entry.title: ConvMemory: A Lightweight Learned Memory Reranker, a Negative Attribution Result, and a Research-Preview Conflict Editor

author.name: Taiheng Pan

entry.summary: ConvMemory is a lightweight 3.6M-parameter learned reranker for conversational long-term memory retrieval, trained with cross-encoder teacher supervision, achieving competitive recall at 12-117x lower latency. The paper also reports a rigorous negative attribution result and a research-preview conflict editor.

entry.title: CuriosAI Submission to the CASTLE Challenge at EgoVis 2026

author.name: Yuto Kanda, Hayato Tanoue, Takayuki Hori

entry.summary: This is a competition submission to the CASTLE Challenge at EgoVis 2026, answering questions over 600+ hours of synchronized multi-view egocentric video using a search-verify-answer pipeline and a temporal-multimodal knowledge graph approach. It includes anti-confabulation rules and evidence-priority fusion.

entry.title: Transfer learning RGB models to hyperspectral images with trainable tensor decompositions

author.name: Mariette Sch\"onfeld, Laurens Devos, Wannes Meert, Hendrik Blockeel

entry.summary: This work proposes transferring RGB-pretrained vision networks to hyperspectral imagery using partially trainable tensor decompositions of convolutional filters, separating spatial and spectral components. The spectral components are replaced with trainable ones to preserve both image and model information.

entry.title: Sketch2Motion: Text-driven 2D Sketch to 3D Animation via Diffusion-guided Skeleton Optimization

author.name: Gaurav Rai, Ojaswa Sharma

entry.summary: Sketch2Motion is a diffusion-guided framework that converts text and 2D hand-drawn sketches into 3D animations via skeleton-based motion synthesis combined with classical animation pipelines. It handles occlusions and motion mapping beyond prior approaches limited to specific motion types.

entry.title: ICAN-Deploy: Identity-Stable Canary Deployment for Safety-Critical Embodied Agents

author.name: Xue Qin, Simin Luan, John See, Zeyd Boukhers, Cong Yang, Zhijun Li

entry.summary: ICAN-Deploy is an identity-stable canary deployment middleware for safety-critical embodied agents that holds the cryptographic identity hash invariant across the canary window by separating frozen capability names from mutable versions. It avoids re-certification per canary that mainstream rollout controllers force.

entry.title: Accelerating Robot Path Planning via Connectivity-Preserving Region Proposal Network

author.name: Zhanzheng Ma, Cancan Zhao, Shuai Zhang, Bo Ouyang

entry.summary: CP-RPN is a segmentation-guided region proposal network for mobile robot path planning that predicts compact, topologically connected candidate regions to compress the search space. It uses a Deformable Attention Transformer for global connectivity and a deconvolutional decoder for fine spatial detail.

entry.title: Agyn: An Open-Source Platform for AI Agents with Scalable On-Demand Execution, Agent Definition as a Code, and Zero-Trust Access

author.name: Nikita Benkovich, Vitalii Valkov

entry.summary: Presents Agyn, an open-source platform for deploying AI agents at scale with a stateful serverless Kubernetes runtime, agent-definition-as-code via Terraform, and zero-trust least-privilege security. It targets production operational challenges of agent governance and isolation.

entry.title: FundaPod: A Multi-Persona Agent Pod Platform with Knowledge Graph Memory for AI-Assisted Fundamental Investment Research

author.name: Di Zhu (Nico), Lei (Nico), Zheng, Zihan Chen

entry.summary: Presents FundaPod, a multi-persona agent platform with knowledge-graph memory for AI-assisted fundamental investment research, framing the task as transparent, reusable, verifiable decision-support rather than prediction. It supports evidence gathering, viewpoint comparison, and investment memo generation.

entry.title: The Illusion of Opting in AI-Mediated Consequential Decisions

author.name: Eugene Yu Ji

entry.summary: This conceptual paper argues that AI systems create an illusion of opting, where people appear to have meaningful consequential choices while their genuine agency is eroded. It proposes evaluating AI by whether it protects a scaffolded meta-capacity for choosing.

entry.title: OpenURMA: A Clean-Room Open Implementation of the Unified Bus Protocol

author.name: Bojie Li

entry.summary: OpenURMA is a clean-room open implementation of Huawei's Unified Bus protocol, which decouples per-application endpoint state from per-host transport state to overcome RDMA NIC bottlenecks at high application fanout. It addresses datacenter networking abstractions rather than core AI methods.

entry.title: Agentic Literacy Debt: A Structural Problem the AI Literacy Field Has Not Yet Named

author.name: Rohith Nama

entry.summary: This conceptual paper names agentic literacy debt, the accumulating societal deficit when autonomous AI agents are deployed at scale without corresponding literacy infrastructure for delegated, opaque, irreversible decisions. It argues existing AI literacy frameworks lack vocabulary for delegation.

entry.title: Supervised Distributional Reduction via Optimal Transport and Dependence Maximization

author.name: Sai-Aakash Ramesh, Archit Sood, Andrew Corbett, Tim Dodwell

entry.summary: Supervised Distributional Reduction (SDR) combines optimal transport with explicit dependence maximization to learn target-aware compressed representations. It builds on Fused Gromov-Wasserstein to balance compression with predictive fidelity.

entry.title: QuITE: Query-Based Irregular Time Series Embedding

author.name: JungHoon Lim

entry.summary: QuITE proposes a plug-and-play input embedding for irregular multivariate time series that lets existing regular time-series models work without interpolation distortions. It identifies that the embedding layer, not the backbone, is the key bottleneck for irregular sampling.

entry.title: A Fresh Look at Lamarckian Evolution and the Baldwin Effect

author.name: In\`es Benito, Johannes F. Lutzeyer, Benjamin Doerr

entry.summary: This work revisits Lamarckian and Baldwinian evolution with modern empirical and theoretical methods, comparing them rigorously to Darwinian evolution on Maximum Independent Set and Maximum Cut problems from the GraphBench benchmark. It finds local-search-augmented evolutionary algorithms consistently outperform plain Darwinian evolution.

entry.title: T-GINEE: A Tensor-Based Multilayer Graph Representation Learning

author.name: Maolin Wang, Ziting Mai, Xuhui Chen, Zhiqi Li, Tianshuo Wei, Yutian Xiao, Wenlin Zhang, Wanyu Wang, Ruocheng Guo, Haoxuan Li, Zenglin Xu, Xiangyu Zhao
