entry.summary: IBM Research penetration testing study on large-scale proprietary agent systems, finding many vulnerabilities reflect recurring weakness classes from prior computing systems. Examines proprietary agents beyond prior open-source focus.

entry.title: RLVR Datasets and Where to Find Them: Tracing Data Lineage for Better Training Data

author.name: Hsiu-Yuan Huang, Weijie Liu, Chenming Tang, Sanwoo Lee, Kai Yang, Yangkun Chen, Saiyong Yang, Yunfang Wu

entry.summary: Introduces ATLAS, a framework that traces RLVR datasets back to atomic sources, attributing 99.7% of 1.45M instances to just 20 atomic sources. Reveals shared upstream lineage and data contamination risks, motivating a new dataset DAPO++.

entry.title: Your Agents Are Aging Too: Agent Lifespan Engineering for Deployed Systems

author.name: Jianing Zhu, Yeonju Ro, John Robertson, Kevin Wang, Junbo Li, Haris Vikalo, Aditya Akella, Zhangyang Wang

entry.summary: AgingBench is a longitudinal reliability benchmark measuring how deployed AI agents degrade over time even with frozen weights, through compressed history, growing memory stores, fact revisions, and maintenance. Introduces the concept of agent lifespan engineering.

entry.title: MemFail: Stress-Testing Failure Modes of LLM Memory Systems

author.name: Ishir Garg, Neel Kolhe, Dawn Song, Xuandong Zhao

entry.summary: MemFail is a diagnostic benchmark that decomposes LLM memory systems into summarization, storage, and retrieval operations to isolate specific failure modes rather than treating memory as a black box. From Dawn Song's group at Berkeley.

entry.title: Composition Collapse: Stable Factual Knowledge Does Not Imply Compositional Reasoning

author.name: Zhe Yu, Wenpeng Xing, Yunzhao Wei, Jie Chen, Hongzhi Wang, Xuyang Teng, Meng Han

entry.summary: Demonstrates composition collapse: post-training recipes with statistically indistinguishable atomic knowledge can produce composition behavior separated by over 40 percentage points, showing stable factual knowledge does not imply compositional reasoning. Proposes double-gate evaluation protocol.

entry.title: A Universal Cliff and a Design Fingerprint: Cross-Section Defect Detection Under LLM Orchestration

author.name: Hiroki Fukui

entry.summary: Empirical study finding a universal detection cliff: every tested LLM that detects cross-section document defects under a single-agent configuration loses two-thirds or more of that ability under multi-agent orchestration. Tests ten systems across five generations and providers.

entry.title: Workflow Closure Is Not Scientific Closure in Auto-Research Systems

author.name: Shuai Wang, Xinyuan Tian, Pangpang Liu, Yize Zhao

entry.summary: Position paper arguing that workflow closure in auto-research systems does not constitute scientific closure, surveying 100+ papers and auditing 21 systems to diagnose recurring failure patterns. Advocates autonomous execution under non-autonomous epistemic control.

entry.title: Quantized Keys Steal Attention: Bias Correction for KV-Cache Compression in Video Diffusion

author.name: Tuna Tuncer, Felix Becker, Thomas Pfeil

entry.summary: Identifies a Jensen bias caused by softmax convexity in KV-cache quantization for video diffusion, where quantized keys steal attention mass from unquantized current chunks. Derives a per-attention-score correction that removes the bias in expectation.

entry.title: E$^3$C: Video Generation with 3D Environmental Memory and Ego-Exo Human Pose Control

author.name: Qiao Gu, Lingni Ma, Adam W Harley, Richard Newcombe, Florian Shkurti, Julian Straub

entry.summary: E3C is a controllable egocentric video diffusion framework that disentangles persistent 3D scene structure (environmental memory) from human-driven dynamics (ego-exo pose control). Authored by researchers including Adam Harley and Richard Newcombe of Meta Reality Labs.

entry.title: VisualNeedle: Benchmarking Active Visual Search in Information-Dense Scenes

author.name: Jingru Chen, Yiming Liu, Mingtao Chen, Sijie Chen, Richeng Xuan, Liang Yang, Zhichao Hu, Fanyang Lu

entry.summary: VisualNeedle benchmarks active visual search in information-dense scenes, exposing shortcuts (linguistic priors, coarse global semantics, tool-image corruption insensitivity) that inflate MLLM scores on fine-grained perception benchmarks. Probes whether high accuracy reflects faithful visual evidence use.

entry.title: Credit-assigned Policy Gradient for Early Stage Retrieval in Two-stage Ranking

author.name: Haruka Kiyohara, Mihaela Curmei, Ariel Evnine, Shankar Kalyanaraman, Israel Nir, Ana-Roxana Pop, Nitzan Razin, Sarah Dean, Thorsten Joachims, Udi Weinsberg

entry.summary: Credit-assigned policy gradient method for training early-stage rankers in two-stage retrieval/RAG architectures, addressing exploding variance of vanilla policy gradient when candidate sets are large. From a strong group including Thorsten Joachims and Meta researchers.

entry.title: Efficient On-policy Visual-RL via Stochastic Decoupled Policy Gradient

author.name: Haoxiang You, Yilang Liu, Davis Zong, Qian Wang, Teeratham Vitchutripop, Qi Wang, Daniel Rakita, Ian Abraham

entry.summary: SDPG is a lightweight visual RL method using stochastic policy gradients via random perturbations of trajectory rollouts, training visuomotor policies on a single RTX 4080 in hours with orders of magnitude less batch rendering. Includes visual robotics benchmarks and sim-to-real demonstrations.

entry.title: Beyond Trajectory-Level Attribution: Graph-Based Credit Assignment for Agentic Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Xin Cheng, Shuo He, Lang Feng, HaiYang Xu, Ming Yan, Lei Feng, Bo An

entry.summary: GraphGPO aggregates rollout trajectories into a state-transition graph and estimates step-level credit using distance to task goal. Improves on coarse trajectory-level attribution in agentic RL.

entry.title: Ratio-Variance Regularized Policy Optimization

author.name: Yu Luo, Shuo Han, Yihan Hu, Lei Lv, Huaping Liu, Fuchun Sun, Jianye Hao, Dong Li

entry.summary: R2VPO replaces hard PPO clipping with explicit policy ratio variance constraints as a principled local trust-region approximation. Acts as a soft brake preserving high-divergence updates while down-weighting stale data.

entry.title: Negligible in Size, Significant in Effect: On Scale Vectors in Large Language Models

author.name: Mingze Wang, Shuchen Zhu, Yuxin Fang, Binghui Li, Kai Shen, Shu Zhong

entry.summary: Systematic study of scale vectors in LLM normalization layers showing they are crucial for optimization despite being a tiny parameter fraction. Theoretical analysis reveals self-acceleration mechanism in Pre-Norm architectures.

entry.title: Tournament-GRPO: Group-Wise Tournament Rewards for Reinforcement Learning in Open-Ended Long-Form Generation

author.name: Zixuan Yang, Yiqun Chen, Wei Yang, Erhan Zhang, Zihan Shen, Xiaochi Wei, Yan Gao, Yi Wu, Yao Hu, Jiaxin Mao

entry.summary: Tournament-GRPO converts pointwise rubric-based judging into tournament-style relative rewards for open-ended long-form generation. Addresses calibration weaknesses in absolute scoring for RL on subjective tasks.

entry.title: Less is More: Early Stopping Rollout for On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Zhou Ziheng, Jiaqi Li, Huacong Tang, Ying Nian Wu, Demetri Terzopoulos

entry.summary: Identifies Off-policy Teacher Decay in on-policy distillation, where teacher's corrective ability degrades on student's off-policy context. Proposes Early Stopping Rollout as simple fix limiting rollout length.

entry.title: Tracing Computation Density in LLMs

author.name: Corentin Kervadec, Iuliia Lysova, Iuri Macocco, Marco Baroni, Gemma Boleda

entry.summary: s-Trace method efficiently estimates the minimal subgraph approximating full LLM output, revealing two-phase computation organization with early-layer head approximation followed by later-layer refinement. Mechanistic interpretability work.

entry.title: Two Speeds of Learning: A Representation-Readout Decomposition of Grokking and Double Descent

author.name: Chi-Ning Chou, Oscar Uzdelewicz, Neng-Chun Chiu, Yao-Yuan Yang, SueYeon Chung

entry.summary: Analyzes grokking and double descent through representation-readout decomposition, identifying two competing learning processes in encoder vs final classifier. Provides task-agnostic framework for these training phenomena.

entry.title: Pair-In, Pair-Out: Latent Multi-Token Prediction for Efficient LLMs

author.name: Wenhui Tan, Minghao Li, Xiaoqian Ma, Siqi Fan, Xiusheng Huang, Liujie Zhang, Ruihua Song, Weihang Chen

entry.summary: PIPO unifies latent input compression with multi-token prediction by treating them as mirror-image fold/unfold operations, eliminating the need for expensive verifier passes in speculative decoding. Targets autoregressive decoding cost in long chain-of-thought reasoning.

entry.title: FineVLA: Fine-Grained Instruction Alignment for Steerable Vision-Language-Action Policies

author.name: Xintong Hu, Xuhong Huang, Jinyu Zhang, Yutong Yao, Yuchong Sun, Qiuyue Wang, Mingsheng Li, Sicheng Xie, Yitao Liu, Junhao Chen, Yixuan Chen, Yingming Zheng, Shuai Bai, Tao Yu

entry.summary: FineVLA provides action-aligned fine-grained instruction supervision for vision-language-action robot policies, with a unified data tool aggregating 972K trajectories and a human-verified dataset of 47K fine-grained samples. Aims to enable steerable policies that follow execution-critical details.

entry.title: Guiding LLM Post-training Data Engineering with Model Internals from Sparse Autoencoders

author.name: Yi Jing, Zao Dai, Jinwu Hu, Zijun Yao, Lei Hou, Juanzi Li, Xiaozhi Wang

entry.summary: SAERL uses sparse autoencoder features as intrinsic signals for engineering RL post-training data, enabling SAE-space clustering for diversity, difficulty curriculum ordering, and quality probing. Bridges mechanistic interpretability with data engineering for RL.

entry.title: AirCast-SR: A Foundation Model for Kilometer-Scale Atmospheric Super-Resolution via Latent Consistency Diffusion

author.name: Somnath Luitel, Manmeet Singh, Joshua Durkee, Abdullah Al Fahad, Naveen Sudharsan, Prabhjot Singh, Cenlin He, Harsh Kamath, Zong-Liang Yang, Krishnagopal Halder, Sandeep Juneja, Parthasarathi Mukhopadhyay, Saptarishi Dhanuka, Amit Kumar Srivastava

entry.summary: AirCast-SR is a foundation model for atmospheric super-resolution downscaling AI weather forecasts from ~28 km to 1 km resolution at hourly intervals over the contiguous US. Uses a 3D U-Net within a Latent Consistency Model diffusion framework.

entry.title: ARBITER: Reasoning Trajectory Basins and Majority Vote Failures in Test-Time Sampling

author.name: Meng Cai, Lars Kulik, Farhana Choudhury

entry.summary: ARBITER analyzes LLM test-time sampling and shows reasoning trajectories cluster into basins, causing wrong-majority failures where correct answers are present but outvoted. Proposes a model-agnostic correction using hidden states and derived evidence.

entry.title: Stateful Inference for Low-Latency Multi-Agent Tool Calling

author.name: Victor Norgren

entry.summary: A stateful inference architecture for multi-agent tool calling that converts per-turn cost from O(n) to O(delta) by maintaining persistent KV caches across turns and combining radix prefix caching with prompt-lookup speculative decoding. Benchmarked against vLLM and SGLang.

entry.title: Balancing Plasticity and Stability with Fast and Slow Successor Features

author.name: Raymond Chua, Doina Precup, Blake Richards

entry.summary: Studies plasticity-stability tradeoffs in deep RL under continual gradual drift in modified Miniworld and MuJoCo environments, proposing fast and slow successor features. From Doina Precup and Blake Richards groups at McGill/Mila.

entry.title: Amortized Factor Inference Networks for Posterior Inference

author.name: Joohwan Ko, Justin Domke

entry.summary: AFINs are encode-merge-decode amortized inference networks built on dimension-independent modules that map model specifications and observations to variational posterior parameters. A single trained AFIN reportedly matches NUTS-level posterior accuracy across varying priors and likelihoods.

entry.title: Extra-Merge: Tracing the Rank-1 Subspace of Model Merging in Language Model Pre-Training

author.name: Wenjie Zhou, Bohan Wang, Hongtao Zhang, Chenxi Jia, Wei Chen, Xueqi Cheng

entry.summary: Identifies a Rank-1 Subspace phenomenon where consecutive merged checkpoints in late-stage LLM pretraining collapse onto a one-dimensional manifold despite oscillating raw optimization steps. Proposes Extra-Merge that extrapolates along this subspace as a training-free improvement strategy.

entry.title: The Stability of Singular Distribution: A Spectral Perspective on the Two-Phase Dynamics of Language Model Pre-training

author.name: Hongtao Zhang, Wenjie Zhou, Chenxi Jia, Wei Chen, Xueqi Cheng

entry.summary: Identifies Stability of Singular Distribution as a spectral phenomenon underlying the two-phase loss curve in LLM pretraining, where the trace-normalized singular spectrum stabilizes early. Proves that growing weight norms inevitably trigger this transition.

entry.title: Beyond Pairwise Preferences: Listwise Reward-Aware Alignment for Diffusion Models

author.name: Austin Wang, Jiaqi Han, Stefano Ermon, Yisong Yue

entry.summary: Diffusion LAIR replaces binary pairwise preference reduction with listwise reward-aware optimization for text-to-image diffusion, converting reward scores into centered advantage weights across candidate groups. From Stanford including Stefano Ermon and Yisong Yue.

entry.title: Near-Optimal Regret in Adversarial Kernel Bandits

author.name: Yu-Jie Zhang, Hao Qiu, Jonathan Scarlett, Kevin Jamieson

entry.summary: Provides near-optimal regret bounds of order sqrt(T d*(lambda) log|X|) for adversarial kernel bandits via exponential weights with regularized importance-weighted estimators. Matches stochastic kernel bandit rates up to log factors.

entry.title: Latent Recurrent Transformer: Architecture Exploration, Training Strategies, and Scaling Behavior

author.name: Zeyi Huang, Xuehai He, LiLiang Ren, Yiping Wang, Baolin Peng, Hao Cheng, Shuohang Wang, Pengcheng He, Jianfeng Gao, Yong Jae Lee, Yelong Shen

entry.summary: Introduces Latent Recurrent Transformer (LRT) which reuses hidden states from previous tokens as recurrent memory across positions, with an interleaved parallel training scheme to avoid sequential unrolling. Preserves standard attention and KV-cache interfaces.

entry.title: SEC-bench Pro: Can Language Models Solve Long-Horizon Software Security Tasks?

author.name: Hwiwon Lee, Jiawei Liu, Dongjun Kim, Ziqi Zhang, Chunqiu Steven Xia, Lingming Zhang

entry.summary: Presents SEC-bench Pro, a benchmark of 183 validated vulnerabilities across V8 and other systems for measuring LLM agent bug hunting capabilities. Uses a three-phase pipeline for vulnerability collection, environment reconstruction, and oracle validation.

entry.title: Vectors Are Not Neutral: Sensitive-Information Inference from Exported LLM Representations in Summarization

author.name: Weixin Liu, Bowen Qu, Juming Xiong, Congning Ni, Bradley A. Malin, Zhijun Yin

entry.summary: Demonstrates that hidden state vectors from LLM summarization can leak sensitive information like race even when source documents are access-restricted. Uses clinical discharge summary generation as audit case with EHR-recorded race labels.

entry.title: OmniInteract: Benchmarking Real-World Streaming Interaction for Real-Time Omnimodal Assistants

author.name: Xudong Lu, Xueying Li, Annan Wang, Yang Bo, Jinpeng Chen, Zengliang Li, Nianzu Yang, Rui Liu, Xue Yang, Jingwen Hou, Hongsheng Li

entry.summary: OmniInteract is a streaming benchmark for real-time omnimodal LLMs evaluated via native online inference over audio-visual streams with 250 videos and 1,430 temporally grounded response slots. Requires detecting multimodal triggers, deciding when to respond, and answering as the stream unfolds.

entry.title: Revealing the core dimensions underlying representations in brains, behavior and AI

author.name: Florian P. Mahner, Ka Chun Lam, Francisco Pereira, Martin N. Hebart

entry.summary: Introduces Similarity-Based Representation Factorization (SRF), a general method for recovering low-dimensional, interpretable, non-negative embeddings from similarity matrices in neural, behavioral, and AI representations. Bridges neuroscience, psychology, and AI representation analysis.

entry.title: On the Robustness of Machine Unlearning for Vision-Language Models

author.name: Yujie Lin, Kaidi Jia, Jiayao Ma, Chengyi Yang, Jinsong Su

entry.summary: First systematic survey and robustness analysis of vision-language model unlearning, proposing three attack paradigms that show existing methods hide rather than remove target knowledge. Provides taxonomy and unified evaluation under multiple prompt settings.

entry.title: MRT: Masked Region Transformer for Layered Image Generation and Editing at Scale

author.name: Zhicong Tang, Zhao Zhang, Jingye Chen, Mohan Zhou, Yifan Pu, Yuchi Liu, Yalong Bai, Ethan Smith, Yuhui Yuan

entry.summary: MRT is a 20B-parameter masked region diffusion transformer for multi-layer transparent image generation and editing, trained on 10M multilingual design samples and unifying text-to-layers, image-to-layers, and layers-to-layers tasks.

entry.title: Can Retrieval Heads See Images? Multimodal Retrieval Heads in Long-Context Vision-Language Models

author.name: Aaron Branson Cigres Li, Zhaowei Wang, Yu Zhao, Yiming Du, Haobo Li, Xiyu Ren, Ginny Wong, Simon See, Lishu Luo, Haodong Duan, Pasquale Minervini, Yangqiu Song

entry.summary: Identifies multimodal retrieval heads in long-context vision-language models, showing that only 4.4-10.2% of attention heads account for 50% of positive retrieval mass. Demonstrates they are sparse, intrinsic, and causally important via masking experiments.

entry.title: Are Mythos' Cyber Capabilities Overstated? - Yes and No

author.name: Muhan Luo

entry.summary: Critique of skeptical claims about Claude Mythos cyber capabilities, arguing that on general cyber tasks skeptics are right but on vulnerability discovery and exploitation specifically, well-designed benchmarks like XBOW AI and ExploitBench show Mythos substantially ahead.

entry.title: Steering Directions Are Explanations, Not Handles

author.name: JackYoung27

entry.summary: Argues that interpretable steering directions in language models, even when causal and predictive, have a smaller linear-validity radius than commonly assumed. Derives a closed-form Taylor bound predicting empirically when steering breaks down.

entry.title: When does debate help a weak judge? Evidence from code and logic

author.name: ethanelasky

entry.summary: Empirical study of debate as a reward-labeling protocol with weak judges deciding whether stronger model answers are correct on code and ARC-style logic tasks. Compares debate against one-sided open consultancy.

entry.title: Quality Without Usefulness: LLM-Generated XAI Narratives as Trust Heuristics Rather Than Decision Aids

author.name: Fabian Lukassen, Jan Herrmann, Christoph Weisser, Alexander Silbersdorff, Benjamin Saefken, Thomas Kneib

entry.summary: Investigates whether high-quality LLM-generated natural-language explanations for XAI improve task accuracy in time-series energy forecasting through five controlled experiments with 2,730 judgments. Finds quality does not translate to usefulness but inflates self-reported confidence.

entry.title: Advancing Creative Physical Intelligence in Large Multimodal Models

author.name: Cheng Qian, Hyeonjeong Ha, Jiayu Liu, Jeonghwan Kim, Emre Can Acikgoz, Bingxuan Li, Kunlun Zhu, Jiateng Liu, Aditi Tiwari, Zhenhailong Wang, Xiusi Chen, Mahdi Namazifar, Heng Ji

entry.summary: MM-CreativityBench tests creative tool use in large multimodal models by evaluating affordance-grounded problem solving where elements must be repurposed in non-obvious but physically feasible ways. Goes beyond pattern recognition to creative physical intelligence.

entry.title: The Attribution Blind Spot: Detecting When Language Models Rely on Memory Rather Than Retrieved Context

author.name: Zhe Yu, Wenpeng Xing, Yunzhao Wei, Bo Yang, Chen Ye, Gaolei Li, Meng Han

entry.summary: Identifies the attribution blind spot in RAG: faithful-looking outputs can come from parametric memory rather than retrieved context when documents overlap with pretraining data. Proposes Computational Reality Monitoring to distinguish memory from context.

entry.title: What Makes Chain-of-Thought Work at Probe Time? Local Co-occurrence Rather Than Global Derivation

author.name: Xiang Wang, Wei Wei

entry.summary: Investigates which properties of CoT rationales drive accuracy gains at probe time, finding even globally shuffled rationales outperform no-rationale baselines and that short-range token adjacency matters more than sentence-level logical ordering.

entry.title: GAC: Noise-Aware Adaptive Mixing for Hybrid SFT-RL Post-Training

author.name: Yuelin Hu, Zhenbo Yu, Zhengxue Cheng, Wei Liu, Li Song

entry.summary: GAC is a noise-aware controller that derives adaptive SFT-RL mixing weights from online gradient variance and disagreement estimates between training signals. Reports consistent improvements over fixed and rule-based hybrid post-training baselines with under 1% overhead.

entry.title: Erased but Exploitable: Black-box Embedding-Aware Prompting Against Unlearned Text-to-Image Diffusion Models

author.name: Arian Komaei Koma, Seyed Amir Kasaei, AmirMahdi Sadeghzadeh, Mohammad Hossein Rohban

entry.summary: BEAP is a black-box embedding-aware adversarial prompting attack that uses an LLM to iteratively generate effective, non-gibberish prompts that defeat machine unlearning in text-to-image diffusion models. Targets a realistic threat model where prior attacks fail.

entry.title: Why LLMs Hallucinate on Structured Knowledge: A Mechanistic Analysis of Reasoning over Linearized Representations

author.name: Shanghao Li, Jinda Han, Yibo Wang, Yuanjie Zhu, Zihe Song, Langzhou He, Kenan Kamel A Alghythee, Philip S. Yu

entry.summary: Mechanistic analysis showing LLM hallucinations on structured knowledge arise from attention disproportionately concentrating on shortcut structural cues and feed-forward representations failing to ground provided knowledge. Examines linearized graph and table representations.

entry.title: InterSketch: An Interleaved Reasoning Model with Self-correcting Visual Sketch and Stepwise Reward

author.name: Zhiwei Ning, Wenwen Tong, Xiangli Kong, Shengnan Ma, Ziyi Shang, Jingcheng Ni, Tao Hu, Yong Xien Chng, Jixuan Ying, Zehuan Wu, Hanming Deng, Jie Yang, Yuanjie Zheng, Wei Liu, Lewei Lu

entry.summary: InterSketch is an interleaved visual-text reasoning model that dynamically generates intermediate visual sketches via external tools and interleaves them with textual reasoning, trained with self-correcting and stepwise reward mechanisms. Targets long-horizon visual reasoning.

entry.title: ReCA: Multi-Shot Long Video Extrapolation via Recursive Context Allocation

author.name: Akide Liu, Jinbo Xing, Chaojie Mao, Ye Li, Zeyu Zhang, Yefei He, Weijie Wang, Zihan Wang, Yu Liu, Gholamreza Haffari, Bohan Zhuang

entry.summary: Defines Multi-Shot Video Extrapolation (MSVE) as extending an observed frame/clip into cinematically structured shots while preserving anchor state and narrative intent, with Recursive Context Allocation addressing planner over-specification under finite per-call generation budgets. Targets minute-scale cinematic video generation.

entry.title: DynFrame: Adaptive Reasoning-Driven Multimodal Framework with Dynamic Frame Augmentation for Complex Video Understanding

author.name: Peng Zhang, Guanghao Zhang, Wanggui He, Longxiang Zhang, Mushui Liu, Yan Xia, Zhenhao Peng, Weilong Dai, Jinlong Liu, Haobing Tang, Le Zhang, Hao Jiang, Pipei Huang

entry.summary: DynFrame addresses two gaps in video MLLMs: learnable per-window sampling density and decoupled optimization of retrieval vs answer generation. Targets thinking-with-video systems for complex video understanding.

entry.title: Stabilizing Recurrent Dynamics for Test-Time Scalable Latent Reasoning in Looped Language Models

author.name: Xiao-Wen Yang, Ziyu Han, Xi-Hua Zhang, Wen-Da Wei, Jie-Jing Shao, Lan-Zhe Guo, Yu-Feng Li

entry.summary: STARS framework constrains looped language models to converge toward stable fixed points, addressing test-time scaling collapse in latent reasoning. Trades off stability and effectiveness in recurrent depth scaling.

entry.title: Beyond Questions: Evaluating What Large Language Models (Actually) Know

author.name: Luca Giordano, Simon Razniewski

entry.summary: Open knowledge evaluation paradigm asking LLMs to surface knowledge through open-ended elicitation rather than predefined questions. Addresses availability bias in existing knowledge benchmarks.

entry.title: Cast a Wider Net: Coordinated Pass@K Policy Optimization for Code Reasoning

author.name: Yilong Li, Suman Banerjee, Tong Che

entry.summary: CPPO performs joint exploration over algorithmic strategies for pass@K code generation, with a planner emitting K alternative methods and shared solver attempting them. Addresses redundant rollouts in independent sampling.

entry.title: BASIS: Batchwise Advantage Estimation from Single-Rollout Information Sharing for LLM Reasoning

author.name: Shijin Gong, Erhan Xu, Kai Ye, Francesco Quinzan, Giulia Livieri, Chengchun Shi

entry.summary: Introduces BASIS, a critic-free post-training algorithm for LLM reasoning that samples only one rollout per prompt while sharing information across the batch for improved value estimation. Reports 69% MSE reduction vs REINFORCE++.

entry.title: In-Context Optimization for Retrieval-Augmented Generation: A Gradient-Descent Perspective

author.name: Mingchen Li, Jiatan Huang, Chuxu Zhang, Liang Zhao, Hong Yu

entry.summary: Frames retrieval-augmented generation as in-context optimization, showing one linear self-attention layer can implement one gradient descent step on a unified linearized RAG objective. Provides theoretical grounding for understanding RAG as adaptation rather than static evidence use.

entry.title: Memory Architectures for Multi-Turn Text-to-SQL: A Benchmark and Empirical Study

author.name: Ravi Kumar Tummalapenta, Suman Addanki

entry.summary: Introduces EnterpriseMem-Bench, a multi-turn Text-to-SQL benchmark with 300 sessions and 1,400 turns across three enterprise domains. Evaluates frontier models including GPT-5.2 and Claude Opus 4.6 across memory conditions ablating window size, episodic retrieval, and semantic augmentation.

entry.title: MicroSpec: Accelerating Speculative Decoding with Lightweight In-Context Vocabularies

author.name: Zhiyang Chen, Daliang Xu, Yinyuan Zhang, Chenghua Wang, Mengwei Xu, Yun Ma

entry.summary: MicroSpec is a training-free speculative decoding technique that builds compact context-sensitive vocabularies per decoding step. Reduces average vocabulary by over 40x to under 3k tokens while preserving draft quality.

entry.title: FinHarness: An Inline Lifecycle Safety Harness for Finance LLM Agents

author.name: Haoxuan Jia, Yang Liu, Bin Chong, Yingguang Yang, Yancheng Chen, Jiayu Liang, Qian Li, Hanning Lu, Kefu Xu, Hao Zheng, Chongyang Zhang, Hao Peng, Philip S. Yu

entry.summary: FinHarness is an inline safety harness wrapping finance LLM agents end-to-end with query and tool monitors plus a tiered LLM-judge cascade. Adaptively routes verification between lightweight and advanced judges to control mid-trajectory irreversible actions.

entry.title: Pop-Up Distractions Reveal Bag-of-Events Behavior in Video Large Language Models

author.name: Oscar Chew, Serhii Honcharenko, Qian-Hui Chen, Patricia Lu, Dishant Zaveri, Khoa D. Doan, Kuan-Hao Huang

entry.summary: DistractionBench reveals bag-of-events behavior in Video LLMs by inserting unrelated ad clips into longer videos. Shows models frequently hallucinate interactions between entities from different segments, attributing actions across boundaries.

entry.title: BAIT: Boundary-Guided Disclosure Escalation via Self-Conditioned Reasoning

author.name: Xuan Luo, Yue Wang, Geng Tu, Jing Li, Ruifeng Xu

entry.summary: Introduces BAIT, a three-step jailbreak framework that exploits a model's own consistency tendencies by asking it to identify, refine, and then exemplify its protection boundary. Demonstrates strong attack success rates across major LLM benchmarks, highlighting a structural weakness in safety alignment.

entry.title: OmniToM: Benchmarking Theory of Mind in LLMs via Explicit Belief Modeling

author.name: Adam Bawatneh, Sagar Sapkota, Amrit Singh Bedi, Santu Karmaker, Mubarak Shah

entry.summary: OmniToM is a benchmark that evaluates theory-of-mind in LLMs by requiring explicit modeling of belief propositions for all actors in a narrative, rather than just end-point QA. Aims to test whether models actually construct mental-state representations.

entry.title: UnityMAS-O: A General RL Optimization Framework for LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Yiqun Chen, Wei Yang, Erhan Zhang, Shijie Wang, Qi Liu, Zechun Niu, Bin Zhang, Haitao Li, Rui Li, Lingyong Yan, Jinyuan Feng, Biqing Qi, Xiaochi Wei, Yan Gao, Yi Wu, Yao Hu, Jiaxin Mao

entry.summary: UnityMAS-O is an RL optimization framework that treats LLM multi-agent workflows as the optimization unit (rather than single responses), supporting role-specific credit assignment, configurable parameter sharing, and structured interaction.

entry.title: SIA: Self Improving AI with Harness & Weight Updates

author.name: Prannay Hebbar, Yogendra Manawat, Samuel Verboomen, Alesia Ivanova, Selvam Palanimalai, Kunal Bhatia, Vignesh Baskaran

entry.summary: SIA combines harness updates (a meta-agent rewriting tools, prompts, retry logic) with weight updates (RL-based test-time training) in a unified self-improvement loop, bridging two largely disjoint research lines.

entry.title: Natural Language Query to Configuration for Retrieval Agents

author.name: Melissa Z. Pan, Negar Arabzadeh, Mathew Jacob, Fiodar Kazhamiaka, Esha Choukse, Matei Zaharia

entry.summary: BRANE selects optimal retrieval pipeline configurations (LLM, retriever, num documents, hops, synthesis) per query using lightweight predictors trained from LLM-derived workload characteristics. From Matei Zaharia's group.

entry.title: TSFMAudit: Data Contamination Auditing in Forecasting Time Series Foundation Models

author.name: Hongkai Li, Shifeng Xie, Lefei Shen, Zhuo Li, Mouxiang Chen, Xiaobin Zhang, Han Fu, Jianling Sun, Xiaoxue Ren, Chenghao Liu

entry.summary: TSFMAudit is the first method for auditing pretraining contamination in time series foundation models, using probe adaptation dynamics to detect unusually efficient fine-tuning that signals exposure. Addresses an open evaluation integrity problem for TSFMs.

entry.title: AutoDFT: A Closed-Loop Multi-Agent Framework for Autonomous DFT Calculations

author.name: Penghui Yang, Zhonghan Zhang, Yue Li, Xinrun Wag, Yanchen Deng, Yuhao Lu, Bijun Tang, Zheng Liu, Bo An

entry.summary: AutoDFT is a closed-loop multi-agent framework for autonomous density functional theory calculations that adapts execution plans based on intermediate results rather than executing fixed upfront plans. Targets materials science and chemistry workflows.

entry.title: CyberEvolver: Structured Self-Evolution for Cybersecurity Agents On the Fly

author.name: Yihe Fan, Changyi Li, Lichen Xu, Xudong Pan, Jiarun Dai, Hong Geng, Min Yang

entry.summary: CyberEvolver is a self-evolving cybersecurity agent framework that iteratively revises its own scaffold from failed execution feedback, addressing limitations of fixed human-designed agent scaffolds. Uses a four-layer evolvable architecture for sparse-feedback domains.

entry.title: CroCo: Cross-Lingual Contrastive Preference Tuning on Self-Generations

author.name: Mike Zhang, Ali Basirat, Desmond Elliott

entry.summary: CroCo extends contrastive preference tuning on self-generations to 14 high and low-resource languages, showing English-trained reward models transfer cross-lingually without language-specific preference annotation. Improvements observed across most language-task pairs.

entry.title: When Correct Demonstrations Hurt: Rethinking the Role of Exemplars in In-Context Learning

author.name: Chenghao Qiu, Chunli Peng, Yufeng Yang, Kuan-Hao Huang, Yi Zhou

entry.summary: Reveals that correct in-context demonstrations can reduce ICL accuracy through task-preserving perturbations where only exemplar inputs are changed. Distinguishes label-updating from target-preserving perturbations to study the correctness-utility gap.

entry.title: Personalized Generative Models for Contextual Debiasing

author.name: Xinran Liang, Esin Tureci, Prachi Sinha, Ye Zhu, Vikram V. Ramaswamy, Olga Russakovsky

entry.summary: Generates images with uncommon contextual combinations (e.g., beach ball on road) to augment training data for vision models, mitigating distributional biases in object recognition. From the Olga Russakovsky group at Princeton.

entry.title: Unified Panoramic Geometry Estimation via Multi-View Foundation Models

author.name: Vukasin Bozic, Isidora Slavkovic, Dominik Narnhofer, Nando Metzger, Denis Rozumny, Konrad Schindler, Nikolai Kalischek

entry.summary: PaGeR lifts perspective-image 3D reconstruction foundation models to panorama domain, producing unified scale-invariant depth, metric depth, and surface predictions from single 360-degree panoramas. From a strong ETH Zurich group with Konrad Schindler.

entry.title: When Does Deep RL Beat Calibrated Baselines? A Benchmark Study on Adaptive Resource Control

author.name: Guilin Zhang, Chuanyi Sun, Kai Zhao, Shahryar Sarkani, John Fossaceca

entry.summary: Reproducible benchmark RLScale-Bench evaluating six deep RL algorithms (PPO, DQN, A2C, SAC, TD3, DDPG) against calibrated rule-based baselines for adaptive resource control on Kubernetes autoscaling. Across 240 runs the rule baseline beats every DRL algorithm on cost across all workloads.

entry.title: Aperiodic and Low-Frequency Spectral Bias in Reconstruction based EEG Foundation Models

author.name: Aditya Kommineni, Emily Zhou, Kleanthis Avramidis, Simon Bock Segaard, Jeppe Roden M\"unster, Andreas Peter Juhl Hansen, Takfarinas Medani, Tiantian Feng, Richard Leahy, Shrikanth Narayanan

entry.summary: Mechanistic analysis showing EEG foundation models are biased toward low-frequency oscillatory components and miss high-power aperiodic structure due to mismatch between reconstruction pretext tasks and EEG spectral structure. Explains why EEG FMs underperform supervised models in low-resource regimes.

entry.title: Towards Error-Free EHRs: Reasoning-Intensive Consistency Verification Between Clinical Notes and Structured Tables in Electronic Health Records

author.name: Yeonsu Kwon, Jiho Kim, Junseong Choi, Paloma Rabaey, Minseo Kim, Sujeong Im, Jeewon Yang, Jun-Min Lee, Sangji Lee, Jiwon Kim, Hangyul Yoon, Hyunwook Kwon, Edward Choi

entry.summary: EHR-ReasonCon is a reasoning-intensive benchmark for consistency verification between clinical notes and structured tables in EHRs, built on MIMIC-III with 8,048 entities and expert-guided annotations. Goes beyond surface-level matching to capture clinical interpretation, event relations, and temporal changes.

entry.title: Bridging Control with Neural Network Verifier alpha-beta-CROWN: A Tutorial

author.name: Haoyu Li, Xiangru Zhong, Hao Cheng, Bin Hu, Huan Zhang

entry.summary: Tutorial on combining alpha-beta-CROWN neural network verifier with control synthesis to formally verify properties of learned controllers. Targets safety-critical control applications.

entry.title: On the Error-Correcting Effects of Stochasticity in Discrete Diffusion

author.name: William Yuan, Sungwon Jeong, Amirali Aghazadeh

entry.summary: Information-theoretic analysis showing that stochasticity in discrete diffusion provides error correction via redundant transitions. Reveals tradeoffs between deterministic fast convergence and stochastic high fidelity.

entry.title: More Expressive Feedforward Layers: Part I. Token-Adaptive Mixing of Activations

author.name: Mingze Wang, Jinbo Wang, Yikuan Xia, Kai Shen, Shu Zhong

entry.summary: Mixture of Activations (MoA) introduces token-adaptive FFN design that mixes a dictionary of activation functions with input-dependent gates. Departs from single fixed activation paradigm in transformer FFNs.

entry.title: An In-Vitro Study on Cross-Lingual Generalization in Language Models

author.name: Adrian Cosma

entry.summary: In-vitro framework for studying cross-lingual transfer using procedurally generated languages with shared ontology but different surface forms. Finds tokenization properties matter more than balance or lexical similarity in 700 controlled runs.

entry.title: Model Merging on Loss Landscape: A Geometry Perspective

author.name: Juanwu Lu, Anand Bhaskar, Brian Axelrod, Ekaterina Tolstaya, Tristan Emrich

entry.summary: EpiMer formulates model merging as Frechet mean on a Riemannian manifold restricted to task-vector subspaces, using expected Hessian as metric. Connects local curvature to epistemic uncertainty.

entry.title: ICICLE: Expanding Retrieval with In-Context Documents

author.name: Yu-Chen Den, Yung-Yu Shih, Zhi Rui Tam, Kuan-Yu Chen, Pu-Jen Cheng, Yun-Nung Chen, Eugene Yang

entry.summary: ICICLE reframes incremental generative retrieval as in-context retrieval, supplying new documents at inference time via a copy-based routing mechanism. Avoids parameter updates and catastrophic forgetting for corpus expansion.

entry.title: Reasoning Depth and Environment Complexity: A Controlled Study of RLVR Data Allocation across Logical Reasoning Tasks

author.name: Yihua Zhu, Qianying Liu, Fei Cheng, Jiaxin Wang, Akiko Aizawa, Sadao Kurohashi, Hidetoshi Shimodaira

entry.summary: Controlled study characterizing reasoning data along two dimensions: depth and environment complexity, plus four ability types (deductive, abductive, inductive, analogical). Examines RLVR data allocation tradeoffs across logical reasoning tasks.

entry.title: JuICE: A Benchmark for Evaluating LLM-Judge in Identifying Cultural Errors

author.name: Jiho Jin, Junho Myung, Juhyun Oh, Junyeong Park, Rifki Afina Putri, Sunipa Dev, Vinodkumar Prabhakaran, Alice Oh

entry.summary: JuICE is a benchmark for evaluating LLM-judges on identifying culturally-thick errors beyond flat fact verification. Examines whether LLM judges capture contextually inappropriate but factually plausible cultural errors.

entry.title: Recon: Reconstruction-Guided Reasoning Synthesis for User Modeling

author.name: Alan Zhu, Mihran Miroyan, Carolyn Wang, Andrew Zhou, Lisa Dunlap, Narges Norouzi, Joseph E. Gonzalez

entry.summary: Recon scores synthesized reasoning traces by predictive power via action reconstruction rather than post-hoc rationalization. Aimed at user modeling where latent decision paths matter more than action justification.

entry.title: Evaluating the Relevance of Uncertainty Estimators for LLM Hallucination

author.name: Yedidia Agnimo, Anna Korba, Annabelle Blangero, Nicolas Chesneau, Karteek Alahari

entry.summary: Empirical evaluation of when and how strongly uncertainty estimators correlate with hallucinations in LLMs. Tests information-theoretic, sampling-based, and reflexive estimators across diverse settings.

entry.title: FoundObj: Self-supervised Foundation Models as Rewards for Label-free 3D Object Segmentation

author.name: Zihui Zhang, Zhixuan Sun, Yafei Yang, Jinxi Li, Jiahao Chen, Bo Yang

entry.summary: FoundObj performs label-free 3D point cloud object segmentation using a superpoint-based discovery agent guided by semantic and geometric reward modules drawing on 2D/3D foundation models. Eliminates need for scene-level annotations.

entry.title: Learning When to Think While Listening in Large Audio-Language Models

author.name: Zhiyuan Song, Weici Zhao, Yang Xiao, Suhao Yu, Cheng Zhu, Jiatao Gu

entry.summary: Proposes a learnable wait-think-answer controller for streaming audio-LLMs that decides when to wait for more audio, externalize reasoning, or answer. Built on Qwen2.5-Omni-7B to balance reasoning quality with response latency.

entry.title: Lost in Sampling: Assessing Lexical Reachability in LLMs via the Word Coverage Score (WCS)

author.name: Samer Awad, Javier Conde, Carlos Arriaga, Tairan Fu, Javier Coronado-Bl\'azquez, Pedro Reviriego

entry.summary: Introduces the Word Coverage Score to measure how much contextually appropriate human vocabulary is pruned by sampling filters like Top-p, Top-k, and Min-p. Audits open-weight models to show decoding mechanics, not just training, suppress lexical diversity.

entry.title: Falcon-X: A Time Series Foundation Model for Heterogeneous Multivariate Modeling

author.name: Yiding Liu, Yifan Hu, Hongjie Xia, Peiyuan Liu, Hongzhou Chen, Xilin Dai, Zewei Dong, Jiang-Ming Yang

entry.summary: Falcon-X is a time-series foundation model that maps variates into a unified latent space to handle heterogeneous multivariate forecasting, addressing limitations of raw-space cross-variate attention. Targets semantic alignment of physical quantities and synergistic/antagonistic interactions.

entry.title: GENESIS: Harnessing AI Agents for Autonomous 6G RAN Synthesis, Research, and Testing

author.name: Tamerlan Aghayev, Maxime Elkael, Michele Polese, Minh Dat Nguyen, Gabriele Gemmi, Andrea Lacava, Ali Saeizadeh, Reshma Prasad, Paolo Testolina, Angelo Feraudo, Soumendra Nanda, Pedram Johari, Salvatore D'Oro, Tommaso Melodia

entry.summary: GENESIS uses LLM-based agents to autonomously synthesize, test, and harden 6G RAN code from standards and research papers, addressing six structural R&D bottlenecks. Demonstrates compressing months-long cellular network engineering iterations.

entry.title: The Constraint Tax: Measuring Validity-Correctness Tradeoffs in Structured Outputs for Small Language Models

author.name: Jaideep Ray

entry.summary: Introduces a constraint tax measurement protocol showing that hard structured-output constraints degrade answer correctness in sub-3B small language models, contradicting the assumption that schemas only affect format. Important for on-device LLM deployment patterns.

entry.title: The Bridge-Garden Dilemma in LLM Distillation: Why Mixing Hard and Soft Labels Works

author.name: Guanghui Wang, Kaiwen Lv Kacuila, Zhiyong Yang, Zitai Wang, Jin-Wen Wu, Longtao Huang, Qianqian Xu, Qingming Huang

entry.summary: Proposes a Bridge-Garden Decomposition theory explaining why mixing hard and soft labels in LLM distillation outperforms soft-only approaches. Attributes the gain to reduced exposure bias rather than closer teacher matching.

entry.title: Scaling World-Model Reinforcement Learning Through Diffusion Policy Optimization

author.name: Xiaoyuan Cheng, Wenxuan Yuan, Zhancun Mu, Yuanzhao Zhang, Yiming Yang, Hai Wang, Zhuo Sun, Che Liu

entry.summary: MBDPO unifies search and value learning in world-model RL by using diffusion policies, addressing a structural misalignment where value functions are typically induced by separate non-search policies. Targets scaling model-based RL.

entry.title: MULTISEISMO: A Multimodal Seismic Dataset and Model for Cross-Modal Seismic Understanding

author.name: Sai Munikoti, Ian Stewart, Chengping Chai, Lisa Linville, Scott Vasquez, Sameera Horawalavithana, Karl Pazdernik

entry.summary: MultiSeismo is a large-scale multimodal seismic dataset combining waveforms, intensity maps, population exposure visualizations, and text metadata for 16K events across 13 years. Addresses the gap in domain-specific multimodal datasets for seismology.

entry.title: Reparametrizing Shampoo and SOAP for Subspace Basis Updates and BFloat16 Storage

author.name: Alan Milligan, Zikun Xu, Simon Lacoste-Julien, Felix Dangel, Wu Lin

entry.summary: Reparameterizes Shampoo and SOAP optimizers to support BFloat16 storage and partial subspace QR updates, reducing the computational cost of preconditioner updates. Addresses a practical bottleneck in scaling these second-order methods.

entry.title: QAM-W: Joint 2D Codebook Quantization for LLM Weights via Hadamard Rotation and Activation-Aware Scaling

author.name: Preetam Sharma, Kacper Dobek

entry.summary: QAM-W applies QAM-style 2D vector quantization with Hadamard rotation and activation-aware scaling to LLM weights, achieving near-BF16 quality at ~5.5 bits per weight. Recovers pairwise coordinate structure that scalar quantizers discard.

entry.title: A PAC-Bayesian View of Generalisation for Physics-Informed Machine Learning

author.name: Thien V. Nguyen, Amaury Habrard, Benjamin Guedj

entry.summary: Develops PAC-Bayesian generalization bounds for physics-informed machine learning under unbounded losses, jointly treating data fidelity, PDE residuals, and boundary conditions as multi-task objectives. Provides high-probability guarantees previously lacking in PIML theory.

entry.title: MechRL: Reinforcement Learning Agents Perform Circuit Discovery for Mechanistic Interpretability

author.name: Barsat Khadka

entry.summary: MechRL trains a PPO agent over GPT-2 small attention heads as a 144-action space to discover circuits via zero-ablation contrastive rewards. Recovers known induction and IOI circuits and transfers to a held-out task.

entry.title: Beyond Holistic Models: Systematic Component-level Benchmarking of Deep Multivariate Time-Series Forecasting

author.name: Shuang Liang, Chaochuan Hou, Xu Yao, Shiping Wang, Hailiang Huang, Songqiao Han, Minqi Jiang

entry.summary: TSCOMP is a large-scale benchmark deconstructing deep multivariate time-series forecasting models into fine-grained components such as preprocessing, encoding, architecture, and optimization. Uses constrained orthogonal experimental design for component-level analysis.

entry.title: RT-Lynx: Putting the GEMM Sparsity In a Right Way for Diffusion Models

author.name: Xing Cong, Hanlin Tang, Kan Liu, Lan Tao, Lin Qu, Chenhao Xie

entry.summary: RT-Lynx applies N:M semi-structured sparsity to diffusion transformer activations rather than weights, leveraging the observation that DiT activations are intrinsically sparse and more robust than weights. Halves FLOPs while preserving generation quality.

entry.title: Not All Disagreement Is Learnable: Token Teachability in On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Yuanyi Wang, Su Lu, Yanggan Gu, Pengkai Wang, Yifan Yang, Zhaoyi Yan, Congkai Xie, Jianmin Wu, Hongxia Yang

entry.summary: Investigates which token-level teacher signals are actually learnable in on-policy distillation, distinguishing learnable disagreement (corrective mass on student top-K) from incompatible disagreement. Proposes refining selective OPD by considering local compatibility.

entry.title: Causal Risk Minimization for High-Dimensional Treatments

author.name: Nikita Dhawan, Arnav Paruthi, Andrew Kim, Lovedeep Gondara, Jekaterina Novikova, Chris J. Maddison

entry.summary: Adapts causal inference as a learning problem for high-dimensional treatment spaces (e.g., text interventions), decomposing causal error into moment-balancing errors of increasing order. Enables predicting effects of interventions with many possible variations.

entry.title: From Scores to Gibbs Correctors: Accelerating Uniform-Rate Discrete Diffusion Models

author.name: Yuchen Liang, Ness Shroff, Yingbin Liang

entry.summary: Introduces GADD, a Gibbs-based corrector for accelerating uniform-rate discrete diffusion models that leverages concrete score function structure without additional training. Achieves polylog(1/epsilon) sampling complexity.

entry.title: RICE-PO: Turning Retrieval Interactions into Credit Signals for Reasoning Agents

author.name: Mingchen Li, Hansi Zeng, Zhuo Qian, Jiatan Huang, Hamed Zamani, Hong Yu

entry.summary: RICE-PO is a critic-free policy optimization framework for retrieval agents that converts retrieval interactions into localized credit signals. Addresses the credit assignment problem between observable retrieval actions and latent reasoning steps.

entry.title: Probing Minimalist Phase Structure in LLMs: What Universal Dependencies Cannot Represent

author.name: Yuanhao Chen, Peter Chin

entry.summary: Probes whether LLMs encode Minimalist Program phase boundaries beyond what Universal Dependencies can represent, using wh-movement stimuli where UD distances are invariant. Finds a phase-count gradient across 12/13 of 13 models tested.

entry.title: Hubness, Not Anisotropy, Drives Cross-Lingual Retrieval Asymmetry in Multilingual Embedding Models

author.name: Adib Sakhawat, Fardeen Sadab, Atik Shahriar

entry.summary: Empirically identifies hubness, not anisotropy, as the dominant cause of cross-lingual retrieval asymmetry in multilingual embeddings. Uses parallel corpora across English, Bangla, Hindi, and Arabic across five production encoders including Gemini, Mistral, OpenAI, and Qwen.

entry.title: Learning to Adapt SFT Data for Better Reasoning Generalization

author.name: Lisong Sun, Li Wang, Chen Zhang, Jinyang Wu, Kui Zhang, Tianhao Peng, Wenjun Wu

entry.summary: DART formulates SFT data use as an optimization over demonstration transformations, training a mapper model with RL to convert misaligned expert data into model-aligned demonstrations. Targets reasoning generalization when SFT data distribution mismatches the target model.

entry.title: Efficient Agentic Reinforcement Learning with On-Policy Intrinsic Knowledge Boundary Enhancement

author.name: Dingwei Chen, Zefang Zong, Zhipeng Ma, Leo Luo, Yang Li, Chengming Li, Peng Chen, Jie Jiang

entry.summary: AKBE is an on-policy method that dynamically probes the LLM's intrinsic knowledge boundary through dual-path with-tool and no-tool rollouts to address redundant tool calls in agentic RL training. Avoids the reward-hacking risk of coarse-grained reward shaping.

entry.title: Prompt Injection Detection is Regime-Dependent: A Deployment-Aware Evaluation with Interpretable Structural Signals

author.name: Akindoyin Akinrele, Shreyank N Gowda

entry.summary: Presents a deployment-aware multi-model multi-regime evaluation of prompt injection detection across lexical, semantic, structural, and transformer-based detectors. Introduces interpretable structural signals capturing hierarchy overrides, system spoofing, and role redefinition.

entry.title: On the Hidden Costs of Counterfactual Knowledge Training in LLM Unlearning

author.name: Xiaotian Ye, Xiaohan Wang, Mengqi Zhang, Shu Wu

entry.summary: Identifies two pitfalls in counterfactual tuning for LLM unlearning: knowledge conflict from inconsistent corpora and hallucination spillover from fitting false targets. Introduces RWKU+ extended benchmark to diagnose these issues.

entry.title: The Coverage Illusion: From Pre-retrieval Routing Failure to Post-retrieval Cascades in a Production RAG System

author.name: Zafar Hussain, Kristoffer Nielbo

entry.summary: Case study of Danish National Encyclopedia RAG showing the Coverage Illusion: synthetic queries suggest 90% need LLM augmentation while real traffic needs only 27.8%. Evaluates five retrieval workflows over 20,000 query-workflow pairs.

entry.title: Chartographer: Counterfactual Chart Generation for Evaluating Vision-Language Models

author.name: Yifan Jiang, Dae Yon Hwang, Jesse C. Cresswell, Freda Shi

entry.summary: Chartographer reverse-engineers charts into executable code to generate counterfactual chart variants with controlled QA logic. Enables strict visual reasoning evaluation by varying underlying charts while fixing the chart-question task.

entry.title: RoMo: A Large-Scale, Richly Organized Dataset and Semantic Taxonomy for Human Motion Generation

author.name: Jiahao Zhang, Joseph Liu, Young-Yoon Lee, Seonghyeon Moon, Victor Zordan, Guy Tevet, Karen Liu, Stephen Gould, Oren Jacob, Haomiao Jiang, Mubbasir Kapadia, Yizhak Ben-Shabat

entry.summary: RoMo is a large-scale, taxonomy-organized dataset of in-the-wild human motions with detailed captions and quality filtering. Aims to bridge the gap between small mocap datasets and noisy large-scale collections for generative motion modeling.

entry.title: $R^3$: 3D Reconstruction via Relative Regression

author.name: Congrong Xu, Huachen Gao, Xingyu Chen, Yuliang Xiu, Jun Gao, Anpei Chen

entry.summary: R^3 uses relative regression with confidence-weighted constraints to enable long-context and streaming 3D reconstruction, lifting the global coordinate frame assumption of feed-forward geometry foundation models. Includes Jun Gao and Anpei Chen.

entry.title: Touch-R1: Reinforcing Touch Reasoning in MLLMs

author.name: Yingxin Lai, Yafei Zhou, Fucai Zhu, Siyu Zhu, Weihao Yuan

entry.summary: Touch-R1 introduces rule-based RL for tactile reasoning in multimodal models, addressing the ordinal nature of physical attributes and cross-sensor distribution shifts. Releases TouchReason-1M dataset across four tactile sensors.

entry.title: SpatialBench: Is Your Spatial Foundation Model an All-Round Player?

author.name: Haosong Peng, Hao Li, Jiaqi Chen, Yuhao Pan, Runmao Yao, Yalun Dai, Fushuo Huo, Fangzhou Hong, Zhaoxi Chen, Haozhao Wang, Dingwen Zhang, Ziwei Liu, Wenchao Xu

entry.summary: SpatialBench is a holistic benchmark for spatial foundation models that evaluates generalization across viewpoints, scene domains, input densities, and hardware constraints. Aims to expose narrow paradigm coverage in current evaluation.

entry.title: Can VLA Models Learn from Real-World Data Continually without Forgetting?

author.name: Jiarun Zhu, Yijun Hong, Xiaoquan Sun, Zetian Xu, Mingqi Yuan, Zhiyong Wang, Wenjun Zeng, Jiayu Chen

entry.summary: Constructs a real-world continual learning dataset of four sequential manipulation tasks for VLA models and shows that VLAs suffer significant catastrophic forgetting under realistic conditions. Highlights an underexplored deployment challenge.

entry.title: Fast Convergence of Policy Regret in Learning Stochastic Optimal Control

author.name: Shengbo Wang, Jose Blanchet, Peter Glynn

entry.summary: Theoretical analysis of value-based policy learning in stochastic optimal control showing fast regret convergence is induced by three geometric structures: a growth exponent, separation properties, and additional regularity. Authors include Stanford's Blanchet and Glynn.

entry.title: Training Language Models for Controlled Stochasticity

author.name: Sruthi Kuriakose

entry.summary: Examines mode collapse in LLM outputs (e.g., Qwen3 picks Wednesday 80 percent of the time) and explores training methods to encourage genuine output diversity without sacrificing quality. Argues this is critical for synthetic data generation.

entry.title: Practical Learnings from Synthetic Document Finetuning

author.name: Axel Højmark

entry.summary: Apollo Research practitioner notes on Synthetic Document Finetuning for implanting beliefs in models, including pipeline tweaks and tips for the universe context, fact extraction, and document generation stages.

entry.title: Generalizable mutation-effect prediction across adaptive immune recognition via unified multimodal framework

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: A Nature Machine Intelligence paper presenting a unified multimodal framework for predicting mutation effects on adaptive immune recognition, generalizing across diverse contexts. The work targets a key challenge in immunology and vaccine design by combining sequence and structural modalities.

entry.title: Is Agent Memory a Database? Rethinking Data Foundations for Long-Term AI Agent Memory

author.name: Abdelghny Orogat, Essam Mansour

entry.summary: Proposes Governed Evolving Memory (GEM), a formalization of long-term AI agent memory as a new data management workload where correctness is a property of the state trajectory rather than individual records. Identifies failure modes like unregulated growth and capacity-driven forgetting.

entry.title: Automatic Layer Selection for Hallucination Detection

author.name: Xinpeng Wang, William Cao, Andrew Gordon Wilson, Zhe Zeng

entry.summary: Investigates how to automatically select the best intermediate layers for hallucination detection in LLMs, proposing hypotheses for why such signals emerge in intermediate layers and evaluating selection criteria across architectures and tasks.

entry.title: AGORA: Adapter-Grounded Observation-Action Retention for Inference-Free Prompt Compression in LLM Agents

author.name: Haoran Zhang, Zhaohua Sun

entry.summary: AGORA identifies action-grammar destruction as a key failure mode of token-level prompt compression in LLM agents (where action-carrying tokens have lowest self-information and get removed). Proposes inference-free step-level compression combining structural parsing with adapters.

entry.title: TADDLE: A Tool-Augmented Agent for Detecting Deficient LLM-Generated Peer Reviews

author.name: Hanqi Duan, Xiang Li

entry.summary: TADDLE is a tool-augmented agent and expert-annotated benchmark (1800 reviews on 50 ICLR 2025 papers across six defect categories) for detecting defects in LLM-generated peer reviews at individual defect-type granularity.

entry.title: Scaling, Benchmarking, and Reasoning of Vision-Language Agents for Mobile GUI Navigation

author.name: Heng Qu, Yike Liu, Renren Jin, Wenzong Zhang, Pengzhi Gao, Wei Liu, Jian Luan

entry.summary: Introduces HyperTrack, a 16000+ task dataset across 650+ Chinese mobile apps for VLM-based GUI agents, plus GUIEvalKit toolkit. Shows reinforcement-based finetuning consistently outperforms supervised finetuning, especially out-of-domain.

entry.title: VitaBench 2.0: Evaluating Personalized and Proactive Agents in Long-Term User Interactions

author.name: Yuxin Chen, Yi Zhang, Zhengzhou Cai, Yaorui Shi, Zhiyuan Yao, Chenhang Cui, Jingnan Zheng, Yaqi Huo, Xi Su, Qi Gu, Xunliang Cai, Xiang Wang, An Zhang, Tat-Seng Chua

entry.summary: VitaBench 2.0 is a benchmark for evaluating personalized and proactive agent behavior in long-term user interactions, with tasks organized as temporal fragments requiring user-intent inference beyond explicit statements.

entry.title: Tool-Schema Compression Enables Agentic RAG Under Constrained Context Budgets

author.name: Furkan Sakizli

entry.summary: Systematic study of the tool-schema vs retrieval context trade-off in agentic RAG, showing schema compression enables RAG functionality at 8K context budgets where uncompressed schemas overflow. Evaluates 14 models across 6,566 controlled API calls.

entry.title: PitchBench: Measuring Pitch Hearing in Audio-Language Models

author.name: Milan Liessens Dujardin, Song-Ze Yu, Craver Corbyn Thomas-Smith, David M. Chan, Karina Nguyen

entry.summary: PitchBench is a benchmark measuring pitch hearing as a fundamental musical perception ability in audio-language models, addressing a gap in existing audio evaluations. Includes contributions from David Chan and Karina Nguyen.

entry.title: Alignment Tuning for Large Language Models: A Data-Centric Lens on Alignment Data Pipelines

author.name: Hwanjun Song

entry.summary: Survey reframing alignment tuning as a pipeline design problem with three stages (response synthesis, preference evaluation, preference instantiation) and a unified taxonomy of methods. From Hwanjun Song at KAIST.

entry.title: Unveiling the Fragility of Vision-Language Models: Multi-Modal Adversarial Synergy via Texture-Constrained Perturbations and Cross-Modal Optimization

author.name: Xiang Fang, Wanlong Fang, Changshuo Wang

entry.summary: Multi-Modal Adversarial Synergy crafts universal black-box adversarial attacks against LVLMs by simultaneously generating texture-scale-constrained universal perturbations and cross-modal optimization. Targets practical scenarios like autonomous driving and content moderation.

entry.title: Aligning Few-Step Generative Models by Amortizing Sample-based Variational Inference

author.name: Jaewoo Lee, Hyeongyu Kang, Dohyun Kim, Kyuil Sim, Woocheol Shin, Minsu Kim, Taeyoung Yun, Jeongjae Lee, Sanghyeok Choi, Tabitha Edith Lee, Jongchul Ye, Jinkyoo Park

entry.summary: FAV is a sample-based variational inference framework for aligning few-step generative models without requiring tractable likelihoods or specific solvers. It uses Stein Variational Gradient Descent amortized into generator parameters.

entry.title: AI evaluation may bias perceptions: The importance of context in interpreting academic writing

author.name: Shang Wu, Randol Yao

entry.summary: Examines how AI-use detection in scientific writing is biased by ignoring country and field-specific stylistic differences. Shows that pooled benchmarks systematically distort estimates and proposes country-field-specific baselines.

entry.title: The Labyrinth and the Thread: Rethinking Regularizations in Sequential Knowledge Editing for Large Language Models

author.name: Zheng Wang, Kaixuan Zhang, Wanfang Chen, Jingwen Zhang, Xiaonan Lu

entry.summary: Investigates regularization mechanisms in sequential knowledge editing for LLMs, establishing equivalence between one-time and sequential editing under proper accumulated constraint accounting. Argues stability emerges from constraint handling rather than complex regularization.

entry.title: Black-box Membership Inference Attacks on the Pre-training Data of Image-generation Models

author.name: Tao Qi, Huili Wang, Yuanhong Huang, Wendan Wang, Lianchao Zhao, Jinrui Wang, Zichen Qin, Shangguang Wang, Yongfeng Huang

entry.summary: Black-box membership inference attacks targeting pre-training data of image-generation models, where existing methods relying on memorization fail. Addresses limitations of denoising-based features for less-exposed data.

entry.title: Trust Region Q Adjoint Matching

author.name: Yonghoon Dong, Kyungmin Lee, Changyeon Kim, Jaehyuk Kim, Jinwoo Shin

entry.summary: TRQAM is a stable off-policy fine-tuning algorithm for pretrained flow policies, using path-space KL trust regions via projected dual descent. Addresses critic ill-conditioning that causes model collapse in QAM.

entry.title: Localizing Memorized Regions in Diffusion Models via Coordinate-Wise Curvature Differences

author.name: Gwangho Kim, Sungyoon Lee

entry.summary: Provides a geometric characterization of memorization in diffusion models as coordinate-wise variance collapse, and proposes curvature-difference methods to localize memorized regions within generated images. Addresses privacy and copyright concerns.

entry.title: Sampling Data with Chains of Forward-Backward Diffusion Steps

author.name: Hyunmo Kang, Noam Itzhak Levi, Corinna Elena Wegner, Daniel J. Korchinski, Matthieu Wyart

entry.summary: Introduces U-turn chains, Markov chains obtained by iterating short forward-backward diffusion steps with Metropolis-Hastings corrections, to sample from energy-modified targets. Identifies an ergodicity-breaking phase transition driven by manifold fragmentation.

entry.title: Transformers Can Learn Posterior Predictive Distributions In-Context

author.name: Gyeonghun Kang, Changwoo J. Lee, Xiang Cheng

entry.summary: Theoretically shows by construction that transformers can implement gradient descent targeting the posterior predictive mean and variance for Gaussian process regression. Studies error bounds for prior-data fitted networks approximating posterior predictive distributions.

entry.title: SPEAR: Code-Augmented Agentic Prompt Optimization

author.name: Mengyin Lu, Cong Feng, Huimin Han, Guangming Lu, Yu Sun, Xiaonan Ding, Shihui Long, Fengyi Li, Tanvi Motwani

entry.summary: SPEAR adapts the code-as-action paradigm for automatic prompt engineering, giving an agent tools including a Python sandbox to perform structural error analysis on evaluation data. Adds guardrails like rollback to handle long-horizon agentic optimization.

entry.title: Cultural Value Alignment Via Latent Activation Steering in Large Language Models

author.name: Trung Duc Anh Dang, Sarah Masud

entry.summary: Proposes activation steering to shift LLM cultural alignment using scenario-based behavioral probing across 300 dilemmas tied to the World Values Survey. Bypasses surface alignment via implicit token probabilities to access latent cultural representations.

entry.title: Model Unlearning Objectives Vary for Distinct Language Functions

author.name: Berk Atil, Vipul Gupta, Rebecca J. Passonneau

entry.summary: Argues unlearning methods should be tailored to language function, proposing a cosine-based meta-learned RMU variant for dangerous knowledge and a multi-layer probe-direction objective for toxicity. Evaluates across four open-source 7-8B models.

entry.title: NestedKV: Nested Memory Routing for Long-Context KV Cache Compression

author.name: Hong Chen, Xiang Liu, Yubo Gao, Yuxuan Fan, Bo Wang, Yuanlin Chu, Yuanguo Lin, Xuming Hu

entry.summary: NestedKV is a key-only KV cache compression method maintaining global, block, and sliding-window key anchors, scoring tokens via multi-timescale cosine anomaly. Combines training-free outer learner with head-adaptive mixing and surprise-gated routing.

entry.title: PRISM: A Multi-Dimensional Benchmark for Evaluating LLM Peer Reviewers

author.name: Ngoc Phan Phuoc Loc, Toan Huynh La Viet, Thanh Tran Khanh, Duy A Nguyen, Tuan Anh Nguyen Pham, Thanh Nguyen, Nitesh V. Chawla, Wray Buntine, Kok-Seng Wong, Khoa D. Doan, Binh T. Nguyen

entry.summary: PRISM is a structured multi-dimensional benchmark for evaluating LLM peer reviewers across depth, novelty, flaw identification, and constructiveness. Compares to humans on catching scientific gaps beyond surface-level ROUGE/BLEU metrics.

entry.title: Are Video Models Zero-Shot Learners and Reasoners in Education? EduVideoBench, A Knowledge-Skills-Attitude Benchmark for Educational Video Generation

author.name: Unggi Lee, Hoyoung Ahn, Yoon Choi, Seonmin Eun, Jahyun Jeong, Seonmin Jin, Harmony Jung, Hye Jin Kim, Chaerin Lee, Hyunji Lee, Jeongjin Lee, Soohwan Lee, Young-Seok Oh, Jaehyeon Park, Sun-ok Ryu, Sunyoung Shin, Yoorim Son, Haeun Park, Yeil Jeong

entry.summary: Introduces EduVideoBench, a Knowledge-Skills-Attitude framework benchmark for educational video generation across five frontier video models. Finds substantial gaps in pedagogical adequacy and educational safety before classroom readiness.

entry.title: Attribute-Based Diagnosis of LLM Alignment with Hate Speech Annotations

author.name: Mohammad Amine Jradi, Faeze Ghorbanpour, Alexander Fraser

entry.summary: Analyzes LLM alignment with hate-speech annotations across ten theoretically grounded subjective attributes for Llama 3.1 and Qwen 2.5. Finds behaviorally explicit dimensions correlate strongly with humans while evaluative dimensions are systematically inverted.

entry.title: Share More, Search Less: Collaborative Parallel Thinking for Efficient Test-Time Scaling

author.name: Xinglin Wang, Hao Lin, Shaoxiong Feng, Peiwen Yuan, Yiwei Li, Jiayi Shi, Yueqi Zhang, Chuyi Tan, Ji Zhang, Boyuan Pan, Yao Hu, Kan Li

entry.summary: Collaborative Parallel Thinking (CPT) enables information sharing across parallel reasoning branches during test-time scaling, reducing redundant exploration. Training-free framework targets the inefficiency of branch-private intermediate discoveries.

entry.title: MAIGO: Mitigating Lost-in-Conversation with History-Cleaned On-Policy Self-Distillation

author.name: Haoyu Zheng, Yun Zhu, Shu Yuan, Shangming Chen, Qing Wang, Wenqiao Zhang, Jun Xiao, Yueting Zhuang

entry.summary: MAIGO reduces lost-in-conversation degradation through on-policy self-distillation using history-cleaned references. Removes prior assistant replies in middle turns while preserving user-visible content to mitigate self-contamination.

entry.title: Separating Semantic Competition from Context Length in RAG Reading

author.name: Vyzantinos Repantis, Ameya Gawde, Harshvardhan Singh, Rohit Alekar, Cien Zhang, Svetlana Karslioglu, Akash Vishwakarma

entry.summary: Introduces a matched-control protocol for RAG reading that fixes context length while replacing hard competitors with less competitive real passages. Shows semantic competition rather than context length dominates reader failures.

entry.title: Real Images, Worse Judgments: Evaluating Vision-Language Models on Concreteness and Imagery

author.name: Yifan Jiang, Ruoxi Ning, Sheng Yao, Freda Shi

entry.summary: Examines whether VLMs distinguish useful visual evidence from incidental image context using human concreteness and imagery ratings. Finds real-image contexts hurt alignment with human ratings, sharpest when visual evidence is least relevant.

entry.title: Sentinel: Embodied Cooperative Spatial Reasoning and Planning

author.name: Xiangye Lin, Hongxin Zhang, Ruxi Deng, Qinhong Zhou, Chuang Gan

entry.summary: Sentinel introduces a benchmark and CoSaR framework for decentralized embodied agents that communicate in natural language to coordinate meeting points in city-scale outdoor environments while avoiding patrolling sentinels. Tests cooperative spatial reasoning capabilities of foundation models.

entry.title: RadarSim: Simulating Single-Chip Radar via Multimodal Neural Fields

author.name: Chuhan Chen, Tianshu Huang, Akarsh Prabhakara, Chaithanya Kumar Mummadi, Zhongxiao Cong, Anthony Rowe, Matthew O'Toole, Deva Ramanan

entry.summary: RadarSim is a unified differentiable renderer that uses multimodal neural fields to simulate single-chip radar data, overcoming radar's low spatial resolution by leveraging camera information. Includes authors from CMU including Deva Ramanan.

entry.title: LongCat-Video-Avatar 1.5 Technical Report

author.name: Meituan LongCat Team, Xunliang Cai, Meng Cheng, Feng Gao, Zhe Kong, Jiamu Li, Le Li, Weiheng Li, Hongyu Liu, Shuai Tan, Xiaoming Wei, Tianyu Yang, Yong Zhang

entry.summary: LongCat-Video-Avatar 1.5 is Meituan's open-source audio-driven video generation framework focused on production-ready stability with Whisper Large audio encoding and RLHF training. Achieves accurate lip-sync, identity consistency, and long-video generation.

entry.title: OmniRetriever: Any-to-Any Audio-Video-Text Retrieval via Fusion-as-Teacher Distillation

author.name: Yunze Liu, Chi-Hao Wu, Enmin Zhou, Junxiao Shen

entry.summary: OmniRetriever-7B uses fusion-as-teacher distillation to make the fused (T,V,A) embedding supervise single-modal embeddings during training, paired with Tuple-InfoNCE. Surpasses prior audio-video-text retrievers on six zero-shot benchmarks.

entry.title: REVERSE: Reinforcing Evidence Verification and Search for Agentic Image geo-localization

author.name: Yong Li, Furong Jia, Dacheng Yin, Kang Rong, Fengyun Rao, Jing Lyu, Fan Zhang

entry.summary: REVERSE is a reinforcement learning framework for agentic image geo-localization that supervises evidence search, query formulation, and result filtering jointly with prediction. Captures the iterative human-expert workflow of hypothesis-then-evidence reasoning.

entry.title: ChartAct: A Benchmark for Dynamic Chart Understanding

author.name: Muye Huang, Wu Lin, Lingling Zhang, Hang Yan, Zhiyuan Wang, Yumeng Fu, Zesheng Yang, Jun Liu

entry.summary: ChartAct is an interactive benchmark for dynamic chart understanding with 673 dynamic charts and 1440 QA pairs requiring hover, click, zoom, or drag interactions. Tests models' ability to choose proper actions and reason over changing chart states.

entry.title: Uncertainty-Aware Budget Allocation for Adaptive Test-Time Reasoning

author.name: Manh Nguyen, Sunil Gupta, Hung Le

entry.summary: Uncertainty-Aware Budget Allocation uses per-question average negative log-likelihood as a difficulty signal to reallocate sampling budget across questions. Solves a concave coverage-maximization problem via marginal-greedy assignment.

entry.title: Anchor: Mitigating Artifact Drift in Agent Benchmark Generation

author.name: Maksim Ivanov, Abhijay Rana

entry.summary: Anchor is a task generation pipeline that formalizes business workflow specifications as constraint optimization programs to jointly produce environments, oracles, and verifiers, addressing artifact drift in agent benchmark creation. Targets enterprise agent training and evaluation.

entry.title: From Static Context to Calibrated Interactive RL: Mitigating Distribution Shift in Multi-turn Dialogue with Aligned Simulator

author.name: Xiaohua Wang, Jiakang Yuan, Zisu Huang, Muzhao Tian, Changze Lv, Kaitao Song, Tao Chen, Xiaoqing Zheng

entry.summary: Theoretically shows that context distribution shift between training and real conversations compounds quadratically over dialogue turns, attributing the shift to both policy-induced and simulator sources. Proposes interactive RL approach to mitigate this.

entry.title: Which Changes Matter? Towards Trustworthy Legal AI via Relevance-Sensitive Evaluation and Solver-Grounded Reasoning

author.name: Chen Linze, Cai Yufan, Hou Zhe, Dong Jin Song

entry.summary: Proposes a legal-relevance-sensitive evaluation suite testing whether LLMs change outputs only when legally material facts change, finding existing legal LLMs are systematically sensitive to irrelevant variations. Introduces solver-grounded reasoning to mitigate failures.

entry.title: PolyFusionAgent: A Multimodal Foundation Model and Autonomous AI Assistant for Polymer Property Prediction and Inverse Design

author.name: Manpreet Kaur, Xingying Zhang, Qian Liu

entry.summary: PolyFusionAgent couples a multimodal polymer foundation model (PolyFusion) with a tool-augmented design agent for polymer property prediction and inverse design, aligning sequence, topology, 3D geometry, and fingerprints in a shared latent space.

entry.title: MedGuideX: Internalizing Decision Logic from Executable Guidelines into Large Language Models for Clinical Reasoning

author.name: Yuhao Shen, Lang Cao, Simo Du, Yuqing Wang, Juexiao Zhou, Hao Peng, Yue Guo

entry.summary: MedGuideX transforms clinical practice guidelines into executable decision logic and generates factual/counterfactual QA data to teach LLMs both guideline-supported decisions and how decisions change under different patient conditions.

entry.title: It's Not the Capability: Harness Sensitivity Is Non-Monotone Across LLM Agent Tiers

author.name: Yong-eun Cho

entry.summary: Tests the assumption that more structured agent harnesses universally improve reliability across 432 runs spanning four capability tiers, finding the relationship is non-monotone and refuting the inverse capability-harness hypothesis on the frontier Gemini 2.5 Flash model.

entry.title: Multi-Stakeholder LLM Alignment: Decomposing Estimation from Aggregation

author.name: Lulu Zheng, Wenjin Yang, Xiangwen Zhang, Rong Yin, Yulan Hu, Zheng Pan, Xin Li

entry.summary: Decomposes multi-stakeholder LLM alignment into separate utility estimation and aggregation steps, showing that holistic judges conflate them and create weight-induced score shifts that grow with stakeholder count. Proposes DecompR with counterfactual-calibrated weights.

entry.title: Generating Robust Portfolios of Optimization Models using Large Language Models

author.name: Eleni Straitouri, Cheol Woo Kim, Milind Tambe

entry.summary: Proposes generating diverse portfolios of optimization models from natural language using LLMs to mitigate the risk of unreliable single-model outputs. From Milind Tambe's group.

entry.title: Counteraction-Aware Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation for General Capability Recovery with Domain Preservation

author.name: Tianlei Chen, Jiao Ou, Ziyuan Liu, Ruiming Tang, Jian Liang, Han Li

entry.summary: Studies general capability recovery in domain-specialized LLMs using multi-teacher on-policy distillation with proxy general prompts when teacher prompt distributions are unknown. Identifies and addresses counteraction failure modes in vanilla MOPD.

entry.title: ICCU: In-Context Continual Unlearning via Pattern-Induced Refusal Rules

author.name: Ruihao Pan, Suhang Wang

entry.summary: ICCU performs continual unlearning by inducing readable refusal rules from unlearning datasets and applying them as filters or system prompts at inference time, avoiding parameter modifications and cross-request interference.

entry.title: StepOPSD: Step-Aware Online Preference Distillation for Agent Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Yanfei Zhang, Xu Lin, Chenglin Wu

entry.summary: StepOPSD performs step-aware online preference distillation for agent RL by decomposing trajectories into action-centered step segments and rescoring them with hindsight-enriched teacher contexts to provide denser credit assignment than trajectory-level rewards.

entry.title: Learning to Act under Noise: Enhancing Agent Robustness via Noisy Environments

author.name: Yuxin Chen, Xiaodong Cai, Junfeng Fang, Zhuowen Han, Yu Wang, Yaorui Shi, Yi Zhang, Qi Gu, Xunliang Cai, Xiang Wang, An Zhang, Tat-Seng Chua

entry.summary: NoisyAgent is an agentic training framework that explicitly incorporates environmental imperfections (stochasticity, noise) into training to improve real-world robustness, addressing the mismatch between curated training and noisy deployment.

entry.title: Xe-Forge: Multi-Stage LLM-Powered Kernel Optimization for Intel GPU

author.name: Marcin Spoczynski, Daniel Fleischer, Moshe Berchansky, Gabriela Ben-Melech Stan, Shira Guskin, Weilin Xu, Adam Siemieniuk, Alexander Heinecke

entry.summary: Xe-Forge is a multi-stage LLM-powered pipeline that automates up to nine optimization stages for Triton kernels on Intel GPUs, including quantization, memory coalescing, tile size tuning, and architecture-specific workarounds.

entry.title: GEM: Geometric Entropy Mixing for Optimal LLM Data Curation

author.name: Yue Min, Ziyun Qiao, Ruining Chen, Yujun Li

entry.summary: GEM reformulates LLM pretraining data curation as a variational optimization problem on the hypersphere with mixing-balance regularization, addressing cluster collapse in Euclidean clustering through provable MM algorithm and teacher-student distillation.

entry.title: Pretraining Data Exposure in Large Language Models: A Survey of Membership Inference, Data Contamination, and Security Implications

author.name: Ziyi Tong, Feifei Sun, Le Minh Nguyen

entry.summary: Survey unifying membership inference and data contamination research under a Pretraining Data Exposure framework, covering exposure levels, attack/defense methods, and empirical findings with security implications.

entry.title: VISTA: An End-to-End Benchmark for Visual Spec-to-Web-App Coding Agents

author.name: JunJia Guo (Joe), Yuhang Yao (Joe), Jiawei (Joe), Zhou, Jingdi Chen

entry.summary: VISTA is a benchmark for evaluating LLM agents on end-to-end web application generation from visual specifications, varying inputs across text, screenshots, Figma structures, and stack constraints. It targets realistic UI-centric development rather than algorithmic coding tasks.

entry.title: InfoQuant: Shaping Activation Distributions for Low-Bit LLM Quantization

author.name: Ke Li, Dong An, Xiaoling Zang, Can Ye, Liang Xie, Qibo Qiu, Chen Shen, Xiaofei He, Wenxiao Wang

entry.summary: InfoQuant recasts activation transformation in LLM quantization as quantizer-facing distribution design, focusing on what distributions are easy to discretize rather than just suppressing outliers. Targets low-bit post-training quantization.

entry.title: SetupX: Can LLM Agents Learn from Past Failures in Functionality-Correct Code Repository Setup?
